16.s:
atha putrakatvasiddhyai nirūpyate śivanirūpito 'tra vidhiḥ /
yadā tu samayasthasya putrakatve niyojanam /
gurutve sādhakatve vā kartumicchati daiśikaḥ // 1
16.d:
अथ पुत्रकत्वसिद्ध्यै निरूप्यते शिवनिरूपितो ऽत्र विधिः ।
यदा तु समयस्थस्य पुत्रकत्वे नियोजनम् ।
गुरुत्वे साधकत्वे वा कर्तुमिच्छति दैशिकः ॥ 1
16.m: Now the procedure taught by Śiva is explained for achieving status as a spiritual son: / when the master wishes to appoint one situated in the rule / to status as a spiritual son, or to masterhood or adeptship,

16.s:
tadādhivāsaṃ kṛtvāhni dvitīye maṇḍalaṃ likhet /
sāmudāyikayāge'tha tathānyatra yathoditam // 2
16.d:
तदाधिवासं कृत्वाह्नि द्वितीये मण्डलं लिखेत् ।
सामुदायिकयागेऽथ तथान्यत्र यथोदितम् ॥ 2
16.m: then, having performed the preliminary consecration, on the second day he should draw the mandala / for the collective sacrifice, as taught elsewhere.

16.s:
ṣaḍaṣṭataddviguṇitacaturviṃśatisaṃkhyayā /
cakrapañcakamākhyātaṃ śāstre śrīpūrvasaṃjñite // 3
16.d:
षडष्टतद्द्विगुणितचतुर्विंशतिसंख्यया ।
चक्रपञ्चकमाख्यातं शास्त्रे श्रीपूर्वसंज्ञिते ॥ 3
16.m: In the scripture named revered Pūrva, a group of five circles is declared / with the numbers six, eight, twice that (sixteen), and twenty-four.

16.s:
dvātriṃśattaddviguṇitaṃ śrīmattraiśirase mate /
asaṃkhyacakrasaṃbandhaḥ śrīsiddhādau nirūpitaḥ // 4
16.d:
द्वात्रिंशत्तद्द्विगुणितं श्रीमत्त्रैशिरसे मते ।
असंख्यचक्रसंबन्धः श्रीसिद्धादौ निरूपितः ॥ 4
16.m: In the doctrine of the revered Traiśirasa, [the number] is thirty-two and twice that (sixty-four). / An association of countless circles is taught in the revered Siddhā and other texts.

16.s:
tasmādyathātathā yāgaṃ yāvaccakreṇa saṃmitam /
pūjayedyena tenātra triśūlatrayamālikhet // 5
16.d:
तस्माद्यथातथा यागं यावच्चक्रेण संमितम् ।
पूजयेद्येन तेनात्र त्रिशूलत्रयमालिखेत् ॥ 5
16.m: Therefore, however [constituted], to the extent that the sacrifice corresponds to the circle, / he should worship; on whatever [base], here he should draw three tridents.

16.s:
triśūlatritaye devītrayaṃ paryāyavṛttitaḥ /
madhyasavyānyabhedena pūrṇaṃ saṃpūjitaṃ bhavet // 6
16.d:
त्रिशूलत्रितये देवीत्रयं पर्यायवृत्तितः ।
मध्यसव्यान्यभेदेन पूर्णं संपूजितं भवेत् ॥ 6
16.m: On the group of three tridents, the triad of goddesses will be fully worshipped / through alternating operation, / divided into center, right, and other [left].

16.s:
vartanā maṇḍalasyāgre saṃkṣepādupadekṣyate /
ālikhya maṇḍalaṃ gandhavastreṇaivāsya mārjanam // 7
16.d:
वर्तना मण्डलस्याग्रे संक्षेपादुपदेक्ष्यते ।
आलिख्य मण्डलं गन्धवस्त्रेणैवास्य मार्जनम् ॥ 7
16.m: The execution of the mandala will be taught briefly below. / Having drawn the mandala and wiped it with a perfumed cloth,

16.s:
kṛtvā snāto guruḥ prāgvanmaṇḍalāgre'tra devatāḥ /
bāhyagāḥ pūjayeddvāradeśe ca dvāradevatāḥ // 8
16.d:
कृत्वा स्नातो गुरुः प्राग्वन्मण्डलाग्रेऽत्र देवताः ।
बाह्यगाः पूजयेद्द्वारदेशे च द्वारदेवताः ॥ 8
16.m: the guru, bathed as before, should worship the external deities here / in front of the mandala, and the door deities at the location of the entrance.

16.s:
maṇḍalasya purobhāge tadaiśānadiśaḥ kramāt /
āgneyyantaṃ gaṇeśādīn kṣetrapāntānprapūjayet // 9
16.d:
मण्डलस्य पुरोभागे तदैशानदिशः क्रमात् ।
आग्नेय्यन्तं गणेशादीन् क्षेत्रपान्तान्प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 9
16.m:
In front of the maṇḍala, starting in succession from its northeastern direction
up to the southeast, one should worship [the deities] beginning with Gaṇeśa and ending with Kṣetrapāla.

16.s:
gaṇapatiguruparamākhyāḥ parameṣṭhī pūrvasiddhavākkṣetrapatiḥ /
iti saptakamākhyātaṃ gurupaṅktividhau prapūjyamasmadgurubhiḥ // 10
16.d:
गणपतिगुरुपरमाख्याः परमेष्ठी पूर्वसिद्धवाक्क्षेत्रपतिः ।
इति सप्तकमाख्यातं गुरुपङ्क्तिविधौ प्रपूज्यमस्मद्गुरुभिः ॥ 10
16.m:
Gaṇapati, Guru, Parama[-guru], Parameṣṭhin, Pūrvasiddha, Vāc, and Kṣetrapati:
this heptad to be worshipped in the rite of the line of gurus has been declared by our gurus.

16.s:
tata ājñāṃ gṛhītvā tu puṣpadhūpādipūjitam /
pūjyamādhāraśaktyādi śūlamūlātprabhṛtyalam // 11
16.d:
तत आज्ञां गृहीत्वा तु पुष्पधूपादिपूजितम् ।
पूज्यमाधारशक्त्यादि शूलमूलात्प्रभृत्यलम् ॥ 11
16.m:
Then, having received permission, [having] worshipped with flowers, incense, and so forth,
one should fully worship [the deities] beginning with the foundational power (ādhāraśakti) up from the base of the trident,

16.s:
śivāntaṃ sitapadmānte triśūlānāṃ traye kramāt /
madhyaśūle madhyagaḥ syātsadbhāvaḥ parayā saha // 12
16.d:
शिवान्तं सितपद्मान्ते त्रिशूलानां त्रये क्रमात् ।
मध्यशूले मध्यगः स्यात्सद्भावः परया सह ॥ 12
16.m:
ending with Śiva at the end of the white lotus, in succession upon the three tridents:
upon the central trident, Sadbhāva along with Parā should occupy the central [prong];

16.s:
vāme cāparayā sākaṃ navātmā dakṣagaṃ param /
triśūle dakṣiṇe madhyaśṛṅgastho ratiśekharaḥ // 13
16.d:
वामे चापरया साकं नवात्मा दक्षगं परम् ।
त्रिशूले दक्षिणे मध्यशृङ्गस्थो रतिशेखरः ॥ 13
16.m:
on the left [prong] Navātman along with Aparā, [and] on the right [prong] Param [worshipped].
Upon the right trident, Ratiśekhara situated on the central prong

16.s:
syātparāparayā sākaṃ dakṣe bhairavasatpare /
vāme triśūle madhyastho navātmāparayā saha // 14
16.d:
स्यात्परापरया साकं दक्षे भैरवसत्परे ।
वामे त्रिशूले मध्यस्थो नवात्मापरया सह ॥ 14
16.m:
should be [worshipped] along with Parāparā; Bhairava on the right, and Satpara [on the left].
Upon the left trident, Navātman situated in the center along with Aparā;

16.s:
syātpare parayā sākaṃ vāmāre saṃśca bhairavaḥ /
itthaṃ sarvagatatve śrīparādevyāḥ sthite sati // 15
16.d:
स्यात्परे परया साकं वामारे संश्च भैरवः ।
इत्थं सर्वगतत्वे श्रीपरादेव्याः स्थिते सति ॥ 15
16.m:
on the right along with Parā, and Bhairava situated on the left prong.
Thus, since the glorious goddess Parā is all-pervading,

16.s:
yāgo bhavetsusaṃpūrṇastadadhiṣṭhānamātrataḥ /
ekaśūle'pyato yāge cintayettadadhiṣṭhitam // 16
16.d:
यागो भवेत्सुसंपूर्णस्तदधिष्ठानमात्रतः ।
एकशूलेऽप्यतो यागे चिन्तयेत्तदधिष्ठितम् ॥ 16
16.m:
the sacrifice becomes completely fulfilled merely through her presiding influence.
Therefore, even in a sacrifice upon a single trident, one should contemplate it as presided over by her.

16.s:
avidhijño vidhānajña ityevaṃ trīśikoditam /
tato madhye tathā dakṣe vāme śṛṅge ca sarvataḥ // 17
16.d:
अविधिज्ञो विधानज्ञ इत्येवं त्रीशिकोदितम् ।
ततो मध्ये तथा दक्षे वामे शृङ्गे च सर्वतः ॥ 17
16.m:
‘One who knows the rule, one who knows the injunction,’ thus it is stated in the Triśikā.
Then in the center, and likewise on the right and left prong everywhere,

16.s:
lokapālāstraparyantamekātmatvena pūjayet /
paratvena ca sarvāsāṃ devatānāṃ prapūjayet // 18
16.d:
लोकपालास्त्रपर्यन्तमेकात्मत्वेन पूजयेत् ।
परत्वेन च सर्वासां देवतानां प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 18
16.m:
one should worship as a single self up to the guardians of the world (lokapāla) and their weapons;
and as supreme among all deities one should worship

16.s:
śrīmantaṃ mātṛsadbhāvabhaṭṭārakamanāmayam /
tato'pi bhogayāgena vidyāṅgaṃ bhairavāṣṭakam // 19
16.d:
श्रीमन्तं मातृसद्भावभट्टारकमनामयम् ।
ततोऽपि भोगयागेन विद्याङ्गं भैरवाष्टकम् ॥ 19
16.m:
the glorious Lord Mātṛsadbhāva, free from affliction.
Then, moreover, by a sacrifice of enjoyment, [one should worship] the limbs of the vidyā, the eight Bhairavas,

16.s:
yāmalaṃ cakradevīśca svasthāne pūjayedbahiḥ /
lokapālānastrayutāngandhapuṣpāsavādibhiḥ // 20
16.d:
यामलं चक्रदेवीश्च स्वस्थाने पूजयेद्बहिः ।
लोकपालानस्त्रयुतान्गन्धपुष्पासवादिभिः ॥ 20
16.m:
the dyad, and the goddesses of the cakra in their own place; externally,
one should worship the guardians of the world together with their weapons, with perfumes, flowers, liquor, and so forth,

16.s:
pūjayetparayā bhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ /
tataḥ kumbhāstrakalaśīmaṇḍalasthānalātmanām // 21
16.d:
पूजयेत्परया भक्त्या वित्तशाठ्यविवर्जितः ।
ततः कुम्भास्त्रकलशीमण्डलस्थानलात्मनाम् ॥ 21
16.m:
with supreme devotion, devoid of stinginess with wealth.
Then one should effect the integration of the five—

16.s:
pañcānāmanusandhānaṃ kuryādadvayabhāvanāt /
ye tu tāmadvayavyāptiṃ na vindanti śivātmikām // 22
16.d:
पञ्चानामनुसन्धानं कुर्यादद्वयभावनात् ।
ये तु तामद्वयव्याप्तिं न विन्दन्ति शिवात्मिकाम् ॥ 22
16.m:
the pot, the weapon-jar, the maṇḍala, the fire pit, and oneself—through the contemplation of non-duality.
Those, however, who do not attain that non-dual pervasion whose essence is Śiva,

16.s:
mantranāḍīprayogeṇa te viśantyadvaye pathi /
svadakṣiṇena niḥsṛtya maṇḍalasthasya vāmataḥ // 23
16.d:
मन्त्रनाडीप्रयोगेण ते विशन्त्यद्वये पथि ।
स्वदक्षिणेन निःसृत्य मण्डलस्थस्य वामतः ॥ 23
16.m:
enter the non-dual path by the deployment of mantra and subtle channels (nāḍī):
emerging through one's own right [nostril], entering through the left of the one in the maṇḍala,

16.s:
praviśyānyena niḥsṛtya kumbhasthe karkarīgate /
vahnisthe ca krameṇetthaṃ yāvatsvasminsvavāmataḥ // 24
16.d:
प्रविश्यान्येन निःसृत्य कुम्भस्थे कर्करीगते ।
वह्निस्थे च क्रमेणेत्थं यावत्स्वस्मिन्स्ववामतः ॥ 24
16.m:
emerging through the other, entering the one in the pot, the one in the jug (karkarī),
and the one in the fire, in this order, until [it enters] into oneself through one's own left [nostril].

16.s:
mūlānusandhānabalātprāṇatantūmbhane sati /
itthamaikyasphurattātmā vyāptisaṃvitprakāśate // 25
16.d:
मूलानुसन्धानबलात्प्राणतन्तूम्भने सति ।
इत्थमैक्यस्फुरत्तात्मा व्याप्तिसंवित्प्रकाशते ॥ 25
16.m:
When the thread of vital breath is woven through the power of contemplation of the root [mantra],
thus does the consciousness of pervasion, whose essence is the vibrant radiance of unity, shine forth.

16.s:
tato viśeṣapūjāṃ ca kuryādadvayabhāvitām /
yacchivādvayapīyūṣasaṃsiktaṃ paramaṃ hi tat // 26
16.d:
ततो विशेषपूजां च कुर्यादद्वयभाविताम् ।
यच्छिवाद्वयपीयूषसंसिक्तं परमं हि तत् ॥ 26
16.m:
Then one should perform the special worship, cultivated through non-duality;
for that which is sprinkled with the nectar of Śiva's non-duality is indeed supreme.

16.s:
tenārghapuṣpagandhāderāsavasya paśoratha /
yā śivādvayatādṛṣṭiḥ sā śuddhiḥ paramīkṛtiḥ // 27
16.d:
तेनार्घपुष्पगन्धादेरासवस्य पशोरथ ।
या शिवाद्वयतादृष्टिः सा शुद्धिः परमीकृतिः ॥ 27
16.m:
Therefore, regarding the oblation-water (argha), flowers, perfume, and so forth, the liquor, and the animal victim (paśu):
that vision of them as non-dual with Śiva is their purification, their transformation into the supreme.

16.s:
nivedayedvibhoragre jīvāndhātūṃstadutthitān /
siddhānasiddhānvyāmiśrānyadvā kiṃciccarācaram // 28
16.d:
निवेदयेद्विभोरग्रे जीवान्धातूंस्तदुत्थितान् ।
सिद्धानसिद्धान्व्यामिश्रान्यद्वा किंचिच्चराचरम् ॥ 28
16.m:
Before the omnipresent Lord one should offer living beings, the bodily elements arisen from them,
prepared, raw, mixed, or whatever is mobile and immobile.

16.s:
dṛṣṭaprokṣitasaṃdraṣṭṛprālabdhopāttayojitaḥ /
nirvāpito vīrapaśuḥ so'ṣṭadhottaratottamaḥ // 29
16.d:
दृष्टप्रोक्षितसंद्रष्टृप्रालब्धोपात्तयोजितः ।
निर्वापितो वीरपशुः सोऽष्टधोत्तरतोत्तमः ॥ 29
16.m:
Seen, sprinkled, fully viewed, undertaken, seized, integrated,
and extinguished: the heroic animal victim (vīrapaśu) is eightfold, each higher than the previous.

16.s:
yathottaraṃ na dātavyamayogyebhyaḥ kadācana /
śivopayuktaṃ hi havirna sarvo bhoktumarhati // 30
16.d:
यथोत्तरं न दातव्यमयोग्येभ्यः कदाचन ।
शिवोपयुक्तं हि हविर्न सर्वो भोक्तुमर्हति ॥ 30
16.m:
The progressively higher should never be given to unworthy persons;
for not everyone is entitled to enjoy an oblation utilized for Śiva.

16.s:
yastu dīkṣāvihīno'pi śivecchāvidhicoditaḥ /
bhaktyāśnāti sa saṃpūrṇaḥ samayī syātsubhāvitaḥ // 31
16.d:
यस्तु दीक्षाविहीनोऽपि शिवेच्छाविधिचोदितः ।
भक्त्याश्नाति स संपूर्णः समयी स्यात्सुभावितः ॥ 31
16.m:
Yet whoever, even if uninitiated, eats with devotion
impelled by the ordinance of Śiva's will, becomes a complete initiate into the rule, well cultivated.

16.s:
dṛṣṭo'valokitaścaiva kiraṇeddhadṛgarpaṇāt /
prokṣitaḥ kevalaṃ hyarghapātravipruḍbhirukṣitaḥ // 32
16.d:
दृष्टोऽवलोकितश्चैव किरणेद्धदृगर्पणात् ।
प्रोक्षितः केवलं ह्यर्घपात्रविप्रुड्भिरुक्षितः ॥ 32
16.m:
‘Seen’ is observed by casting a glance blazing with rays;
‘sprinkled’ is merely moistened with drops from the oblation vessel;

16.s:
saṃdraṣṭā darśitāśeṣasamyakpūjitamaṇḍalaḥ /
prālabdha uktatritayasaṃskṛtaḥ so'pi dhūnayet // 33
16.d:
संद्रष्टा दर्शिताशेषसम्यक्पूजितमण्डलः ।
प्रालब्ध उक्तत्रितयसंस्कृतः सोऽपि धूनयेत् ॥ 33
16.m:
‘fully viewed’ is one shown the entirely and properly worshipped maṇḍala;
‘undertaken’ is consecrated by the stated triad—he too may shake,

16.s:
kampeta prasravetstabdhaḥ pralīno vā yathottaram /
upātto yāgasānnidhye śamitaḥ śastramārutaiḥ // 34
16.d:
कम्पेत प्रस्रवेत्स्तब्धः प्रलीनो वा यथोत्तरम् ।
उपात्तो यागसान्निध्ये शमितः शस्त्रमारुतैः ॥ 34
16.m:
tremble, sweat, become rigid, or dissolve, progressively;
‘seized’ is brought near the sacrifice and calmed by the winds of the weapon [mantras];

16.s:
yojitaḥ kāraṇatyāgakrameṇa śivayojanāt /
nirvāpitaḥ kṛtābhyāsaguruprāṇamanorpaṇāt // 35
16.d:
योजितः कारणत्यागक्रमेण शिवयोजनात् ।
निर्वापितः कृताभ्यासगुरुप्राणमनोर्पणात् ॥ 35
16.m:
‘integrated’ is through joining with Śiva by the method of abandoning the instruments (kāraṇa);
‘extinguished’ is by the offering of the mind and breath of the guru who has mastered the practice,

16.s:
dakṣiṇenāgninā saumyakalājālavilāpanāt /
tathāhyādau paraṃ rūpamekībhāvena saṃśrayet // 36
16.d:
दक्षिणेनाग्निना सौम्यकलाजालविलापनात् ।
तथाह्यादौ परं रूपमेकीभावेन संश्रयेत् ॥ 36
16.m:
through dissolving the array of lunar parts (kalā) by the solar fire on the right.
Thus, first, one should resort in unity to the supreme form:

16.s:
tasmādāgneyacāreṇa jvālāmālāmucāviśet /
paśorvāmena candrāṃśujālaṃ tāpena gālayet // 37
16.d:
तस्मादाग्नेयचारेण ज्वालामालामुचाविशेत् ।
पशोर्वामेन चन्द्रांशुजालं तापेन गालयेत् ॥ 37
16.m:
from that, by the solar passage emitting a garland of flames, one should enter;
through the animal's left, one should melt the mass of lunar rays with heat.

16.s:
nābhicakre'tha viśrāmyetprāṇaraśmigaṇaiḥ saha /
paro bhūtvā svaśaktyātra jīvaṃ jīvena veṣṭayet // 38
16.d:
नाभिचक्रेऽथ विश्राम्येत्प्राणरश्मिगणैः सह ।
परो भूत्वा स्वशक्त्यात्र जीवं जीवेन वेष्टयेत् ॥ 38
16.m:
Then one should rest in the navel wheel together with the rays of vital breath;
having become supreme by one's own power, one should envelop the individual soul with one's soul here.

16.s:
svacitsūryeṇa saṃtāpya drāvayet kalāṃ kalām /
tato drutaṃ kalājālaṃ prāpayyaikatvamātmani // 39
16.d:
स्वचित्सूर्येण संताप्य द्रावयेत् कलां कलाम् ।
ततो द्रुतं कलाजालं प्रापय्यैकत्वमात्मनि ॥ 39
16.m:
Heating with the sun of one's own consciousness, one should liquefy part by part;
then, having brought the liquefied collection of parts to oneness within oneself,

16.s:
samastatattvasaṃpūrṇamāpyāyanavidhāyinam /
unmūlayeta saṃrambhātkarmabaddhamamuṃ rasāt // 40
16.d:
समस्ततत्त्वसंपूर्णमाप्यायनविधायिनम् ।
उन्मूलयेत संरम्भात्कर्मबद्धममुं रसात् ॥ 40
16.m:
which is filled with all cosmic principles and effects nourishing replenishment,
one should passionately uproot from its essence this [soul] bound by karma.

16.s:
tata unmūlanodveṣṭayogādvāmaṃ paribhraman /
kuṇḍalyamṛtasaṃpūrṇasvakaprāṇaprasevakaḥ // 41
16.d:
तत उन्मूलनोद्वेष्टयोगाद्वामं परिभ्रमन् ।
कुण्डल्यमृतसंपूर्णस्वकप्राणप्रसेवकः ॥ 41
16.m:
Then, from the union of uprooting and unwinding, circulating to the left,
one who pours forth one's own vital breath filled with the nectar of the kuṇḍalinī,

16.s:
vāmāvartakramopāttahṛtpadmāmṛtakesaraḥ /
hṛtkarṇikārūḍhilābhādojodhātuṃ vilāpitam // 42
16.d:
वामावर्तक्रमोपात्तहृत्पद्मामृतकेसरः ।
हृत्कर्णिकारूढिलाभादोजोधातुं विलापितम् ॥ 42
16.m:
having gathered the filaments of nectar of the heart lotus by a counter-clockwise movement,
from gaining a footing in the pericarp of the heart, [one takes] the dissolved bodily element of vitality (ojas),

16.s:
śuddhasomātmakaṃ sāramīṣallohitapītalam /
ādāya karihastāgrasadṛśe prāṇavigrahe // 43
16.d:
शुद्धसोमात्मकं सारमीषल्लोहितपीतलम् ।
आदाय करिहस्ताग्रसदृशे प्राणविग्रहे ॥ 43
16.m:
which is pure lunar essence, slightly reddish-yellow;
having taken it into the body of vital breath resembling the tip of an elephant's trunk,

16.s:
niḥsṛtya jhaṭiti svātmavāmamārgeṇa saṃviśet /
āpyāyayannapānākhyacandracakrahṛdambuje // 44
16.d:
निःसृत्य झटिति स्वात्मवाममार्गेण संविशेत् ।
आप्याययन्नपानाख्यचन्द्रचक्रहृदम्बुजे ॥ 44
16.m:
emerging, one should swiftly enter through one's own left path,
nourishing [it] in the heart lotus of the lunar wheel known as the descending breath (apāna);

16.s:
sthitaṃ taddevatācakraṃ tena sāreṇa tarpayet /
anena vidhinā sarvānrasaraktādikāṃstathā // 45
16.d:
स्थितं तद्देवताचक्रं तेन सारेण तर्पयेत् ।
अनेन विधिना सर्वान्रसरक्तादिकांस्तथा ॥ 45
16.m:
one should satisfy with that essence the circle of deities stationed therein.
By this method, one should extract all bodily elements,
such as chyle (rasa), blood, and so forth, either collectively or one by one.

16.s:
dhātūnsamāharetsaṃghakramādekaikaśo'thavā /
kevalaṃ tvathavāgnīnduravisaṃghaṭṭamadhyagam // 46
16.d:
धातून्समाहरेत्संघक्रमादेकैकशोऽथवा ।
केवलं त्वथवाग्नीन्दुरविसंघट्टमध्यगम् ॥ 46
16.m:
Alternatively, one may simply extract the living soul known as the power of breath,
which is of the nature of light, located in the middle of the union of fire, moon, and sun.

16.s:
jyotīrūpamatha prāṇaśaktyākhyaṃ jīvamāharet /
jīvaṃ samarasīkuryāddevīcakreṇa bhāvanāt // 47
16.d:
ज्योतीरूपमथ प्राणशक्त्याख्यं जीवमाहरेत् ।
जीवं समरसीकुर्याद्देवीचक्रेण भावनात् ॥ 47
16.m: One should harmonize the living soul into one savor with the circle of goddesses through contemplation;

16.s:
tadeva tarpaṇaṃ mukhyaṃ bhogyabhoktrātmataiva sā /
agnisaṃpuṭaphullārṇatryaśrakālātmako mahān // 48
16.d:
तदेव तर्पणं मुख्यं भोग्यभोक्त्रात्मतैव सा ।
अग्निसंपुटफुल्लार्णत्र्यश्रकालात्मको महान् ॥ 48
16.m:
that alone is the supreme satisfaction (tarpaṇa), that is indeed the identity of the enjoyed and the enjoyer.
The great mass, consisting of the time of the triangle whose syllables are opened by enclosing with fire,

16.s:
piṇḍo raktādisāraughacālanākarṣaṇādiṣu /
itthaṃ viśrāntiyogena ghaṭikārdhakrame sati // 49
16.d:
पिण्डो रक्तादिसारौघचालनाकर्षणादिषु ।
इत्थं विश्रान्तियोगेन घटिकार्धक्रमे सति ॥ 49
16.m:
is used in moving, drawing in, and so forth the flood of essence such as blood.
Thus, through the practice of repose, over the course of half a ghaṭikā,

16.s:
āvṛttiśatayogena paśornirvāpaṇaṃ bhavet /
kṛtvā katipayaṃ kālaṃ tatrābhyāsamananyadhīḥ // 50
16.d:
आवृत्तिशतयोगेन पशोर्निर्वापणं भवेत् ।
कृत्वा कतिपयं कालं तत्राभ्यासमनन्यधीः ॥ 50
16.m:
by the application of a hundred repetitions, the extinction of the animal victim takes place.
Having practiced there for some time with undivided mind,

16.s:
yathā cintāmaṇau proktaṃ tena rūpeṇa yogavit /
niḥśaṅkaḥ siddhimāpnoti gopyaṃ tatprāṇavatsphuṭam // 51
16.d:
यथा चिन्तामणौ प्रोक्तं तेन रूपेण योगवित् ।
निःशङ्कः सिद्धिमाप्नोति गोप्यं तत्प्राणवत्स्फुटम् ॥ 51
16.m:
in the manner declared in the Cintāmaṇi, the knower of yoga,
free of doubt, attains spiritual accomplishment; that secret must clearly be guarded like one's life.

16.s:
parokṣe'pi paśāvevaṃ vidhiḥ syādyojanaṃ prati /
praveśito yāgabhuvi hatastatraiva sādhitaḥ // 52
16.d:
परोक्षेऽपि पशावेवं विधिः स्याद्योजनं प्रति ।
प्रवेशितो यागभुवि हतस्तत्रैव साधितः ॥ 52
16.m:
Even when the animal victim is out of sight, this rule applies regarding integration.
Brought onto the sacrificial ground, slain right there, ritually accomplished,

16.s:
cakrajuṣṭaśca tatraiva sa vīrapaśurucyate /
yastvanyatrāpi nihataḥ sāmastyenāṃśato'pivā // 53
16.d:
चक्रजुष्टश्च तत्रैव स वीरपशुरुच्यते ।
यस्त्वन्यत्रापि निहतः सामस्त्येनांशतोऽपिवा ॥ 53
16.m:
and enjoyed by the cakra right there—that is called a heroic animal victim (vīrapaśu).
That which is slain elsewhere, whether entirely or in part,

16.s:
devāya vinivedyeta sa vai bāhyapaśurmataḥ /
rājyaṃ lābho'tha tatsthairyaṃ śive bhaktistadātmatā // 54
16.d:
देवाय विनिवेद्येत स वै बाह्यपशुर्मतः ।
राज्यं लाभोऽथ तत्स्थैर्यं शिवे भक्तिस्तदात्मता ॥ 54
16.m:
and offered to the deity, is considered indeed an external animal victim (bāhyapaśu).
Sovereignty, acquisition, then stability thereof, devotion to Śiva, oneness with him,

16.s:
śivajñānaṃ mantralokaprāptistatparivāratā /
tatsāyujyaṃ paśoḥ sāmyādbāhyādervīradharmaṇaḥ // 55
16.d:
शिवज्ञानं मन्त्रलोकप्राप्तिस्तत्परिवारता ।
तत्सायुज्यं पशोः साम्याद्बाह्यादेर्वीरधर्मणः ॥ 55
16.m:
knowledge of Śiva, attainment of the realm of mantras, belonging to his retinue,
[and] assimilation with him: [these are attained] by virtue of the animal victim's equality, from external to heroic nature.

16.s:
puṣpādayo'pi tallābhabhāginaḥ śivapūjayā /
ekopāyena deveśo viśvānugrahaṇātmakaḥ // 56
16.d:
पुष्पादयोऽपि तल्लाभभागिनः शिवपूजया ।
एकोपायेन देवेशो विश्वानुग्रहणात्मकः ॥ 56
16.m: Flowers and the like also share in attaining that through the worship of Śiva; / by a single means, the Lord of Gods is of the nature of universal grace.

16.s:
yāgenaivānugṛhṇāti kiṃ kiṃ yanna carācaram /
tenāvīro'pi śaṅkādiyuktaḥ kāruṇiko'pica // 57
16.d:
यागेनैवानुगृह्णाति किं किं यन्न चराचरम् ।
तेनावीरोऽपि शङ्कादियुक्तः कारुणिकोऽपिच ॥ 57
16.m: Through sacrifice alone does He grace whatever is moving and unmoving; / therefore even one who is not a hero, beset with doubt and the like, or compassionate,

16.s:
na hiṃsābuddhimādadhyātpaśukarmaṇi jātucit /
paśormahopakāro'yaṃ tadātve'pyapriyaṃ bhavet // 58
16.d:
न हिंसाबुद्धिमादध्यात्पशुकर्मणि जातुचित् ।
पशोर्महोपकारोऽयं तदात्वेऽप्यप्रियं भवेत् ॥ 58
16.m: should never conceive an intention of violence regarding the ritual of the sacrificial animal. / This is a great favor to the animal, even though it may be unpleasant at the moment.

16.s:
vyādhicchedauṣadhatapoyojanātra nidarśanam /
śrīmanmṛtyuñjaye proktaṃ pāśacchede kṛte paśoḥ // 59
16.d:
व्याधिच्छेदौषधतपोयोजनात्र निदर्शनम् ।
श्रीमन्मृत्युञ्जये प्रोक्तं पाशच्छेदे कृते पशोः ॥ 59
16.m: The illustration here is the application of surgery, medicine, and austerities for disease. / In the venerable Mṛtyuñjaya it is stated: when the fetter of the animal is cut,

16.s:
malatrayaviyogena śarīraṃ na prarohati /
dharmādharmaughavicchedāccharīraṃ cyacate kila // 60
16.d:
मलत्रयवियोगेन शरीरं न प्ररोहति ।
धर्माधर्मौघविच्छेदाच्छरीरं च्यचते किल ॥ 60
16.m: by separation from the three impurities, the body does not sprout anew. / Through the severance of the flood of merit and demerit, the body indeed falls away.

16.s:
tenaitanmāraṇaṃ noktaṃ dīkṣeyaṃ citrarūpiṇī /
rūḍhapāśasya yaḥ prāṇairviyogo māraṇaṃ hi tat // 61
16.d:
तेनैतन्मारणं नोक्तं दीक्षेयं चित्ररूपिणी ।
रूढपाशस्य यः प्राणैर्वियोगो मारणं हि तत् ॥ 61
16.m: Therefore this is not called killing; this is initiation of a manifold nature. / Indeed, killing is that separation from the vital breaths of one whose fetters remain intact.

16.s:
iyaṃ tu yojanaiva syātpaśordevāya tarpaṇe /
tasmāddevoktimāśritya paśūndadyādbahūniti // 62
16.d:
इयं तु योजनैव स्यात्पशोर्देवाय तर्पणे ।
तस्माद्देवोक्तिमाश्रित्य पशून्दद्याद्बहूनिति ॥ 62
16.m: This, however, is precisely joining the animal to God in satisfaction. / Therefore, relying on the word of God, one should offer many animals.

16.s:
niveditaḥ punaḥprāptadeho bhūyoniveditaḥ /
ṣaṭkṛtva itthaṃ yaḥ so'tra ṣaḍjanmā paśuruttamaḥ // 63
16.d:
निवेदितः पुनःप्राप्तदेहो भूयोनिवेदितः ।
षट्कृत्व इत्थं यः सोऽत्र षड्जन्मा पशुरुत्तमः ॥ 63
16.m: Offered, obtaining a body again, offered once more— / one who does so six times is here the highest animal of six births.

16.s:
yathā pākakramācchuddhaṃ hema tadvatsa kīrtitaḥ /
kāṃ siddhiṃ naiva vitaretsvayaṃ kiṃvā na mucyate // 64
16.d:
यथा पाकक्रमाच्छुद्धं हेम तद्वत्स कीर्तितः ।
कां सिद्धिं नैव वितरेत्स्वयं किंवा न मुच्यते ॥ 64
16.m: Just as gold is purified through the process of heating, so is that [animal] praised. / What accomplishment would it not bestow, or is it not itself liberated?

16.s:
uktaṃ tvānandaśāstre yo mantrasaṃskāravāṃstyajet /
samayānkutsayeddevīrdadyānmantrānvinā nayāt // 65
16.d:
उक्तं त्वानन्दशास्त्रे यो मन्त्रसंस्कारवांस्त्यजेत् ।
समयान्कुत्सयेद्देवीर्दद्यान्मन्त्रान्विना नयात् ॥ 65
16.m: However, it is said in the Ānandaśāstra: whoever, having the purificatory consecrations of mantras, abandons them, / reviles the rules, insults the goddesses, gives mantras without proper transmission,

16.s:
dīkṣāmantrādikaṃ prāpya tyajetputrādimohitaḥ /
tato manuṣyatāmetya punarevaṃ karotyapi // 66
16.d:
दीक्षामन्त्रादिकं प्राप्य त्यजेत्पुत्रादिमोहितः ।
ततो मनुष्यतामेत्य पुनरेवं करोत्यपि ॥ 66
16.m: having received initiation, mantras, and the like, abandons them, deluded by children and the like— / then, attaining human birth, does the same again,

16.s:
itthamekādisaptāntajanmāsau dvividho dvipāt /
catuṣpādvā paśurdevīcarukārthaṃ prajāyate // 67
16.d:
इत्थमेकादिसप्तान्तजन्मासौ द्विविधो द्विपात् ।
चतुष्पाद्वा पशुर्देवीचरुकार्थं प्रजायते ॥ 67
16.m: in this way, having from one up to seven births, this twofold animal, two-legged / or four-legged, is born for the sake of the sacrificial offering to the goddess.

16.s:
dātrarpito'sau taddvārā yāti sāyujyataḥ śivam /
iti saṃbhāvya citraṃ tatpaśūnāṃ praviceṣṭitam // 68
16.d:
दात्रर्पितोऽसौ तद्द्वारा याति सायुज्यतः शिवम् ।
इति संभाव्य चित्रं तत्पशूनां प्रविचेष्टितम् ॥ 68
16.m: Offered by the donor, through that means it attains Śiva through union. / Reflecting thus upon that wondrous behavior of bound souls,

16.s:
bhogyīcikīrṣitaṃ naiva kuryādanyatra taṃ paśum /
nāpi naiṣa bhavedyogya iti buddhvāpasārayet // 69
16.d:
भोग्यीचिकीर्षितं नैव कुर्यादन्यत्र तं पशुम् ।
नापि नैष भवेद्योग्य इति बुद्ध्वापसारयेत् ॥ 69
16.m: one must never assign to another purpose that animal intended for consumption [by the deity], / nor dismiss it thinking, 'this one is not fit.'

16.s:
taṃ paśuṃ kiṃtu kāṅkṣā cedviśeṣe taṃ tu ḍhaukayet /
tāvatastānpaśūndadyāttathācoktaṃ maheśinā // 70
16.d:
तं पशुं किंतु काङ्क्षा चेद्विशेषे तं तु ढौकयेत् ।
तावतस्तान्पशून्दद्यात्तथाचोक्तं महेशिना ॥ 70
16.m: However, if there is a desire for a distinction concerning that animal, one should offer it; / one should offer as many of those animals [as required], and so it has been spoken by the Great Lord.

16.s:
paśorvapāmedasī ca gālite vahnimadhyataḥ /
arpayecchakticakrāya paramaṃ tarpaṇaṃ matam // 71
16.d:
पशोर्वपामेदसी च गालिते वह्निमध्यतः ।
अर्पयेच्छक्तिचक्राय परमं तर्पणं मतम् ॥ 71
16.m: The caul and the fat of the animal, rendered in the midst of fire, / one should offer to the wheel of powers; it is regarded as the supreme satisfaction.

16.s:
hṛdantramuṇḍāṃsayakṛtpradhānaṃ vinivedayet /
karṇikākuṇḍalīmajjaparśu mukhyataraṃ ca vā // 72
16.d:
हृदन्त्रमुण्डांसयकृत्प्रधानं विनिवेदयेत् ।
कर्णिकाकुण्डलीमज्जपर्शु मुख्यतरं च वा ॥ 72
16.m: One should offer the heart, entrails, head, shoulder, and liver as the primary parts, / or more prominently the pericarp, spiral canal, marrow, and ribs.

16.s:
tato'gnau tarpaṇaṃ kuryānmantracakrasya daiśikaḥ /
tannivedya ca devāya tato vijñāpayetprabhum // 73
16.d:
ततोऽग्नौ तर्पणं कुर्यान्मन्त्रचक्रस्य दैशिकः ।
तन्निवेद्य च देवाय ततो विज्ञापयेत्प्रभुम् ॥ 73
16.m: Then the guru should perform satisfaction to the wheel of mantras in the fire. / Having offered that to the deity, he should then address the Lord:

16.s:
gurutvena tvayaivāhamājñātaḥ parameśvara /
sākṣātsvapnopadeśādyairjapairgurumukhena vā // 74
16.d:
गुरुत्वेन त्वयैवाहमाज्ञातः परमेश्वर ।
साक्षात्स्वप्नोपदेशाद्यैर्जपैर्गुरुमुखेन वा ॥ 74
16.m: 'O Supreme Lord, by You alone have I been commanded to the state of guru, / directly, through dream instruction and the like, through recitations, or through the mouth of the guru:

16.s:
anugrāhyāstvayā śiṣyāḥ śivaśaktipracoditāḥ /
tadete tadvidhāḥ prāptāstvamebhyaḥ kurvanugraham // 75
16.d:
अनुग्राह्यास्त्वया शिष्याः शिवशक्तिप्रचोदिताः ।
तदेते तद्विधाः प्राप्तास्त्वमेभ्यः कुर्वनुग्रहम् ॥ 75
16.m: "Disciples impelled by the power of Śiva are to be graced by you." / Therefore, these [disciples] of such nature have arrived; bestow grace upon them!

16.s:
samāveśaya māṃ svātmaraśmibhiryadahaṃ śivaḥ /
evaṃ bhavatviti tataḥ śivoktimabhinandayet // 76
16.d:
समावेशय मां स्वात्मरश्मिभिर्यदहं शिवः ।
एवं भवत्विति ततः शिवोक्तिमभिनन्दयेत् ॥ 76
16.m: Pervade me with Your own rays of consciousness, so that I am Śiva!' / Then he should welcome the word of Śiva: 'So be it!'

16.s:
śivābhinnamathātmānaṃ pañcakṛtyakaraṃ smaret /
svātmanaḥ karaṇaṃ mantrānmūrtiṃ cānujighṛkṣayā // 77
16.d:
शिवाभिन्नमथात्मानं पञ्चकृत्यकरं स्मरेत् ।
स्वात्मनः करणं मन्त्रान्मूर्तिं चानुजिघृक्षया ॥ 77
16.m: Then, with the desire to bestow grace, he should contemplate himself as non-different from Śiva, the performer of the five cosmic acts, / the mantras as his own instruments, and the ritual image [as his own body].

16.s:
tato baddhvā sitoṣṇīṣaṃ hastayorarcayetkramāt /
anyonyaṃ pāśadāhāya śuddhatattvavisṛṣṭaye // 78
16.d:
ततो बद्ध्वा सितोष्णीषं हस्तयोरर्चयेत्क्रमात् ।
अन्योन्यं पाशदाहाय शुद्धतत्त्वविसृष्टये ॥ 78
16.m: Then, having bound a white turban, he should worship them in sequence on both hands / mutually, for the burning of fetters and the emission of the pure principles of reality.

16.s:
tejorūpeṇa mantrāṃśca śivahaste samarcayet /
garbhāvaraṇagānaṅgaparivārāsanojjhitān // 79
16.d:
तेजोरूपेण मन्त्रांश्च शिवहस्ते समर्चयेत् ।
गर्भावरणगानङ्गपरिवारासनोज्झितान् ॥ 79
16.m: And he should worship the mantras in the form of fiery light upon the hand of Śiva, / residing in the inner enclosure, devoid of secondary limbs, retinue, and seats.

16.s:
ātmānaṃ bhāvayetpaścādekakaṃ jalacandravat /
kṛtyopādhivaśādbhinnaṃ ṣoḍhābhinnaṃ tu vastutaḥ // 80
16.d:
आत्मानं भावयेत्पश्चादेककं जलचन्द्रवत् ।
कृत्योपाधिवशाद्भिन्नं षोढाभिन्नं तु वस्तुतः ॥ 80
16.m: Then he should contemplate himself as single, like the moon in water, / divided on account of the conditions of ritual acts, though sixfold, undivided in reality:

16.s:
maṇḍalastho'hamevāyaṃ sākṣī cākhilakarmaṇām /
śuddhā hi draṣṭṛtā śambhormaṇḍale kalpitā mayā // 81
16.d:
मण्डलस्थोऽहमेवायं साक्षी चाखिलकर्मणाम् ।
शुद्धा हि द्रष्टृता शम्भोर्मण्डले कल्पिता मया ॥ 81
16.m: 'I myself am this one situated in the mandala, the witness of all actions; / for pure spectatorship of Śambhu has been conceived by me in the mandala.

16.s:
homādhikaraṇatvena vahnāvahamavasthitaḥ /
yadātmateddhā mantrāḥ syuḥ pāśaploṣavidhāvalam // 82
16.d:
होमाधिकरणत्वेन वह्नावहमवस्थितः ।
यदात्मतेद्धा मन्त्राः स्युः पाशप्लोषविधावलम् ॥ 82
16.m: I am seated in the fire as the locus of oblations, / so that the mantras, ignited by My nature, are fully capable in the rite of burning away fetters.

16.s:
sāmānyatejorūpāntarāhūtā bhuvaneśvarāḥ /
tarpitāḥ śrāvitāścāṇornādhikāraṃ pratanvate // 83
16.d:
सामान्यतेजोरूपान्तराहूता भुवनेश्वराः ।
तर्पिताः श्राविताश्चाणोर्नाधिकारं प्रतन्वते ॥ 83
16.m: Invoked into the general form of fiery light, satisfied, and addressed, / the lords of the worlds do not exercise authority over the individual soul.

16.s:
ā yāgāntamahaṃ kumbhe saṃsthito vighnaśāntaye /
sāmānyarūpatā yena viśeṣāpyāyakāriṇī // 84
16.d:
आ यागान्तमहं कुम्भे संस्थितो विघ्नशान्तये ।
सामान्यरूपता येन विशेषाप्यायकारिणी ॥ 84
16.m: Until the end of the sacrifice I reside in the pot for the pacification of obstacles, / whereby general nature brings about the nourishing of particularity.

16.s:
śiṣyadehe ca tatpāśaśithilatvaprasiddhaye /
sa hi svecchāvaśātpāśānvidhunvanniva vartate // 85
16.d:
शिष्यदेहे च तत्पाशशिथिलत्वप्रसिद्धये ।
स हि स्वेच्छावशात्पाशान्विधुन्वन्निव वर्तते ॥ 85
16.m: And [I reside] in the body of the disciple to bring about the loosening of his fetters; / for by the power of his own will he remains, as it were, shaking off the fetters.

16.s:
sākṣātsvadehasaṃstho'haṃ kartānugrahakarmaṇām /
jñānakriyāsvatantratvāddīkṣākarmaṇi peśalaḥ // 86
16.d:
साक्षात्स्वदेहसंस्थोऽहं कर्तानुग्रहकर्मणाम् ।
ज्ञानक्रियास्वतन्त्रत्वाद्दीक्षाकर्मणि पेशलः ॥ 86
16.m: Directly situated in my own body, I am the agent of acts of grace, / skilled in the rite of initiation because of autonomy in knowledge and action.

16.s:
bhinnakāryākṛtivrātendriyacakrānusandhimān /
eko yathāhaṃ vahnyādiṣaḍrūpo'smi tathā sphuṭam // 87
16.d:
भिन्नकार्याकृतिव्रातेन्द्रियचक्रानुसन्धिमान् ।
एको यथाहं वह्न्यादिषड्रूपोऽस्मि तथा स्फुटम् ॥ 87
16.m: Just as I, although one, focusing upon the wheel of sense organs and the host of manifold bodily forms of effects, / am thus clearly of six forms, beginning with fire.'

16.s:
evamālocya yenaiṣo'dhvanā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣati /
anusaṃhitaye śiṣyavarjaṃ pañcasu taṃ yajet // 88
16.d:
एवमालोच्य येनैषोऽध्वना दीक्षां चिकीर्षति ।
अनुसंहितये शिष्यवर्जं पञ्चसु तं यजेत् ॥ 88
16.m: Reflecting thus, through whichever path he desires to perform initiation, / he should worship it in the five [loci], excluding the disciple, for the sake of unification.

16.s:
anusandhibalānte ca samāsavyāsabhedataḥ /
kuryādatyantamabhyastamanyāntarbhāvapūritam // 89
16.d:
अनुसन्धिबलान्ते च समासव्यासभेदतः ।
कुर्यादत्यन्तमभ्यस्तमन्यान्तर्भावपूरितम् ॥ 89
16.m: And at the end of the power of focused unification, through the division of synthesis and analysis, / he should make it thoroughly habitual, filled with inclusion of the others.

16.s:
tato'pi cintayā bhūyo'nusandadhyācchivātmatām /
ahameva paraṃ tattvaṃ naca paddhaṭavat kvacit // 90
16.d:
ततोऽपि चिन्तया भूयोऽनुसन्दध्याच्छिवात्मताम् ।
अहमेव परं तत्त्वं नच पद्धटवत् क्वचित् ॥ 90
16.m: Then, through contemplation, he should repeatedly focus upon his nature as Śiva: / 'I alone am the supreme principle of reality, and nowhere like a low road.

16.s:
mahāprakāśastattena mayi sarvamidaṃ jagat /
naca tatkenacidbāhyapratibimbavadarpitam // 91
16.d:
महाप्रकाशस्तत्तेन मयि सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
नच तत्केनचिद्बाह्यप्रतिबिम्बवदर्पितम् ॥ 91
16.m: The Great Luminosity is real; therefore all this universe exists in Me, / and it is not impressed by anyone like an external reflection.

16.s:
kartāhamasya tannānyādhīnaṃ ca madadhiṣṭhitam /
itthaṃbhūtamahāvyāptisaṃvedanapavitritaḥ // 92
16.d:
कर्ताहमस्य तन्नान्याधीनं च मदधिष्ठितम् ।
इत्थंभूतमहाव्याप्तिसंवेदनपवित्रितः ॥ 92
16.m: I am the agent of this; therefore it is not dependent on anything else and is presided over by Me.' / Purified by the awareness of such a great all-pervasion,

16.s:
matsamatvaṃ gato janturmukta ityabhidhīyate /
tāpanirgharṣasekādipāramparyeṇa vahnitām // 93
16.d:
मत्समत्वं गतो जन्तुर्मुक्त इत्यभिधीयते ।
तापनिर्घर्षसेकादिपारम्पर्येण वह्निताम् ॥ 93
16.m: a creature who attains equality with Me is called liberated. / Just as an iron ball attains the nature of fire through a succession of heating, rubbing, sprinkling, and so forth,

16.s:
yathāyogolako yāti gururevaṃ śivātmatām /
tataḥ puraḥsthitaṃ yadvā purobhāvitavigraham // 94
16.d:
यथायोगोलको याति गुरुरेवं शिवात्मताम् ।
ततः पुरःस्थितं यद्वा पुरोभावितविग्रहम् ॥ 94
16.m: so the guru attains the nature of Śiva. / Then, having looked upon the disciple situated in front, or whose body is visualized in front,

16.s:
parokṣadīkṣaṇe yadvā darbhādyaiḥ kalpite mṛte /
śiṣye vīkṣyārcya puṣpādyairnyasedadhvānamasya tam // 95
16.d:
परोक्षदीक्षणे यद्वा दर्भाद्यैः कल्पिते मृते ।
शिष्ये वीक्ष्यार्च्य पुष्पाद्यैर्न्यसेदध्वानमस्य तम् ॥ 95
16.m: or, in initiation in absentia, upon a deceased disciple fashioned with kuśa grass and the like, and having worshipped him with flowers and so on, he should deposit upon him that path.

16.s:
yenādhvanā mukhyatayā dīkṣāmicchati daiśikaḥ /
taṃ dehe nyasya tatrāntarbhāvyamanyaditi sthitiḥ // 96
16.d:
येनाध्वना मुख्यतया दीक्षामिच्छति दैशिकः ।
तं देहे न्यस्य तत्रान्तर्भाव्यमन्यदिति स्थितिः ॥ 96
16.m: Through whichever path the guru primarily wishes to initiate, / having deposited that on the body, the other is to be included within it: this is the established rule.

16.s:
śodhyādhvani ca vinyaste tatraiva pariśodhakam /
nyasedyathepsitaṃ mantraṃ śodhyaucityānusārataḥ // 97
16.d:
शोध्याध्वनि च विन्यस्ते तत्रैव परिशोधकम् ।
न्यसेद्यथेप्सितं मन्त्रं शोध्यौचित्यानुसारतः ॥ 97
16.m: And when the path to be purified is deposited, right there he should deposit / the purifier, the desired mantra, according to the suitability of what is to be purified.

16.s:
kvacicchodhyaṃ tvavinyasya śodhakanyāsamātrataḥ /
svayaṃ śuddhyati saṃśodhyaṃ śodhakasya prabhāvataḥ // 98
16.d:
क्वचिच्छोध्यं त्वविन्यस्य शोधकन्यासमात्रतः ।
स्वयं शुद्ध्यति संशोध्यं शोधकस्य प्रभावतः ॥ 98
16.m: In some cases, however, without depositing what is to be purified, merely by depositing the purifier, / what is to be purified is spontaneously purified through the efficacy of the purifier.

16.s:
aparaṃ parāparaṃ ca paraṃ ca vidhimicchayā /
tadyojanānusāreṇa śritvā nyāsaḥ ṣaḍadhvanaḥ // 99
16.d:
अपरं परापरं च परं च विधिमिच्छया ।
तद्योजनानुसारेण श्रित्वा न्यासः षडध्वनः ॥ 99
16.m: Resorting at will to the lower, the intermediate, and the supreme procedure / according to its application, the imposition of the sixfold path is performed.

16.s:
lalāṭāntaṃ vedavasau randhrāntaṃ rasarandhrake /
vasukhendau dvādaśāntamityeṣa trividho vidhiḥ // 100
16.d:
ललाटान्तं वेदवसौ रन्ध्रान्तं रसरन्ध्रके ।
वसुखेन्दौ द्वादशान्तमित्येष त्रिविधो विधिः ॥ 100
16.m: Ending at the forehead in eighty-four, ending at the aperture [of Brahmā] in ninety-six, / ending at the twelve-finger space in one hundred and eight: this is the threefold procedure,

16.s:
krameṇa kathyate dṛṣṭaḥ śāstre śrīpūrvasaṃjñite /
tatra tattveṣu vinyāso gulphānte caturaṅgule // 101
16.d:
क्रमेण कथ्यते दृष्टः शास्त्रे श्रीपूर्वसंज्ञिते ।
तत्र तत्त्वेषु विन्यासो गुल्फान्ते चतुरङ्गुले ॥ 101
16.m: explained in sequence as seen in the scripture named the Venerable Pūrva. / Among these, the placement across the principles of reality is four finger-widths ending at the ankles;

16.s:
dharā jalādimūlāntaṃ pratyekaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ kramāt /
rasaśrutyaṅgulaṃ nābherūrdhvamitthaṃ ṣaḍaṅgule // 102
16.d:
धरा जलादिमूलान्तं प्रत्येकं द्व्यङ्गुलं क्रमात् ।
रसश्रुत्यङ्गुलं नाभेरूर्ध्वमित्थं षडङ्गुले ॥ 102
16.m:
Earth [occupies] four finger-widths [up to the ankle]; from water to root-matter (mūla/prakṛti), each [occupies] two finger-widths successively.
Thus [a total of] forty-six finger-widths, six finger-widths above the navel. // 102

16.s:
puṃsaḥ kalāntaṃ ṣaṭtattvīṃ pratyekaṃ tryaṅgule kṣipet /
aṣṭādaśāṅgulaṃ tvevaṃ kaṇṭhakūpāvasānakam // 103
16.d:
पुंसः कलान्तं षट्तत्त्वीं प्रत्येकं त्र्यङ्गुले क्षिपेत् ।
अष्टादशाङ्गुलं त्वेवं कण्ठकूपावसानकम् ॥ 103
16.m: he should assign the group of six principles up to the principle of the person, at three finger-widths each; / thus it is eighteen finger-widths ending at the hollow of the throat.

16.s:
sadāśivāntaṃ māyādicatuṣkaṃ caturaṅgule /
pratyekamityabdhivasusaṃkhyamālikadeśataḥ // 104
16.d:
सदाशिवान्तं मायादिचतुष्कं चतुरङ्गुले ।
प्रत्येकमित्यब्धिवसुसंख्यमालिकदेशतः ॥ 104
16.m: Ending with Sadāśiva, the tetrad beginning with māyā [is placed] in four digits / each: thus, counting eighty-four [digits] from the region of the crown of the head.

16.s:
śivatattvaṃ tataḥ paścāttejorūpamanākulam /
sarveṣāṃ vyāpakatvena sabāhyābhyantaraṃ smaret // 105
16.d:
शिवतत्त्वं ततः पश्चात्तेजोरूपमनाकुलम् ।
सर्वेषां व्यापकत्वेन सबाह्याभ्यन्तरं स्मरेत् ॥ 105
16.m: After that, one should contemplate the Śiva-principle as consisting of light, unperturbed, / pervading all things, both externally and internally.

16.s:
jalāddhyantaṃ sārdhayugmaṃ mūlaṃ tryaṅgulamityataḥ /
dvādaśāṅgulatādhikyādvidhireṣa parāparaḥ // 106
16.d:
जलाद्ध्यन्तं सार्धयुग्मं मूलं त्र्यङ्गुलमित्यतः ।
द्वादशाङ्गुलताधिक्याद्विधिरेष परापरः ॥ 106
16.m: From water to intellect [each is] two and a half [digits], and primordial matter is three digits; hence, / because of an excess of twelve digits, this rule is the higher-lower (parāpara).

16.s:
jalāddhyantaṃ tryaṅgule cedavyaktaṃ tu catuṣṭaye /
taccaturviṃśatyādhikyātparo'pyaṣṭaśate vidhiḥ // 107
16.d:
जलाद्ध्यन्तं त्र्यङ्गुले चेदव्यक्तं तु चतुष्टये ।
तच्चतुर्विंशत्याधिक्यात्परोऽप्यष्टशते विधिः ॥ 107
16.m: If from water to intellect [each is] three digits, while the unmanifest (avyakta) is four [digits], / then because of an excess of twenty-four, this rule is also the highest (para), in one hundred and eight [digits].

16.s:
trividhonmānakaṃ vyaktaṃ vasudigbhyo ravikṣayāt /
mayatantre tathācoktaṃ tattatsvaphalavāñchayā // 108
16.d:
त्रिविधोन्मानकं व्यक्तं वसुदिग्भ्यो रविक्षयात् ।
मयतन्त्रे तथाचोक्तं तत्तत्स्वफलवाञ्छया ॥ 108
16.m: The manifest measure is threefold, by subtraction of twelve from eighty-four and from [ninety-]six. / And so it is stated in the Mayatantra, according to the desire for their respective fruits.

16.s:
navapañcacatustryekatattvanyāse svayaṃ dhiyā /
nyāsaṃ prakalpayettāvattattvāntarbhāvacintanāt // 109
16.d:
नवपञ्चचतुस्त्र्येकतत्त्वन्यासे स्वयं धिया ।
न्यासं प्रकल्पयेत्तावत्तत्त्वान्तर्भावचिन्तनात् ॥ 109
16.m: When performing the placement of nine, five, four, three, or one principle, by one's own intellect / one should devise the placement by contemplating the inclusion of those principles.

16.s:
kalāpañcakavedāṇḍanyāso'nenaiva lakṣitaḥ /
uktaṃ ca triśirastantre svādhārasthaṃ yathāsthitam // 110
16.d:
कलापञ्चकवेदाण्डन्यासोऽनेनैव लक्षितः ।
उक्तं च त्रिशिरस्तन्त्रे स्वाधारस्थं यथास्थितम् ॥ 110
16.m: The placement of the five capacities (kalā) and the four cosmic eggs is also indicated by this very [method]. / And it is stated in the Triśirastantra that it resides in its own support as it is situated:

16.s:
dvādaśāṅgulamutthānaṃ dehātītaṃ samaṃ tataḥ /
dvāsaptatirdaśa dve ca dehasthaṃ śiraso'ntataḥ // 111
16.d:
द्वादशाङ्गुलमुत्थानं देहातीतं समं ततः ।
द्वासप्ततिर्दश द्वे च देहस्थं शिरसोऽन्ततः ॥ 111
16.m: “The ascent is twelve digits; equal to that, it transcends the body. / Then, seventy-two and ten and two [digits, total eighty-four,] reside within the body, up to the end of the head.

16.s:
pādādārabhya suśroṇi anāhatapadāvadhi /
dehātīte'pi viśrāntyā saṃvitteḥ kalpanāvaśāt // 112
16.d:
पादादारभ्य सुश्रोणि अनाहतपदावधि ।
देहातीतेऽपि विश्रान्त्या संवित्तेः कल्पनावशात् ॥ 112
16.m: Beginning from the feet, O fair-hipped one, up to the stage of the anāhata, / because consciousness comes to rest even in what transcends the body through conceptualization,

16.s:
dehatvamiti tasmātsyādutthānaṃ dvādaśāṅgulam /
iti nirṇetumatraitaduktamaṣṭottaraṃ śatam // 113
16.d:
देहत्वमिति तस्मात्स्यादुत्थानं द्वादशाङ्गुलम् ।
इति निर्णेतुमत्रैतदुक्तमष्टोत्तरं शतम् ॥ 113
16.m: it is said to have the nature of the body; therefore the ascent is twelve digits.” / To determine this here, this [measure of] one hundred and eight has been stated.

16.s:
puranyāso'tha gulphāntaṃ bhūḥ purāṇyatra ṣoḍaśa /
tasmādekāṅgulavyāptyā pratyekaṃ lakulāditaḥ // 114
16.d:
पुरन्यासोऽथ गुल्फान्तं भूः पुराण्यत्र षोडश ।
तस्मादेकाङ्गुलव्याप्त्या प्रत्येकं लकुलादितः ॥ 114
16.m: Now, the placement of the worlds: earth [extends] up to the ankles; here there are sixteen worlds. / Therefore, with an extent of one digit each, beginning with Lakulin [they are placed].

16.s:
dviraṇḍāntaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ tu cchagalāṇḍamathābdhiṣu /
devayogāṣṭake dve hi pratyekāṅgulapādataḥ // 115
16.d:
द्विरण्डान्तं त्र्यङ्गुलं तु च्छगलाण्डमथाब्धिषु ।
देवयोगाष्टके द्वे हि प्रत्येकाङ्गुलपादतः ॥ 115
16.m: Up to Dviranda is three digits; then Chagalāṇḍa is in four; / in the eight devayogas there are two [digits], with a quarter digit for each.

16.s:
iti pradhānaparyantaṃ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadaṅgulam /
ṣaṭpañcāśatpurāṇītthaṃ prāgdharāyāṃ tu ṣoḍaśa // 116
16.d:
इति प्रधानपर्यन्तं षट्चत्वारिंशदङ्गुलम् ।
षट्पञ्चाशत्पुराणीत्थं प्राग्धरायां तु षोडश ॥ 116
16.m: Thus, up to pradhāna is forty-six digits; / thus there are fifty-six worlds, while previously in earth there were sixteen.

16.s:
tato'pyardhāṅgulavyāptyā ṣaṭpurāṇyaṅgulatraye /
catvāri yugma ekasminnekaṃ ca puramaṅgule // 117
16.d:
ततोऽप्यर्धाङ्गुलव्याप्त्या षट्पुराण्यङ्गुलत्रये ।
चत्वारि युग्म एकस्मिन्नेकं च पुरमङ्गुले ॥ 117
16.m: Then, with an extent of half a digit [each], six worlds are in three digits; / four [worlds] are in two [digits], and one world in one digit.

16.s:
sarāge puṃspurāṇīśasaṃkhyānītthaṃ ṣaḍaṅgule /
krodheśapuramekasmindvaye cāṇḍamiyaṃ ca vit // 118
16.d:
सरागे पुंस्पुराणीशसंख्यानीत्थं षडङ्गुले ।
क्रोधेशपुरमेकस्मिन्द्वये चाण्डमियं च वित् ॥ 118
16.m: With passion, the worlds of the puruṣa are eleven in number, thus in six digits. / The world of Krodheśa is in one [digit], and the cosmic egg is in two, and this is knowledge (vidyā).

16.s:
saṃvartajyotiṣorevaṃ kalātattvagayoḥ kramāt /
śūrapañcāntapurayorniyatau caikayugmatā // 119
16.d:
संवर्तज्योतिषोरेवं कलातत्त्वगयोः क्रमात् ।
शूरपञ्चान्तपुरयोर्नियतौ चैकयुग्मता ॥ 119
16.m: In this way, in Samvarta and Jyotis, situated in the kalā-principle respectively, / and in the worlds Śūra and Pañcānta, in niyati, there is one pair.

16.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre taccoktaṃ parameśena śaṃbhunā /
uttarādikramādadvyekabhedo vidyādike traye // 120
16.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तच्चोक्तं परमेशेन शंभुना ।
उत्तरादिक्रमादद्व्येकभेदो विद्यादिके त्रये ॥ 120
16.m: And that has been spoken in the revered Pūrvaśāstra by the supreme Lord, Śambhu. / By the upward order, there is a distinction of two and one in the triad beginning with vidyā.

16.s:
asāratvātkramasyādau niyatiḥ parataḥ kalā /
athavānyonyasaṃjñābhyāṃ tattvayorvyapadeśyatā // 121
16.d:
असारत्वात्क्रमस्यादौ नियतिः परतः कला ।
अथवान्योन्यसंज्ञाभ्यां तत्त्वयोर्व्यपदेश्यता ॥ 121
16.m: Because of the lack of essentiality in the order, niyati is first and kalā is beyond, / or the two principles are designated by each other's names.

16.s:
ekavīraśikheśaśrīkaṇṭhāḥ kāle trayastraye /
kālasya pūrvaṃ vinyāso niyaterabhidhīyate // 122
16.d:
एकवीरशिखेशश्रीकण्ठाः काले त्रयस्त्रये ।
कालस्य पूर्वं विन्यासो नियतेरभिधीयते ॥ 122
16.m: Ekavīra, Śikheśa, and Śrīkaṇṭha are three in three [digits] in time (kāla). / The placement of kāla is stated before niyati,

16.s:
athavānyonyasaṃjñābhirvyapadeśo hi dṛśyate /
evaṃ pumādiṣaṭtattvī vinyastāṣṭādaśāṅgule // 123
16.d:
अथवान्योन्यसंज्ञाभिर्व्यपदेशो हि दृश्यते ।
एवं पुमादिषट्तत्त्वी विन्यस्ताष्टादशाङ्गुले ॥ 123
16.m: or indeed their designation is seen through mutual names. / Thus the hexad of principles beginning with the soul is placed in eighteen digits.

16.s:
tato'pyaṅguṣṭhamātrāntaṃ māyātattvasthamaṣṭakam /
pratyekamardhāṅgulataḥ syādaṅgulacatuṣṭaye // 124
16.d:
ततोऽप्यङ्गुष्ठमात्रान्तं मायातत्त्वस्थमष्टकम् ।
प्रत्येकमर्धाङ्गुलतः स्यादङ्गुलचतुष्टये ॥ 124
16.m: Then, ending with the measure of a thumb, the octad situated in the māyā-principle / consists of half a digit each, in four digits.

16.s:
itthaṃ dvyakṣṇi purāṇyaṣṭāviṃśatiḥ puruṣānniśi /
puratrayaṃ dvayostryaṃśanyūnāṅgulamiti kramāt // 125
16.d:
इत्थं द्व्यक्ष्णि पुराण्यष्टाविंशतिः पुरुषान्निशि ।
पुरत्रयं द्वयोस्त्र्यंशन्यूनाङ्गुलमिति क्रमात् ॥ 125
16.m: Thus in twenty-two [digits] there are twenty-eight worlds from the puruṣa in darkness (niśi). / The triad of worlds in two [digits] is one digit less by a third, in this order;

16.s:
dvayordvayaṃ pañcapurī vaidyīye caturaṅgule /
tata aiśapurāṇyaṣṭau catuṣke'rdhāṅgulakramāt // 126
16.d:
द्वयोर्द्वयं पञ्चपुरी वैद्यीये चतुरङ्गुले ।
तत ऐशपुराण्यष्टौ चतुष्केऽर्धाङ्गुलक्रमात् ॥ 126
16.m: in two [digits] there are two, making a pentad of worlds in four digits of the Śuddhavidyā. / Then there are eight worlds of Īśvara in four [digits], in the order of half a digit [each].

16.s:
tatastrīṇi dvaye dve ca dvayoritthaṃ catuṣṭaye /
sādāśivaṃ pañcakaṃ syāditthaṃ vasvekakaṃ ravau // 127
16.d:
ततस्त्रीणि द्वये द्वे च द्वयोरित्थं चतुष्टये ।
सादाशिवं पञ्चकं स्यादित्थं वस्वेककं रवौ ॥ 127
16.m: Then three [worlds] in two [digits] and two in two [digits]: thus in four [digits] / there is the pentad of Sadāśiva; thus there are eighteen in twelve [digits].

16.s:
ṣoḍaśakaṃ rasaviśikhaṃ vasudvikaṃ vasuśaśīti puravargāḥ /
vedā rasābdhi yugmākṣi ca ravayastatra cāṅgulāḥ kramaśaḥ // 128
16.d:
षोडशकं रसविशिखं वसुद्विकं वसुशशीति पुरवर्गाः ।
वेदा रसाब्धि युग्माक्षि च रवयस्तत्र चाङ्गुलाः क्रमशः ॥ 128
16.m: Sixteen, fifty-six, twenty-eight, and eighteen are the groups of worlds; / four, forty-six, twenty-two, and twelve are the digits there, in order.

16.s:
aṣṭādaśādhikaśataṃ purāṇi dehe'tra caturaśītimite /
vinyastāni taditthaṃ śeṣe tu vyāpakaṃ śivaṃ tattvam // 129
16.d:
अष्टादशाधिकशतं पुराणि देहेऽत्र चतुरशीतिमिते ।
विन्यस्तानि तदित्थं शेषे तु व्यापकं शिवं तत्त्वम् ॥ 129
16.m: One hundred and eighteen worlds are thus placed in this body measuring eighty-four [digits]; / but in what remains, the Śiva-principle is all-pervading.

16.s:
iti vidhiraparaḥ kathitaḥ parāparākhyo rasaśrutisthāne /
aṣṭaśaraṃ saṃkhyānaṃ khamunikṛtaṃ tatpare vidhau jñeyam // 130
16.d:
इति विधिरपरः कथितः परापराख्यो रसश्रुतिस्थाने ।
अष्टशरं संख्यानं खमुनिकृतं तत्परे विधौ ज्ञेयम् ॥ 130
16.m: Thus the lower rule is declared. In the place of sixty-six, the one called the higher-lower / has the number fifty-eight; and in the highest rule, it should be known as made of seventy.

16.s:
lakulāderyogāṣṭakaparyantasyātra bhuvanapūgasya /
adhikīkuryādgaṇanāvaśena bhāgaṃ vidhidvaye kramaśaḥ // 131
16.d:
लकुलादेर्योगाष्टकपर्यन्तस्यात्र भुवनपूगस्य ।
अधिकीकुर्याद्गणनावशेन भागं विधिद्वये क्रमशः ॥ 131
16.m: Here, for the group of worlds from Lakulin up to the eight yogas, / one should increase the portion according to the calculation in the two rules, respectively.

16.s:
aparādividhitraitādatha nyāsaḥ padādhvanaḥ /
pūrvaṃ daśapadī coktā svatantrā nyasyate yadā // 132
16.d:
अपरादिविधित्रैतादथ न्यासः पदाध्वनः ।
पूर्वं दशपदी चोक्ता स्वतन्त्रा न्यस्यते यदा ॥ 132
16.m: From this triad of rules, beginning with the lower, [proceeds] next the placement of the path of words (pada). / Earlier, the decad of words was stated when placed independently.

16.s:
tayaiva dīkṣā kāryā cettadeyaṃ nyāsakalpanā /
tattvādimukhyatāyogāddīkṣāyāṃ tu padāvalī // 133
16.d:
तयैव दीक्षा कार्या चेत्तदेयं न्यासकल्पना ।
तत्त्वादिमुख्यतायोगाद्दीक्षायां तु पदावली ॥ 133
16.m: If initiation is to be performed by that alone, then this arrangement of placement [applies]. / But in an initiation connected with the prominence of the principles and the rest, the series of words,

16.s:
tattattvādyanusāreṇa tatrāntarbhāvyate tathā /
svapradhānatvayoge tu dīkṣāyāṃ padapaddhatim // 134
16.d:
तत्तत्त्वाद्यनुसारेण तत्रान्तर्भाव्यते तथा ।
स्वप्रधानत्वयोगे तु दीक्षायां पदपद्धतिम् ॥ 134
16.m: in accordance with those respective principles and so forth, is likewise subsumed therein. / But in the event of its own predominance in initiation, the series of words,

16.s:
nyasyetkrameṇa tattvādivadanānavalokinīm /
caturṣvaṣṭāsu cāṣṭāsu daśasvatha daśasvatha // 135
16.d:
न्यस्येत्क्रमेण तत्त्वादिवदनानवलोकिनीम् ।
चतुर्ष्वष्टासु चाष्टासु दशस्वथ दशस्वथ ॥ 135
16.m: which does not look upon the face of the principles and the rest, one should place in order: / in four, in eight, and in eight; then in ten, then in ten;

16.s:
daśasvatho pañcadaśasvatha vedaśarenduṣu /
dharāpadānnavapadīṃ mātṛkāmālinīgatām // 136
16.d:
दशस्वथो पञ्चदशस्वथ वेदशरेन्दुषु ।
धरापदान्नवपदीं मातृकामालिनीगताम् ॥ 136
16.m: then in ten, then in fifteen, and then in one hundred and fifty-four: / one should join the ennead of words belonging to the mātṛkā and mālinī, beginning with the word for earth (dharā);

16.s:
yojayedvyāptṛ daśamaṃ padaṃ tu śivasaṃjñitam /
dharāpadaṃ varjayitvā pañca yāni padāni tu // 137
16.d:
योजयेद्व्याप्तृ दशमं पदं तु शिवसंज्ञितम् ।
धरापदं वर्जयित्वा पञ्च यानि पदानि तु ॥ 137
16.m: and the tenth word, called Śiva, is the all-pervader. / But excluding the word for earth, the five words which [remain],

16.s:
vidhidvayaṃ syānnikṣipya dvādaśa dvādaśāṅgulān /
mantrādhvano'pyeṣa eva vidhirvinyāsayojane // 138
16.d:
विधिद्वयं स्यान्निक्षिप्य द्वादश द्वादशाङ्गुलान् ।
मन्त्राध्वनोऽप्येष एव विधिर्विन्यासयोजने ॥ 138
16.m: placing twelve digits each, become the two [other] rules. / This very same rule applies to the placement and application of the path of mantras.

16.s:
vyāptimātraṃ hi bhidyetetyuktaṃ prāgeva tattathā /
varṇādhvano'tha vinyāsaḥ kathyate'tra vidhitraye // 139
16.d:
व्याप्तिमात्रं हि भिद्येतेत्युक्तं प्रागेव तत्तथा ।
वर्णाध्वनोऽथ विन्यासः कथ्यतेऽत्र विधित्रये ॥ 139
16.m: For it was already stated earlier that only the pervasion differs, and that is so. / Now the placement of the path of phonemes (varṇa) is explained here in the triad of rules:

16.s:
ekaṃ caturṣu pratyekaṃ dvayoraṅgulayoḥ kramāt /
trayoviṃśativarṇī syāt ṣaḍvarṇyekaikaśastriṣu // 140
16.d:
एकं चतुर्षु प्रत्येकं द्वयोरङ्गुलयोः क्रमात् ।
त्रयोविंशतिवर्णी स्यात् षड्वर्ण्येकैकशस्त्रिषु ॥ 140
16.m: one in four, each in two digits in order; / there is the group of twenty-three phonemes, and the group of six phonemes, each one in three [digits];

16.s:
pratyekamatha catvāraścaturṣviti vilomataḥ /
mālinīmātṛkārṇāḥ syurvyāptṛ śaivaṃ rasendutaḥ // 141
16.d:
प्रत्येकमथ चत्वारश्चतुर्ष्विति विलोमतः ।
मालिनीमातृकार्णाः स्युर्व्याप्तृ शैवं रसेन्दुतः ॥ 141
16.m: then four in four [digits] each; thus, in reverse order, / the phonemes of the mālinī and mātṛkā are [placed]; that which belongs to Śiva is the pervader in sixteen [digits].

16.s:
varjayitvādyavarṇaṃ tu tattvavatsyādravīnnavīn /
tāṃ trayoviṃśatau varṇeṣvapyanyatsyādvidhidvayam // 142
16.d:
वर्जयित्वाद्यवर्णं तु तत्त्ववत्स्याद्रवीन्नवीन् ।
तां त्रयोविंशतौ वर्णेष्वप्यन्यत्स्याद्विधिद्वयम् ॥ 142
16.m: Excluding the initial phoneme, just as with the principles, there would be twelve and nine; / and in those twenty-three phonemes there are two other rules.

16.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre tenādau tattveṣūktaṃ vidhitrayam /
atidiṣṭaṃ tu tadbhinnābhinnavarṇadvaye samam // 143
16.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तेनादौ तत्त्वेषूक्तं विधित्रयम् ।
अतिदिष्टं तु तद्भिन्नाभिन्नवर्णद्वये समम् ॥ 143
16.m: Therefore, in the revered Pūrvaśāstra the triad of rules was first stated for the principles, / but it is extended equally to the two phoneme-series, both differentiated and undifferentiated from it.

16.s:
dvividho'pi hi varṇānāṃ ṣaḍvidho bheda ucyate /
tattvamārgavidhānena jñātavyaḥ paramārthataḥ // 144
16.d:
द्विविधोऽपि हि वर्णानां षड्विधो भेद उच्यते ।
तत्त्वमार्गविधानेन ज्ञातव्यः परमार्थतः ॥ 144
16.m: For even though twofold, the sixfold division of phonemes is spoken of; / it should be known in ultimate reality through the procedure of the path of principles.

16.s:
upadeśātideśābhyāṃ yaduktaṃ tatpadādiṣu /
bhūyo'tidiṣṭaṃ tatraiva śāstre'smaddhṛdayeśvare // 145
16.d:
उपदेशातिदेशाभ्यां यदुक्तं तत्पदादिषु ।
भूयोऽतिदिष्टं तत्रैव शास्त्रेऽस्मद्धृदयेश्वरे ॥ 145
16.m: What was stated by direct instruction and by extension regarding words and the rest / is further extended right there in that scripture, the lord of our heart.

16.s:
padamantrakalādīnāṃ pūrvasūtrānusārataḥ /
tritayatvaṃ prakurvīta tattvavarṇoktavartmanā // 146
16.d:
पदमन्त्रकलादीनां पूर्वसूत्रानुसारतः ।
त्रितयत्वं प्रकुर्वीत तत्त्ववर्णोक्तवर्त्मना ॥ 146
16.m: In accordance with the earlier aphorism, one should make the threefold nature / of words, mantras, capacities (kalā), and so on, following the way declared for principles and phonemes.

16.s:
uktaṃ tatpadamantreṣu kalāsvatha nirūpyate /
caturṣu rasavede dvāviṃśatau dvādaśasvatha // 147
16.d:
उक्तं तत्पदमन्त्रेषु कलास्वथ निरूप्यते ।
चतुर्षु रसवेदे द्वाविंशतौ द्वादशस्वथ ॥ 147
16.m: That has been stated regarding words and mantras; now it is examined regarding the capacities (kalā): / in four, forty-six, twenty-two, and in twelve,

16.s:
nivṛttyādyāścatasraḥ syurvyāptrī syācchāntyatītikā /
dvitīyasyāṃ kalāyāṃ tu dvādaśa dvādaśāṅgulān // 148
16.d:
निवृत्त्याद्याश्चतस्रः स्युर्व्याप्त्री स्याच्छान्त्यतीतिका ।
द्वितीयस्यां कलायां तु द्वादश द्वादशाङ्गुलान् ॥ 148
16.m: there are the four beginning with nivṛtti; the pervader is śāntyatīta. / But in the second capacity, [one places] twelve digits [and] twelve digits,

16.s:
kramātkṣiptvā vidhidvaitaṃ parāparaparātmakam /
caturaṇḍavidhistvādiśabdeneha pragṛhyate // 149
16.d:
क्रमात्क्षिप्त्वा विधिद्वैतं परापरपरात्मकम् ।
चतुरण्डविधिस्त्वादिशब्देनेह प्रगृह्यते ॥ 149
16.m: having sequentially arranged the two rules consisting of the higher and the lower-and-higher. / But the rule of the four cosmic eggs is understood here by the word "etcetera".

16.s:
kalācatuṣkavattena tasminvācyaṃ vidhitrayam /
evaṃ ṣaḍvidhamadhvānaṃ śodhyaśiṣyatanau purā // 150
16.d:
कलाचतुष्कवत्तेन तस्मिन्वाच्यं विधित्रयम् ।
एवं षड्विधमध्वानं शोध्यशिष्यतनौ पुरा ॥ 150
16.m: Therefore, like the set of four kalās, the threefold rule should be stated with respect to that. / Having first imposed the sixfold path in this manner upon the body of the disciple to be purified,

16.s:
nyasyaikatamamukhyatvānnyasyecchodhakasaṃmatam /
adhvanyāsanamantraughaḥ śodhako hyeka āditaḥ // 151
16.d:
न्यस्यैकतममुख्यत्वान्न्यस्येच्छोधकसंमतम् ।
अध्वन्यासनमन्त्रौघः शोधको ह्येक आदितः ॥ 151
16.m: he should impose [it] through one principal [method] or as approved by the purifier. / For the host of mantras for the imposition of the path is the purifier, single from the beginning:

16.s:
śabdarāśirmālinī ca samastavyastato dvidhā /
ekavīratayā yadvā ṣaṭkaṃ yāmalayogataḥ // 152
16.d:
शब्दराशिर्मालिनी च समस्तव्यस्ततो द्विधा ।
एकवीरतया यद्वा षट्कं यामलयोगतः ॥ 152
16.m: the aggregate of phonemes and Mālinī are twofold by being collective or distributive; / or as sixfold by the state of being a solitary hero, [or] through union as a dyad.

16.s:
pañcavaktrī śaktitadvadbhedātṣoḍhā punardvidhā /
ekākiyāmalatvenetyevaṃ sā dvādaśātmikā // 153
16.d:
पञ्चवक्त्री शक्तितद्वद्भेदात्षोढा पुनर्द्विधा ।
एकाकियामलत्वेनेत्येवं सा द्वादशात्मिका ॥ 153
16.m: The five-faced [mantra] is sixfold through the distinction of the power and the possessor of power, and twofold again / through the state of being solitary or a dyad; thus it consists of twelve.

16.s:
ṣaḍaṅgī sakalānyatvāddvividhā vaktravatpunaḥ /
dvādaśatvena guṇitā caturviṃśatibhedikā // 154
16.d:
षडङ्गी सकलान्यत्वाद्द्विविधा वक्त्रवत्पुनः ।
द्वादशत्वेन गुणिता चतुर्विंशतिभेदिका ॥ 154
16.m: The six-limbed [mantra] is twofold like the face[-mantras] because of being complete or otherwise; / multiplied by twelve, it has twenty-four divisions.

16.s:
aghorādyaṣṭake dve ca tṛtīyaṃ yāmalodayāt /
mātṛsadbhāvamantraśca kevalaḥ śruticakragaḥ // 155
16.d:
अघोराद्यष्टके द्वे च तृतीयं यामलोदयात् ।
मातृसद्भावमन्त्रश्च केवलः श्रुतिचक्रगः ॥ 155
16.m: There are two octads beginning with Aghora, and a third arising from the dyad; / and the Mātṛsadbhāva mantra is single, residing in the wheel of sacred texts,

16.s:
ekadvitricaturbhedāttrayodaśabhidātmakaḥ /
ekavīratayā so'yaṃ caturdaśatayā sthitaḥ // 156
16.d:
एकद्वित्रिचतुर्भेदात्त्रयोदशभिदात्मकः ।
एकवीरतया सोऽयं चतुर्दशतया स्थितः ॥ 156
16.m: consisting of thirteen varieties through the divisions of one, two, three, and four; / this, in the state of being a solitary hero, stands as fourteenfold.

16.s:
anāmasaṃhṛtisthairyasṛṣṭicakraṃ caturvidham /
devatābhirnijābhistanmātṛsadbhāvavṛṃhitam // 157
16.d:
अनामसंहृतिस्थैर्यसृष्टिचक्रं चतुर्विधम् ।
देवताभिर्निजाभिस्तन्मातृसद्भाववृंहितम् ॥ 157
16.m: The fourfold wheel of the nameless, resorption, stability, and creation, / with their own deities, is amplified by the Mātṛsadbhāva.

16.s:
itthaṃ śodhakavargo'yaṃ mantrāṇāṃ saptatiḥ smṛtā /
ṣaḍardhaśāstreṣu śrīmatsāraśāstre ca kathyate // 158
16.d:
इत्थं शोधकवर्गोऽयं मन्त्राणां सप्ततिः स्मृता ।
षडर्धशास्त्रेषु श्रीमत्सारशास्त्रे च कथ्यते ॥ 158
16.m: Thus this purifier group of mantras is traditionally remembered as seventy. / In the Trika scriptures and in the venerable Sāraśāstra it is said:

16.s:
aghorādyaṣṭakeneha śodhanīyaṃ vipaścitā /
athavaikākṣarāmantrairathavā mātṛkākramāt // 159
16.d:
अघोराद्यष्टकेनेह शोधनीयं विपश्चिता ।
अथवैकाक्षरामन्त्रैरथवा मातृकाक्रमात् ॥ 159
16.m: “Here purification is to be performed by the wise master by the octad beginning with Aghora, / or by single-syllable mantras, or by the sequence of the phonemes,

16.s:
bhairavīyahṛdā vāpi khecarīhṛdayena vā /
bhairaveṇa mahādevi tvatha vaktrāṅgapañcakaiḥ // 160
16.d:
भैरवीयहृदा वापि खेचरीहृदयेन वा ।
भैरवेण महादेवि त्वथ वक्त्राङ्गपञ्चकैः ॥ 160
16.m: or by the heart of Bhairavī, or by the heart of Khecarī, / by Bhairava, O great goddess, or by the five faces and limbs.

16.s:
yena yena hi mantreṇa tantre'sminnudbhavaḥ kṛtaḥ /
tenaiva dīkṣayenmantrī ityājñā pārameśvarī // 161
16.d:
येन येन हि मन्त्रेण तन्त्रेऽस्मिन्नुद्भवः कृतः ।
तेनैव दीक्षयेन्मन्त्री इत्याज्ञा पारमेश्वरी ॥ 161
16.m: Indeed, by whatever mantra the emergence [of the initiate] was effected in this Tantra, / by that very [mantra] the mantrin should initiate him: such is the command of the Supreme Lord.”

16.s:
evaṃ śodhakabhedena saptatiḥ kīrtitā bhidaḥ /
śodhyanyāsaṃ vinā mantrairetairdīkṣā yadā bhavet // 162
16.d:
एवं शोधकभेदेन सप्ततिः कीर्तिता भिदः ।
शोध्यन्यासं विना मन्त्रैरेतैर्दीक्षा यदा भवेत् ॥ 162
16.m: Thus, through the division of purifiers, seventy varieties have been proclaimed. / When initiation is performed by these mantras without the imposition of what is to be purified,

16.s:
tadā saptatidhā jñeyā jananādivivarjitā /
śodhyabhedo'tha vaktavyaḥ saṃkṣepātso'pi kathyate // 163
16.d:
तदा सप्ततिधा ज्ञेया जननादिविवर्जिता ।
शोध्यभेदोऽथ वक्तव्यः संक्षेपात्सोऽपि कथ्यते ॥ 163
16.m: then it is to be known as seventyfold, free from [the rites of] birth and the rest. / Next, the division of what is to be purified should be stated; that too is related in brief:

16.s:
ekatripañcaṣaṭtriṃśadbhedāttāttvaścaturvidhaḥ /
pañcaikabhedāccādhvānastathaivāṇḍacatuṣṭayam // 164
16.d:
एकत्रिपञ्चषट्त्रिंशद्भेदात्तात्त्वश्चतुर्विधः ।
पञ्चैकभेदाच्चाध्वानस्तथैवाण्डचतुष्टयम् ॥ 164
16.m: pertaining to the principles, it is fourfold through the division into one, three, five, and thirty-six; / and the paths are [twofold] through the division into five and one, as likewise is the set of four cosmic eggs.

16.s:
evaṃ daśavidhaṃ śodhyaṃ triṃśaddhā tadvidhitrayāt /
śodhyaśodhakabhedena śatāni tvekaviṃśatiḥ // 165
16.d:
एवं दशविधं शोध्यं त्रिंशद्धा तद्विधित्रयात् ।
शोध्यशोधकभेदेन शतानि त्वेकविंशतिः ॥ 165
16.m: Thus what is to be purified is ten-fold; [and becomes] thirtyfold through their threefold rule. / Through the division of what is to be purified and the purifiers, there are twenty-one hundred [varieties].

16.s:
atrāpi nyāsayogena śodhye'dhvani tathākṛteḥ /
śataikaviṃśatibhidā jananādyujjhitā bhavet // 166
16.d:
अत्रापि न्यासयोगेन शोध्येऽध्वनि तथाकृतेः ।
शतैकविंशतिभिदा जननाद्युज्झिता भवेत् ॥ 166
16.m: Here too, when it is performed thus upon the path to be purified by means of imposition, / the twenty-one-hundred varieties are devoid of [rites like] birth and the rest.

16.s:
jananādimayī tāvatyevaṃ śatadṛśi śrutiḥ /
syātsaptatyadhikā sāpi dravyavijñānabhedataḥ // 167
16.d:
जननादिमयी तावत्येवं शतदृशि श्रुतिः ।
स्यात्सप्तत्यधिका सापि द्रव्यविज्ञानभेदतः ॥ 167
16.m: There are just as many consisting of birth and the rest; thus in the view of the scriptures, there are a hundred / plus seventy; and that too, through the division of substances and conscious awareness,

16.s:
dvidheti pañcāśītiḥ syācchatānyadhikakhābdhikā /
bhogamokṣānusandhānāddvividhā sā prakīrtitā // 168
16.d:
द्विधेति पञ्चाशीतिः स्याच्छतान्यधिकखाब्धिका ।
भोगमोक्षानुसन्धानाद्द्विविधा सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 168
16.m: is twofold; thus it amounts to eighty-five hundred plus forty. / It is proclaimed as twofold through the intention directed toward enjoyment or liberation.

16.s:
aśubhasyaiva saṃśuddhyā śubhasyāpyatha śodhanāt /
dvidhā bhogaḥ śubhe śuddhiḥ kālatrayavibhedini // 169
16.d:
अशुभस्यैव संशुद्ध्या शुभस्याप्यथ शोधनात् ।
द्विधा भोगः शुभे शुद्धिः कालत्रयविभेदिनि ॥ 169
16.m: Enjoyment is twofold, through the purification of the inauspicious [karma] alone, or through the purification of the auspicious as well. / When the auspicious [karma] dividing into the three times is purified,

16.s:
ekadvisāmastyavaśātsaptadhetyaṣṭadhā bhujiḥ /
guruśiṣyakramātso'pi dvidhetyevaṃ vibhidyate // 170
16.d:
एकद्विसामस्त्यवशात्सप्तधेत्यष्टधा भुजिः ।
गुरुशिष्यक्रमात्सोऽपि द्विधेत्येवं विभिद्यते ॥ 170
16.m: it is sevenfold through the operation of one, two, or all together; thus enjoyment is eightfold. / That too is divided into two in this manner, according to the sequence of guru and disciple,

16.s:
pratyakṣadīkṣaṇe yasmāddvayorekānusandhitaḥ /
tādṛgdīkṣāphalaṃ pūrṇaṃ visaṃvāde tu viplavaḥ // 171
16.d:
प्रत्यक्षदीक्षणे यस्माद्द्वयोरेकानुसन्धितः ।
तादृग्दीक्षाफलं पूर्णं विसंवादे तु विप्लवः ॥ 171
16.m: since in visible initiation, from the single intention of both, / the fruit of such an initiation is complete, but in case of disagreement there is ruin.

16.s:
parokṣamṛtadīkṣādau gururevānusandhimān /
kriyājñānamahimnā taṃ śiṣyaṃ dhāmnīpsite nayet // 172
16.d:
परोक्षमृतदीक्षादौ गुरुरेवानुसन्धिमान् ।
क्रियाज्ञानमहिम्ना तं शिष्यं धाम्नीप्सिते नयेत् ॥ 172
16.m: In invisible initiation, initiation of the dead, and so forth, the guru alone holds the intention; / by the power of action and knowledge, he should lead that disciple to the desired abode.

16.s:
avibhinne kriyājñāne karmaśuddhau tathaiva te /
anusandhiḥ punarbhinnaḥ karma yasmāttadātmakam // 173
16.d:
अविभिन्ने क्रियाज्ञाने कर्मशुद्धौ तथैव ते ।
अनुसन्धिः पुनर्भिन्नः कर्म यस्मात्तदात्मकम् ॥ 173
16.m: Even when action and knowledge are undivided, in the purification of karma they are likewise so; / but the intention is diverse, because karma is of that nature.

16.s:
śrīmatsvacchandaśāstre ca vāsanābhedataḥ phalam /
śiṣyāṇāṃ ca guroścoktamabhinne'pi kriyādike // 174
16.d:
श्रीमत्स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे च वासनाभेदतः फलम् ।
शिष्याणां च गुरोश्चोक्तमभिन्नेऽपि क्रियादिके ॥ 174
16.m: And in the venerable Svacchanda scripture, the fruit for the disciples and the guru / is declared to be due to diversity of latent traces, even when action and the rest are undivided.

16.s:
bhogasya śodhakācchodhyādanusandheśca tādṛśāt /
vaicitryamasti bhedasya vaicitryaprāṇatā yataḥ // 175
16.d:
भोगस्य शोधकाच्छोध्यादनुसन्धेश्च तादृशात् ।
वैचित्र्यमस्ति भेदस्य वैचित्र्यप्राणता यतः ॥ 175
16.m: There is a manifold variety of enjoyment arising from the purifier, from what is to be purified, and from such an intention, / because manifold variety is the very life of distinction.

16.s:
tathāhi vaktrairyasyādhvā śuddhastaireva yojitaḥ /
bhoktumiṣṭe kvacittattve sa bhoktā tadbalānvitaḥ // 176
16.d:
तथाहि वक्त्रैर्यस्याध्वा शुद्धस्तैरेव योजितः ।
भोक्तुमिष्टे क्वचित्तत्त्वे स भोक्ता तद्बलान्वितः ॥ 176
16.m: To explain: he whose path is purified by the face[-mantras] and united by them, / endowed with their power, becomes an enjoyer in whatever principle he desires to enjoy.

16.s:
śubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ cātra sadbhāve bhogacitratā /
tādṛgeva bhavetkarmaśuddhau tvanyaiva citratā // 177
16.d:
शुभानां कर्मणां चात्र सद्भावे भोगचित्रता ।
तादृगेव भवेत्कर्मशुद्धौ त्वन्यैव चित्रता ॥ 177
16.m: And in this case, when auspicious karmas exist, the manifoldness of enjoyment / is of such a kind; but when karma is purified, the manifoldness is of quite another kind.

16.s:
bhogaśca sadya+utkrāntyā dehenaivātha saṃgataḥ /
tadaivābhyāsato vāpi dehānte vetyasau catuḥ // 178
16.d:
भोगश्च सद्य+उत्क्रान्त्या देहेनैवाथ संगतः ।
तदैवाभ्यासतो वापि देहान्ते वेत्यसौ चतुः ॥ 178
16.m: And enjoyment is fourfold: through immediate departure, associated with this very body, / or right then through practice, or at the end of the body.

16.s:
prāktanāṣṭabhidā yogāddvātriṃśadbheda ucyate /
mokṣa eko'pi bījasya samayākhyasya tādṛśam // 179
16.d:
प्राक्तनाष्टभिदा योगाद्द्वात्रिंशद्भेद उच्यते ।
मोक्ष एकोऽपि बीजस्य समयाख्यस्य तादृशम् ॥ 179
16.m: Through association with the eight previous divisions, thirty-two varieties are spoken of. / Liberation, though one, is of such a kind through the seed called the rule of conduct;

16.s:
bālādikaṃ jñātaśīghramaraṇaṃ śaktivarjitam /
vṛddhaṃ voddiśya śaktaṃ vā śodhanāśodhanāddvidhā // 180
16.d:
बालादिकं ज्ञातशीघ्रमरणं शक्तिवर्जितम् ।
वृद्धं वोद्दिश्य शक्तं वा शोधनाशोधनाद्द्विधा ॥ 180
16.m: it is twofold, through purification or non-purification, with reference to a child or the like, one whose death is known to be imminent, one devoid of capacity, / an old person, or one who is capable.

16.s:
sadya+utkrāntitastraidhaṃ sā cāsannamṛtau guroḥ /
kāryetyājñā maheśasya śrīmadgahvarabhāṣitā // 181
16.d:
सद्य+उत्क्रान्तितस्त्रैधं सा चासन्नमृतौ गुरोः ।
कार्येत्याज्ञा महेशस्य श्रीमद्गह्वरभाषिता ॥ 181
16.m: It is threefold through immediate departure; and that must be performed by the guru when death is near: / such is the command of the Great Lord stated in the venerable Gahvara:

16.s:
dṛṣṭvā śiṣyaṃ jarāgrastaṃ vyādhinā paripīḍitam /
utkramayya tatastvenaṃ paratattve niyojayet // 182
16.d:
दृष्ट्वा शिष्यं जराग्रस्तं व्याधिना परिपीडितम् ।
उत्क्रमय्य ततस्त्वेनं परतत्त्वे नियोजयेत् ॥ 182
16.m: “Having seen a disciple seized by old age, tormented by disease, / having then caused him to depart, he should unite him with the supreme reality.”

16.s:
pañcatriṃśadamī bhedā gurorvā guruśiṣyayoḥ /
uktadvaividhyakalanātsaptatiḥ parikīrtitāḥ // 183
16.d:
पञ्चत्रिंशदमी भेदा गुरोर्वा गुरुशिष्ययोः ।
उक्तद्वैविध्यकलनात्सप्ततिः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 183
16.m: These varieties are thirty-five, belonging to the guru, or to the guru and disciple; / through taking into account the stated twofoldness, they are proclaimed as seventy.

16.s:
etairbhedaiḥ puroktāṃstānbhedāndīkṣāgatānguruḥ /
hatvā vadetprasaṃkhyānaṃ svabhyastajñānasiddhaye // 184
16.d:
एतैर्भेदैः पुरोक्तांस्तान्भेदान्दीक्षागतान्गुरुः ।
हत्वा वदेत्प्रसंख्यानं स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानसिद्धये ॥ 184
16.m: Multiplying those varieties belonging to initiation mentioned before by these varieties, / the guru should declare the total enumeration for the accomplishment of well-practiced knowledge.

16.s:
pañcāśītiśatī yā catvāriṃśatsamuttarā kathitā /
tāṃ saptatyā bhittvā dīkṣābhedānsvayaṃ kalayet // 185
16.d:
पञ्चाशीतिशती या चत्वारिंशत्समुत्तरा कथिता ।
तां सप्तत्या भित्त्वा दीक्षाभेदान्स्वयं कलयेत् ॥ 185
16.m: Dividing that eighty-five hundred plus forty which has been stated / by seventy, one should calculate by oneself the varieties of initiation:

16.s:
pañcakamiha lakṣāṇāṃ ca saptanavatiḥ sahasraparisaṃkhyā /
aṣṭau śatāni dīkṣābhedo'yaṃ mālinītantre // 186
16.d:
पञ्चकमिह लक्षाणां च सप्तनवतिः सहस्रपरिसंख्या ।
अष्टौ शतानि दीक्षाभेदोऽयं मालिनीतन्त्रे ॥ 186
16.m: here the enumeration is five hundred thousand / and ninety-seven thousand / eight hundred varieties of initiation in the Mālinītantra.

16.s:
saptatidhā śoddhṛgaṇastriṃśaddhā śodhya ekatattvādiḥ /
sāṇḍaḥ ṣaḍadhvarūpastathetikartavyatā caturbhedā // 187
16.d:
सप्ततिधा शोद्धृगणस्त्रिंशद्धा शोध्य एकतत्त्वादिः ।
साण्डः षडध्वरूपस्तथेतिकर्तव्यता चतुर्भेदा ॥ 187
16.m: The group of purifiers is seventyfold; what is to be purified, such as the single principle and the rest, / having cosmic eggs and having the form of the six paths, is thirtyfold; likewise the ritual procedure is of four varieties,

16.s:
dravyajñānamayī sā jananādivivarjitātha tadyuktā /
pañcatriṃśaddhā punareṣā bhogāpavargasandhānāt // 188
16.d:
द्रव्यज्ञानमयी सा जननादिविवर्जिताथ तद्युक्ता ।
पञ्चत्रिंशद्धा पुनरेषा भोगापवर्गसन्धानात् ॥ 188
16.m: consisting of substance and knowledge, devoid of [rites of] birth and the rest, or endowed with them; / and this is again thirty-five-fold through the intention of enjoyment and liberation,

16.s:
yasmāddvātriṃśaddhā bhogaḥ śubhaśuddhyaśuddhikālabhidā /
mokṣastredhā dviguṇā saptatiritikāryatābhedāḥ // 189
16.d:
यस्माद्द्वात्रिंशद्धा भोगः शुभशुद्ध्यशुद्धिकालभिदा ।
मोक्षस्त्रेधा द्विगुणा सप्ततिरितिकार्यताभेदाः ॥ 189
16.m: since enjoyment is thirty-two-fold through the division of purification of the auspicious, non-purification, and time; / liberation is threefold; doubled, the varieties of ritual procedure are seventy.

16.s:
śodhanaśodhyavibhedāditikartavyatvabhedataścaiṣā /
dīkṣā bahudhā bhinnā śodhyavihīnā tu saptatidhā // 190
16.d:
शोधनशोध्यविभेदादितिकर्तव्यत्वभेदतश्चैषा ।
दीक्षा बहुधा भिन्ना शोध्यविहीना तु सप्ततिधा ॥ 190
16.m: Through the division of purification and what is to be purified, and through the division of ritual procedure, / this initiation is divided into many ways; but devoid of what is to be purified, it is seventyfold.

16.s:
mantrāṇāṃ sakaletarasāṅganiraṅgādibhedasaṃkalanāt /
śyodhyasya ca tattvādeḥ pañcadaśādyuktabhedaparigaṇanāt // 191
16.d:
मन्त्राणां सकलेतरसाङ्गनिरङ्गादिभेदसंकलनात् ।
श्योध्यस्य च तत्त्वादेः पञ्चदशाद्युक्तभेदपरिगणनात् ॥ 191
16.m: Due to combining the distinctions of mantras into complete and otherwise, with limbs and without limbs, and so forth, / and due to calculating the stated divisions of what is to be purified, such as the principles, as fifteen and so forth,

16.s:
bhedānāṃ parigaṇanā na śakyate kartumityasaṃkīrṇāḥ /
bhedāḥ saṃkīrṇāḥ punaranye bhūyastvakāriṇo bahudhā // 192
16.d:
भेदानां परिगणना न शक्यते कर्तुमित्यसंकीर्णाः ।
भेदाः संकीर्णाः पुनरन्ये भूयस्त्वकारिणो बहुधा ॥ 192
16.m: an exhaustive calculation of the divisions cannot be made; thus unmixed varieties [have been stated]; / but other mixed varieties, producing multiplication, are manifold,

16.s:
śodhakaśodhyādīnāṃ dvitrādivibhedasadbhāvāt /
bhoge sādhye yadyadbahu kartavyaṃ tadāśrayenmatimān // 193
16.d:
शोधकशोध्यादीनां द्वित्रादिविभेदसद्भावात् ।
भोगे साध्ये यद्यद्बहु कर्तव्यं तदाश्रयेन्मतिमान् ॥ 193
16.m: because there exists division into two, three, and so on of the purifier, what is to be purified, and the rest. / Whatever manifold [rites] must be performed when enjoyment is to be attained, the wise man should adopt that.

16.s:
kāraṇabhūyastvaṃ kila phalabhūyastvāya kiṃ citram /
apavarge natu bhedastenāsminvāsanādṛḍhatvajuṣā // 194
16.d:
कारणभूयस्त्वं किल फलभूयस्त्वाय किं चित्रम् ।
अपवर्गे नतु भेदस्तेनास्मिन्वासनादृढत्वजुषा ॥ 194
16.m: A multiplicity of causes certainly leads to a multiplicity of fruits—what is strange about that? / But in liberation there is no division; therefore, in this matter, by one who relies on the firmness of latent impressions,

16.s:
alpāpyāśrayaṇīyā kriyātha vijñānamātre vā /
abhinavaguptaguruḥ punarāha hi sati vittadeśakālādau // 195
16.d:
अल्पाप्याश्रयणीया क्रियाथ विज्ञानमात्रे वा ।
अभिनवगुप्तगुरुः पुनराह हि सति वित्तदेशकालादौ ॥ 195
16.m: even a slight action is to be resorted to, or indeed pure knowledge alone. / But the teacher Abhinavagupta says: when wealth, place, time, and so forth are available,

16.s:
apavarge'pi hi vistīrṇakarmavijñānasaṃgrahaḥ kāryaḥ /
cidvṛttervaicitryāccāñcalye'pi krameṇa sandhānāt // 196
16.d:
अपवर्गेऽपि हि विस्तीर्णकर्मविज्ञानसंग्रहः कार्यः ।
चिद्वृत्तेर्वैचित्र्याच्चाञ्चल्येऽपि क्रमेण सन्धानात् ॥ 196
16.m: even in [the pursuit of] liberation, one should perform an extensive collection of rituals and forms of knowledge. / For, though the mind-function is fickle due to its variety, by connecting with it gradually,

16.s:
tasmiṃstasminvastuni rūḍhiravaśyaṃ śivātmikā bhavati /
tattvamidametadātmakametasmātproddhṛto mayā śiṣyaḥ // 197
16.d:
तस्मिंस्तस्मिन्वस्तुनि रूढिरवश्यं शिवात्मिका भवति ।
तत्त्वमिदमेतदात्मकमेतस्मात्प्रोद्धृतो मया शिष्यः ॥ 197
16.m: in each respective reality a firmly rooted state of Śiva's nature inevitably arises: / 'This is the principle; its nature is such; from this the disciple has been extracted by me.'

16.s:
itthaṃ kramasaṃvittau mūḍho'pi śivātmako bhavati /
kramikatathāvidhaśivatānugrahasubhagaṃ ca daiśikaṃ paśyan // 198
16.d:
इत्थं क्रमसंवित्तौ मूढोऽपि शिवात्मको भवति ।
क्रमिकतथाविधशिवतानुग्रहसुभगं च दैशिकं पश्यन् ॥ 198
16.m: In this way, when there is successive consciousness, even a foolish person comes to share the nature of Śiva, / and seeing the teacher graced by the gradual transmission of that kind of Śiva-nature,

16.s:
śiśurapi tadabhedadṛśā bhaktibalāccābhyupaiti śivabhāvam /
yadyapi vikalpavṛtterapi mokṣaṃ dīkṣayaiva dehānte // 199
16.d:
शिशुरपि तदभेददृशा भक्तिबलाच्चाभ्युपैति शिवभावम् ।
यद्यपि विकल्पवृत्तेरपि मोक्षं दीक्षयैव देहान्ते ॥ 199
16.m: even a novice, by virtue of devotion and by seeing non-difference from him, attains the state of Śiva. / Although the Lord declared in the scripture that liberation occurs through initiation alone at the end of the body, even for one with conceptual mind-functions,

16.s:
śāstre provāca vibhustathāpi dṛḍhavāsanā yuktā /
mokṣe'pyasti viśeṣaḥ kriyālpabhūyastvajaḥ salokādiḥ // 200
16.d:
शास्त्रे प्रोवाच विभुस्तथापि दृढवासना युक्ता ।
मोक्षेऽप्यस्ति विशेषः क्रियाल्पभूयस्त्वजः सलोकादिः ॥ 200
16.m: nevertheless, a firm latent impression is appropriate. / Some say: 'Even in liberation there is a distinction born of the paucity or multiplicity of action, such as residing in the same realm (salokatā) and so on.'

16.s:
iti kecittadayuktaṃ sa vicitro bhoga eva kathitaḥ syāt /
saṃskāraśeṣavartanajīvitamadhye'sya samayalopādyam // 201
16.d:
इति केचित्तदयुक्तं स विचित्रो भोग एव कथितः स्यात् ।
संस्कारशेषवर्तनजीवितमध्येऽस्य समयलोपाद्यम् ॥ 201
16.m: That is incorrect; for that would merely be described as varied enjoyment. / During life sustained by the remainder of past karmic traces, the network of obstacles such as transgression of the rule does not arise for him—

16.s:
nāyāti vighnajālaṃ kriyābahutvaṃ mumukṣostat /
yasmāt sabījadīkṣāsaṃskṛtapuruṣasya samayalopādye // 202
16.d:
नायाति विघ्नजालं क्रियाबहुत्वं मुमुक्षोस्तत् ।
यस्मात् सबीजदीक्षासंस्कृतपुरुषस्य समयलोपाद्ये ॥ 202
16.m: that is why an abundance of action is prescribed for one desiring liberation. / Because for a person consecrated by initiation with seeds (sabījadīkṣā), when transgression of the rule and the like occurs,

16.s:
bhukte bhogānmokṣo naivaṃ nirbījadīkṣāyām /
iti kecinmanyante yuktaṃ taccāpi yatsmṛtaṃ śāstre // 203
16.d:
भुक्ते भोगान्मोक्षो नैवं निर्बीजदीक्षायाम् ।
इति केचिन्मन्यन्ते युक्तं तच्चापि यत्स्मृतं शास्त्रे ॥ 203
16.m: liberation occurs only after enjoyments have been experienced, but not so in initiation without seeds (nirbījadīkṣā). / Some hold this view; and that is also appropriate, since it is stated in scripture:

16.s: samayollaṅghanāddevi kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ // 204
16.d: समयोल्लङ्घनाद्देवि क्रव्यादत्वं शतं समाः ॥ 204
16.m: 'From transgressing the rule, O goddess, one becomes a flesh-eater for a hundred years.'

16.s:
tasmāduruśiṣyamatau śivabhāvanirūḍhivitaraṇasamartham /
kramikaṃ tattvoddharaṇādi karma mokṣe'pi yuktamativitatam // 205
16.d:
तस्मादुरुशिष्यमतौ शिवभावनिरूढिवितरणसमर्थम् ।
क्रमिकं तत्त्वोद्धरणादि कर्म मोक्षेऽपि युक्तमतिविततम् ॥ 205
16.m: Therefore, according to the great disciples, an extensive, step-by-step ritual, such as the extraction of principles, capable of bestowing a firm rootedness in the state of Śiva, is appropriate even for liberation.

16.s:
yastu sadā bhāvanayā svabhyastajñānavānguruḥ sa śiśoḥ /
apavargāya yathecchaṃ yaṃ kaṃcidupāyamanutiṣṭhet // 206
16.d:
यस्तु सदा भावनया स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानवान्गुरुः स शिशोः ।
अपवर्गाय यथेच्छं यं कंचिदुपायमनुतिष्ठेत् ॥ 206
16.m: However, that guru who possesses knowledge well-practiced through constant contemplation / may employ any means whatsoever at will for the liberation of the novice.

16.s:
evaṃ śiṣyatanau śodhyaṃ nyasyādhvānaṃ yathepsitam /
śodhakaṃ mantramupari nyasyettattvānusārataḥ // 207
16.d:
एवं शिष्यतनौ शोध्यं न्यस्याध्वानं यथेप्सितम् ।
शोधकं मन्त्रमुपरि न्यस्येत्तत्त्वानुसारतः ॥ 207
16.m: Thus, having imposed the path to be purified onto the disciple's body as desired, / he should impose the purifying mantra above it in accordance with the principles.

16.s:
dvayormātṛkayostattvasthityā varṇakramaḥ purā /
kathitastaṃ tathā nyasyettattattattvaviśuddhaye // 208
16.d:
द्वयोर्मातृकयोस्तत्त्वस्थित्या वर्णक्रमः पुरा ।
कथितस्तं तथा न्यस्येत्तत्तत्तत्त्वविशुद्धये ॥ 208
16.m: The sequence of phonemes for the two phoneme-matrices according to the status of the principles was stated previously; / he should impose that in the same manner for the purification of each respective principle.

16.s:
varṇādhvā yadyapi proktaḥ śodhyaḥ pāśātmakastu saḥ /
māyīyaḥ śodhakastvanyaḥ śivātmā paravāṅmayaḥ // 209
16.d:
वर्णाध्वा यद्यपि प्रोक्तः शोध्यः पाशात्मकस्तु सः ।
मायीयः शोधकस्त्वन्यः शिवात्मा परवाङ्मयः ॥ 209
16.m: Although the phoneme-path is spoken of as the object of purification, it consists of bondage, / being of the nature of Māyā; whereas the purifier is different: it shares the nature of Śiva and consists of supreme speech.

16.s:
uvāca sadyojyotiśca vṛttau svāyambhuvasya tat /
bāḍhameko hi pāśātmā śabdo'nyaśca śivātmakaḥ // 210
16.d:
उवाच सद्योज्योतिश्च वृत्तौ स्वायम्भुवस्य तत् ।
बाढमेको हि पाशात्मा शब्दोऽन्यश्च शिवात्मकः ॥ 210
16.m: And Sadyojyotis said in his commentary on the Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṅgraha: / 'Indeed, one kind of sound consists of bondage, and the other shares the nature of Śiva.'

16.s:
tasmāttasyaiva varṇasya yuktā śodhakaśodhyatā /
śrīpūrvaśāstre cāpyuktaṃ te tairāliṅgitā iti // 211
16.d:
