तस्मात्तस्यैव वर्णस्य युक्ता शोधकशोध्यता ।
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे चाप्युक्तं ते तैरालिङ्गिता इति ॥ 211
16.m: Therefore, it is appropriate that this very phoneme is both purifier and object of purification. / And in the Śrīpūrva scripture it is also said: 'They are embraced by them.'

16.s:
sadyojātādivaktrāṇi hṛdādyaṅgāni pañca ca /
ṣaṭkṛtvo nyasya ṣaṭtriṃśannyāsaṃ kuryāddharāditaḥ // 212
16.d:
सद्योजातादिवक्त्राणि हृदाद्यङ्गानि पञ्च च ।
षट्कृत्वो न्यस्य षट्त्रिंशन्न्यासं कुर्याद्धरादितः ॥ 212
16.m: Having imposed the faces such as Sadyojāta and the five limbs such as the heart six times, / one should perform the thirty-six-fold imposition beginning with earth.

16.s:
parāparāyā vailomyāddharāyāṃ syātpadatrayam /
tato jalādahaṅkāre pañcāṣṭakasamāśrayāt // 213
16.d:
परापराया वैलोम्याद्धरायां स्यात्पदत्रयम् ।
ततो जलादहङ्कारे पञ्चाष्टकसमाश्रयात् ॥ 213
16.m: In reverse order of Parāparā, there should be three words on earth; / then, from water up to egoity, by relying on five sets of eight,

16.s:
padāni pañca dhīmūlapuṃrāgākhye traye trayam /
ekaṃ tvaśuddhavitkāladvaye caikaṃ niyāmake // 214
16.d:
पदानि पञ्च धीमूलपुंरागाख्ये त्रये त्रयम् ।
एकं त्वशुद्धवित्कालद्वये चैकं नियामके ॥ 214
16.m: there are five words; three on the triad named intellect, root-nature, and soul; / one on the pair of impure knowing and time; and one on the regulator (niyati);

16.s:
kalāmāyādvaye caikaṃ padamuktamiha kramāt /
vidyeśvarasadāśaktiśiveṣu padapañcakam // 215
16.d:
कलामायाद्वये चैकं पदमुक्तमिह क्रमात् ।
विद्येश्वरसदाशक्तिशिवेषु पदपञ्चकम् ॥ 215
16.m: one word is taught here successively on the pair of limited agency and Māyā; / five words on knowledge, Lord, Sadāśiva, Śakti, and Śiva.

16.s:
ekonaviṃśatiḥ seyaṃ padānāṃ syātparāparā /
sārdhaṃ caikaṃ caikaṃ sārdhaṃ dve dve śaśī dṛgatha yugmam // 216
16.d:
एकोनविंशतिः सेयं पदानां स्यात्परापरा ।
सार्धं चैकं चैकं सार्धं द्वे द्वे शशी दृगथ युग्मम् ॥ 216
16.m: This constitutes nineteen words of Parāparā: / one and a half, one, one, one and a half, two, two, one, two, and then a pair,

16.s:
trāṇi dṛgabdhiścandraḥ śrutiḥ śaśī pañca vidhumahaścandrāḥ /
ekānnaviṃśatau syādakṣarasaṃkhyā padeṣviyaṃ devyāḥ // 217
16.d:
त्राणि दृगब्धिश्चन्द्रः श्रुतिः शशी पञ्च विधुमहश्चन्द्राः ।
एकान्नविंशतौ स्यादक्षरसंख्या पदेष्वियं देव्याः ॥ 217
16.m: three, two, four, one, four, one, five, one, one, and one: / this should be the count of syllables in the nineteen words of the goddess,

16.s:
haldvayayutavasucitraguparisaṃkhyātasvavarṇāyāḥ /
mūlāntaṃ sārdhavarṇaṃ syānmāyāntaṃ varṇamekakam // 218
16.d:
हल्द्वययुतवसुचित्रगुपरिसंख्यातस्ववर्णायाः ।
मूलान्तं सार्धवर्णं स्यान्मायान्तं वर्णमेककम् ॥ 218
16.m: whose own phonemes are counted as twenty-seven plus two consonants. / Up to the root-nature there is one and a half phonemes; up to Māyā there is one phoneme;

16.s:
śaktyantamekamaparānyāse vidhirudīritaḥ /
māyāntaṃ haltataḥ śaktiparyante svara ucyate // 219
16.d:
शक्त्यन्तमेकमपरान्यासे विधिरुदीरितः ।
मायान्तं हल्ततः शक्तिपर्यन्ते स्वर उच्यते ॥ 219
16.m: up to Śakti there is one—this rule is stated in the imposition of Aparā. / Up to Māyā is a consonant; thereafter, up to Śakti, a vowel is prescribed.

16.s:
niṣkale śivatattve vai paro nyāsaḥ paroditaḥ /
parāparāpadānyeva hyaghoryādyaṣṭakadvaye // 220
16.d:
निष्कले शिवतत्त्वे वै परो न्यासः परोदितः ।
परापरापदान्येव ह्यघोर्याद्यष्टकद्वये ॥ 220
16.m: In the partless Śiva-principle, the supreme imposition is taught as supreme. / Indeed, the words of Parāparā are in the two sets of eight beginning with Aghorī;

16.s:
mantrāstadanusāreṇa tattveṣvetaddvayaṃ kṣipet /
piṇḍākṣarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ varṇasaṃkhyā vibhedataḥ // 221
16.d:
मन्त्रास्तदनुसारेण तत्त्वेष्वेतद्द्वयं क्षिपेत् ।
पिण्डाक्षराणां सर्वेषां वर्णसंख्या विभेदतः ॥ 221
16.m: the mantras are according to them; one should cast these two upon the principles. / Due to the differentiation of the phonemic count of all composite syllables,

16.s:
avyaktāntaṃ svare nyasyā śeṣaṃ śeṣeṣu yojayet /
bījāni sarvatattveṣu vyāptṛtvena prakalpayet // 222
16.d:
अव्यक्तान्तं स्वरे न्यस्या शेषं शेषेषु योजयेत् ।
बीजानि सर्वतत्त्वेषु व्याप्तृत्वेन प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 222
16.m: the portion up to the unmanifest is to be imposed on the vowel, and the remainder should be applied to the remaining [principles]. / One should assign the seed-syllables as pervadors throughout all the principles.

16.s:
piṇḍānāṃ bījavannyāsamanye tu pratipedire /
akṛte vātha śodhyasya nyāse vastubalāt sthiteḥ // 223
16.d:
पिण्डानां बीजवन्न्यासमन्ये तु प्रतिपेदिरे ।
अकृते वाथ शोध्यस्य न्यासे वस्तुबलात् स्थितेः ॥ 223
16.m: Others, however, have accepted the imposition of composite syllables like seed-syllables. / Or even if the imposition of the object to be purified is not performed, since it is established by the force of reality,

16.s:
śodhakanyāsamātreṇa sarvaṃ śodhyaṃ viśudhyati /
śrīmanmṛtyuñjayādau ca kathitaṃ parameṣṭhinā // 224
16.d:
शोधकन्यासमात्रेण सर्वं शोध्यं विशुध्यति ।
श्रीमन्मृत्युञ्जयादौ च कथितं परमेष्ठिना ॥ 224
16.m: everything to be purified is purified merely by the imposition of the purifier. / And in the Śrīmanmṛtyuñjaya and other scriptures, the supreme Lord has declared:

16.s:
adhunā nyāsamātreṇa bhūtaśuddhiḥ prajāyate /
dehaśuddhyarthamapyetattulyametena vastutaḥ // 225
16.d:
अधुना न्यासमात्रेण भूतशुद्धिः प्रजायते ।
देहशुद्ध्यर्थमप्येतत्तुल्यमेतेन वस्तुतः ॥ 225
16.m: 'Purification of the elements is brought about instantly merely by the imposition.' / For the purpose of purifying the body, this is also identical to that in reality.

16.s:
anyaprakaraṇoktaṃ yadyuktaṃ prakaraṇāntare /
jñāpakatvena sākṣādvā tatkiṃ nānyatra gṛhyate // 226
16.d:
अन्यप्रकरणोक्तं यद्युक्तं प्रकरणान्तरे ।
ज्ञापकत्वेन साक्षाद्वा तत्किं नान्यत्र गृह्यते ॥ 226
16.m: What is stated in another section, if it is appropriate in this section / as an indicator or directly, why is it not accepted elsewhere?

16.s:
mālinīmātṛkāṅgasya nyāso yo'rcāvidhau purā /
proktaḥ kevalasaṃśoddhṛmantranyāse sa eva tu // 227
16.d:
मालिनीमातृकाङ्गस्य न्यासो योऽर्चाविधौ पुरा ।
प्रोक्तः केवलसंशोद्धृमन्त्रन्यासे स एव तु ॥ 227
16.m: The imposition of the limbs of the Mālinī and Mātṛkā which was taught previously in the ritual of worship / is the very same in the imposition of the purifying mantras alone.

16.s:
tripadī dvayordvayoḥ syātpratyekamathāṣṭasu śrutipadāni /
dikcandracandrarasaraviśaraśaradṛgdṛṅmṛgāṅkaśaśigaṇane // 228
16.d:
त्रिपदी द्वयोर्द्वयोः स्यात्प्रत्येकमथाष्टसु श्रुतिपदानि ।
दिक्चन्द्रचन्द्ररसरविशरशरदृग्दृङ्मृगाङ्कशशिगणने ॥ 228
16.m: There should be three words each for two [principles], then four words for eight [principles], / in the count of ten, one, one, six, twelve, five, five, two, two, one, and one,

16.s:
aṅgulamāne devyā aṣṭādaśa vaibhavena padamanyat /
aparaṃ mānamidaṃ syāt kevalaśodhakamanunyāse // 229
16.d:
अङ्गुलमाने देव्या अष्टादश वैभवेन पदमन्यत् ।
अपरं मानमिदं स्यात् केवलशोधकमनुन्यासे ॥ 229
16.m: in the digit-measure of the goddess; by expansion, there is another word of eighteen [digits]. / This should be another measure in the imposition of the mantra of the purifier alone.

16.s:
turyapadātpadaṣaṭke mānadvitayaṃ parāparaparākhyam /
dvādaśakaṃ dvādaśakaṃ tattvopari pūrvavattvanyat // 230
16.d:
तुर्यपदात्पदषट्के मानद्वितयं परापरपराख्यम् ।
द्वादशकं द्वादशकं तत्त्वोपरि पूर्ववत्त्वन्यत् ॥ 230
16.m: From the fourth word, across a group of six words, there are two measures known as Parāparā and Parā: / twelve [digits] and twelve [digits]; upon the principle, the other is as before.

16.s:
kevalaśodhakamantranyāsābhiprāyato mahādevaḥ /
tattvakramoditamapi nyāsaṃ punarāha tadviruddhamapi // 231
16.d:
केवलशोधकमन्त्रन्यासाभिप्रायतो महादेवः ।
तत्त्वक्रमोदितमपि न्यासं पुनराह तद्विरुद्धमपि ॥ 231
16.m: With the intention of the imposition of the purifying mantra alone, Mahādeva / taught an imposition according to the sequence of principles, and again one that even contradicts it.

16.s:
niṣkale padamekārṇaṃ yāvattrīṇi tu pārthive /
ityādinā tattvagatakramanyāsa udīritaḥ // 232
16.d:
निष्कले पदमेकार्णं यावत्त्रीणि तु पार्थिवे ।
इत्यादिना तत्त्वगतक्रमन्यास उदीरितः ॥ 232
16.m: Beginning with 'In the partless [Śiva] there is one word of one syllable, up to three in the earthly,' / the imposition according to the order situated in the principles has been declared.

16.s:
punaśca mālinītantre vargavidyāvibhedataḥ /
dvidhā padānītyuktvākhyannyāsamanyādṛśaṃ vibhuḥ // 233
16.d:
पुनश्च मालिनीतन्त्रे वर्गविद्याविभेदतः ।
द्विधा पदानीत्युक्त्वाख्यन्न्यासमन्यादृशं विभुः ॥ 233
16.m: And again in the Mālinītantra, having stated that words are of two kinds / according to the division of class-phonemes (varga) and mantra-phonemes (vidyā), the Lord taught a different kind of imposition:

16.s:
ekaikaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ tatra pūrvaṃ padatrayam /
aṣṭāṅgulāni catvāri daśāṅgulamataḥ param // 234
16.d:
एकैकं द्व्यङ्गुलं ज्ञेयं तत्र पूर्वं पदत्रयम् ।
अष्टाङ्गुलानि चत्वारि दशाङ्गुलमतः परम् ॥ 234
16.m: 'There, the first three words should each be known as measuring two digits; / four words of eight digits; after that, one of ten digits;

16.s:
dvyaṅgule dve pade cānye ṣaḍaṅgulamataḥ param /
dvādaśāṅgulamanyacca dve'nye pañcāṅgule pṛthak // 235
16.d:
द्व्यङ्गुले द्वे पदे चान्ये षडङ्गुलमतः परम् ।
द्वादशाङ्गुलमन्यच्च द्वेऽन्ये पञ्चाङ्गुले पृथक् ॥ 235
16.m: two other words of two digits; after that, one of six digits; / another of twelve digits; two others of five digits individually;

16.s:
padadvayaṃ catuṣparva tathānye dve dviparvaṇī /
evaṃ parāparādevyāḥ svatantro nyāsa ucyate // 236
16.d:
पदद्वयं चतुष्पर्व तथान्ये द्वे द्विपर्वणी ।
एवं परापरादेव्याः स्वतन्त्रो न्यास उच्यते ॥ 236
16.m: two words of four finger-joints, and two others of two finger-joints.' / Thus the independent imposition of the goddess Parāparā is taught.

16.s:
vidyādvayaṃ śiṣyatanau vyāptṛtvenaiva yojayet /
iti darśayituṃ nāsya pṛthaṅnyāsaṃ nyarūpayat // 237
16.d:
विद्याद्वयं शिष्यतनौ व्याप्तृत्वेनैव योजयेत् ।
इति दर्शयितुं नास्य पृथङ्न्यासं न्यरूपयत् ॥ 237
16.m: One should apply the two vidyās onto the disciple's body solely as pervadors; / to demonstrate this, he did not set forth a separate imposition for it.

16.s:
evaṃ śodhakamantrasya nyāse tadraśmiyogataḥ /
pāśajālaṃ vilīyeta taddhyānabalato guroḥ // 238
16.d:
एवं शोधकमन्त्रस्य न्यासे तद्रश्मियोगतः ।
पाशजालं विलीयेत तद्ध्यानबलतो गुरोः ॥ 238
16.m: Thus, when the purifying mantra is imposed, through the union of its rays, / the snare's net dissolves by the power of the guru's meditation upon it.

16.s:
śodhyatattve samastānāṃ yonīnāṃ tulyakālataḥ /
jananādbhogataḥ karmakṣaye syādapavṛktatā // 239
16.d:
शोध्यतत्त्वे समस्तानां योनीनां तुल्यकालतः ।
जननाद्भोगतः कर्मक्षये स्यादपवृक्तता ॥ 239
16.m: In the category being purified, by the simultaneous experiencing / of births in all wombs, liberation occurs upon the destruction of karma.

16.s:
dehaistāvadbhirasyāṇościtraṃ bhokturapi sphuṭam /
mano'nusandhirno viśvasaṃyogapravibhāgavat // 240
16.d:
देहैस्तावद्भिरस्याणोश्चित्रं भोक्तुरपि स्फुटम् ।
मनोऽनुसन्धिर्नो विश्वसंयोगप्रविभागवत् ॥ 240
16.m: Though this individual soul experiences through so many diverse bodies, / clearly there is no synthesis of the mind, just as in the conjunction and disjunction of the universe.

16.s:
niyatyā manaso dehamātre vṛttistataḥ param /
nānusandhā yataḥ saikasvāntayuktākṣakalpitā // 241
16.d:
नियत्या मनसो देहमात्रे वृत्तिस्ततः परम् ।
नानुसन्धा यतः सैकस्वान्तयुक्ताक्षकल्पिता ॥ 241
16.m: Because of limitation (niyati), the mental function is restricted to that body alone; beyond that / there is no synthesis, because it is formed by senses conjoined with a single internal organ.

16.s:
pradeśavṛtti ca jñānamātmanastatra tatra tat /
bhogyajñānaṃ nānyadeheṣvanusandhānamarhati // 242
16.d:
प्रदेशवृत्ति च ज्ञानमात्मनस्तत्र तत्र तत् ।
भोग्यज्ञानं नान्यदेहेष्वनुसन्धानमर्हति ॥ 242
16.m: Moreover, the self's knowledge operates only locally; in each instance, that / cognition of objects cannot achieve synthesis across other bodies.

16.s:
yadā tu manasastasya dehavṛtterapi dhruvam /
yogamantrakriyādeḥ syādvaimalyaṃ tadvidā tadā // 243
16.d:
यदा तु मनसस्तस्य देहवृत्तेरपि ध्रुवम् ।
योगमन्त्रक्रियादेः स्याद्वैमल्यं तद्विदा तदा ॥ 243
16.m: When, however, that very mind, even in its bodily function, surely / achieves purity through yoga, mantra, ritual, and the like, then, by one who knows that,

16.s:
yathāmalaṃ mano dūrasthitamapyāśu paśyati /
tathā pratyayadīkṣāyāṃ tattadbhuvanadarśanam // 244
16.d:
यथामलं मनो दूरस्थितमप्याशु पश्यति ।
तथा प्रत्ययदीक्षायां तत्तद्भुवनदर्शनम् ॥ 244
16.m: just as the pure mind quickly sees even what is stationed far away, / so too in the initiation of verification there is vision of those respective worlds.

16.s:
jananādiviyuktāṃ tu yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣati /
tadāsmāduddharāmīti yuktamūhaprakalpanam // 245
16.d:
जननादिवियुक्तां तु यदा दीक्षां चिकीर्षति ।
तदास्मादुद्धरामीति युक्तमूहप्रकल्पनम् ॥ 245
16.m: When, however, one wishes to perform an initiation devoid of birth and the rest, / then it is fitting to apply reasoning: 'I extract [the soul] from this [reality].'

16.s:
yadā śodhyaṃ vinā śoddhṛnyāsastatrāpi mantrataḥ /
jananādikramaṃ kuryāttattvasaṃśleṣavarjitam // 246
16.d:
यदा शोध्यं विना शोद्धृन्यासस्तत्रापि मन्त्रतः ।
जननादिक्रमं कुर्यात्तत्त्वसंश्लेषवर्जितम् ॥ 246
16.m: When the imposition of the purifier is performed without the [tattva] to be purified, even then through the mantra / one should perform the sequence of birth and the rest, free from conjunction with the tattvas.

16.s:
ekākiśoddhṛnyāse ca jananādivivarjane /
tacchoddhṛsaṃpuṭaṃ nāma kevalaṃ parikalpayet // 247
16.d:
एकाकिशोद्धृन्यासे च जननादिविवर्जने ।
तच्छोद्धृसंपुटं नाम केवलं परिकल्पयेत् ॥ 247
16.m: And in the solitary imposition of the purifier, when birth and the rest are excluded, / one should mentally construct only the enfolding (saṃpuṭa) of that purifier with the name.

16.s:
dravyayogena dīkṣāyāṃ tilājyākṣatataṇḍulam /
tattanmantreṇa juhuyājjanmayogaviyogayoḥ // 248
16.d:
द्रव्ययोगेन दीक्षायां तिलाज्याक्षततण्डुलम् ।
तत्तन्मन्त्रेण जुहुयाज्जन्मयोगवियोगयोः ॥ 248
16.m: In initiation performed with substances, one should offer sesame, ghee, unbroken grains, and husked rice / with the respective mantras for the conjunction and disjunction of birth.

16.s:
yadā vijñānadīkṣāṃ tu kuryācchiṣyaṃ tadā bhṛśam /
tanmantrasaṃjalpabalāt paśyedā cāvikalpakāt // 249
16.d:
यदा विज्ञानदीक्षां तु कुर्याच्छिष्यं तदा भृशम् ।
तन्मन्त्रसंजल्पबलात् पश्येदा चाविकल्पकात् ॥ 249
16.m: When, however, one performs the initiation through knowledge, then one should intensely / behold the disciple by the force of discursive repetition of that mantra, right up to the non-conceptual.

16.s:
vikalpaḥ kila saṃjalpamayo yatsa vimarśakaḥ /
mantrātmāsau vimarśaśca śuddho'pāśavatātmakaḥ // 250
16.d:
विकल्पः किल संजल्पमयो यत्स विमर्शकः ।
मन्त्रात्मासौ विमर्शश्च शुद्धोऽपाशवतात्मकः ॥ 250
16.m: For a conceptual construct consists of discursive speech because it is reflective awareness; / and this reflective awareness is mantra itself, pure and free from snares.

16.s:
nityaścānādivaradaśivābhedopakalpitaḥ /
tadyogāddaiśikasyāpi vikalpaḥ śivatāṃ vrajet // 251
16.d:
नित्यश्चानादिवरदशिवाभेदोपकल्पितः ।
तद्योगाद्दैशिकस्यापि विकल्पः शिवतां व्रजेत् ॥ 251
16.m: It is eternal, established as non-different from Śiva, the eternal giver of boons; / through union with it, the conceptual construct of the teacher too reaches the state of Śiva.

16.s:
śrīsāraśāstre tadidaṃ parameśena bhāṣitam /
arthasya pratipattiryā grāhyagrāhakarūpiṇī // 252
16.d:
श्रीसारशास्त्रे तदिदं परमेशेन भाषितम् ।
अर्थस्य प्रतिपत्तिर्या ग्राह्यग्राहकरूपिणी ॥ 252
16.m: This very thing was spoken by the Supreme Lord in the holy Sāraśāstra: / 'That comprehension of an object which takes the form of object and subject,

16.s:
sā eva mantraśaktistu vitatā mantrasantatau /
parāmarśasvabhāvetthaṃ mantraśaktirudāhṛtā // 253
16.d:
सा एव मन्त्रशक्तिस्तु वितता मन्त्रसन्ततौ ।
परामर्शस्वभावेत्थं मन्त्रशक्तिरुदाहृता ॥ 253
16.m: that alone is the mantra-power extended throughout the continuous series of mantras.' / Thus the mantra-power is declared to have the nature of reflective awareness.

16.s:
parāmarśo dvidhā śuddhāśuddhatvānmantrabhedakaḥ /
uktaṃ śrīpauṣkare'nye ca brahmaviṣṇvādayo'ṇḍagāḥ // 254
16.d:
परामर्शो द्विधा शुद्धाशुद्धत्वान्मन्त्रभेदकः ।
उक्तं श्रीपौष्करेऽन्ये च ब्रह्मविष्ण्वादयोऽण्डगाः ॥ 254
16.m: Reflective awareness is twofold, differentiating mantras through purity and impurity. / It is stated in the holy Pauṣkara: 'The others, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the rest residing in the Egg,

16.s:
prādhānikāḥ sāñjanāste sāttvarājasatāmasāḥ /
tairaśuddhaparāmarśāttanmayībhāvito guruḥ // 255
16.d:
प्राधानिकाः साञ्जनास्ते सात्त्वराजसतामसाः ।
तैरशुद्धपरामर्शात्तन्मयीभावितो गुरुः ॥ 255
16.m: belong to Prakṛti, possess stain, and are composed of sattva, rajas, and tamas; / through impure reflective awareness of them, a guru who has become identified with them,

16.s:
vaiṣṇavādiḥ paśuḥ prokto na yogyaḥ patiśāsane /
ye mantrāḥ śuddhamārgasthāḥ śivabhaṭṭārakādayaḥ // 256
16.d:
वैष्णवादिः पशुः प्रोक्तो न योग्यः पतिशासने ।
ये मन्त्राः शुद्धमार्गस्थाः शिवभट्टारकादयः ॥ 256
16.m: such as a Vaiṣṇava, is declared a bound soul and is unfit in the teaching of the Lord.' / Those mantras that abide in the pure path, such as venerable Śiva and the rest,

16.s:
śrīmanmataṅgādidṛśā tanmayo hi guruḥ śivaḥ /
nanu svatantrasaṃjalpayogādastu vimarśitā // 257
16.d:
श्रीमन्मतङ्गादिदृशा तन्मयो हि गुरुः शिवः ।
ननु स्वतन्त्रसंजल्पयोगादस्तु विमर्शिता ॥ 257
16.m: according to the perspective of the venerable Mataṅga and others, the guru identified with them is truly Śiva. / [Objection:] Now, let reflective awareness arise from union with independent speech;

16.s:
prākkutaḥ sa vimarśāccetkutaḥ so'pi nirūpaṇe /
ādyastathāvikalpatvapradaḥ syādupadeṣṭṛtaḥ // 258
16.d:
प्राक्कुतः स विमर्शाच्चेत्कुतः सोऽपि निरूपणे ।
आद्यस्तथाविकल्पत्वप्रदः स्यादुपदेष्टृतः ॥ 258
16.m: whence came that [speech] before? If you say it arose from reflective awareness, whence came that too on examination? / [Reply:] The first, which grants such non-conceptuality, arises from the instructor.

16.s:
yaḥ saṃkrānto'bhijalpaḥ syāttasyāpyanyopadeṣṭṛtaḥ /
pūrvapūrvakramāditthaṃ ya evādiguroḥ purā // 259
16.d:
यः संक्रान्तोऽभिजल्पः स्यात्तस्याप्यन्योपदेष्टृतः ।
पूर्वपूर्वक्रमादित्थं य एवादिगुरोः पुरा ॥ 259
16.m: The speech that was transmitted to him also came from another instructor, / and thus, through the preceding sequence, it should be grasped that whatever discursive speech was transmitted

16.s:
saṃjalpo hyabhisaṃkrāntaḥ so'dyāpyastīti gṛhyatām /
yastathāvidhasaṃjalpabalātko'pi svatantrakaḥ // 260
16.d:
संजल्पो ह्यभिसंक्रान्तः सोऽद्याप्यस्तीति गृह्यताम् ।
यस्तथाविधसंजल्पबलात्कोऽपि स्वतन्त्रकः ॥ 260
16.m: from the primordial guru of old exists even today. / Whatever independent reflective awareness

16.s:
vimarśaḥ kalpyate so'pi tadātmaiva suniścitaḥ /
ghaṭakumbha itītthaṃ vā yadi bhedo nirūpyate // 261
16.d:
विमर्शः कल्प्यते सोऽपि तदात्मैव सुनिश्चितः ।
घटकुम्भ इतीत्थं वा यदि भेदो निरूप्यते ॥ 261
16.m: is conceived through the power of such discursive speech is definitely identical with that. / Or if a difference is posited, like between 'ghaṭa' and 'kumbha' (pot and pitcher),

16.s:
so'pyanyakalpanādāyī hyanādṛtyaḥ prayatnataḥ /
paṇāyate karotīti vikalpasyocitau sphuṭam // 262
16.d:
सोऽप्यन्यकल्पनादायी ह्यनादृत्यः प्रयत्नतः ।
पणायते करोतीति विकल्पस्योचितौ स्फुटम् ॥ 262
16.m: that too entails assuming something else and must be carefully disregarded; / for when they are appropriate to the conceptual construct, 'paṇāyate' (he trades) and 'karoti' (he makes)

16.s:
karapāṇyabhijalpau tau saṃkīryetāṃ kathaṃ kila /
śabdācchabdāntare tena vyutpattirvyavadhānataḥ // 263
16.d:
करपाण्यभिजल्पौ तौ संकीर्येतां कथं किल ।
शब्दाच्छब्दान्तरे तेन व्युत्पत्तिर्व्यवधानतः ॥ 263
16.m: are evident: how indeed could the verbal expressions for hand, such as 'kara' and 'pāṇi', become confused? / Therefore, comprehension from one word to another occurs through an intermediary;

16.s:
vyavahārāttu sā sākṣāccitropākhyāvimarśinī /
tadvimarśodayaḥ prācyasvavimarśamayaḥ sphuret // 264
16.d:
व्यवहारात्तु सा साक्षाच्चित्रोपाख्याविमर्शिनी ।
तद्विमर्शोदयः प्राच्यस्वविमर्शमयः स्फुरेत् ॥ 264
16.m: but from ordinary practice, it directly reflects various names. / The arising of that reflective awareness shines forth consisting of one's own prior reflective awareness,

16.s:
yāvadbālasya saṃvittirakṛtrimavimarśane /
tena tanmantraśabdārthaviśeṣotthaṃ vikalpanam // 265
16.d:
यावद्बालस्य संवित्तिरकृत्रिमविमर्शने ।
तेन तन्मन्त्रशब्दार्थविशेषोत्थं विकल्पनम् ॥ 265
16.m: which extends back to an infant's consciousness in innate reflective awareness. / Therefore, the conceptual construct arising from the specific word-meaning of that mantra,

16.s:
śabdāntarotthādbhedena paśyatā mantra ādṛtaḥ /
yaccāpi bījapiṇḍāderuktaṃ prāgbodharūpakam // 266
16.d:
शब्दान्तरोत्थाद्भेदेन पश्यता मन्त्र आदृतः ।
यच्चापि बीजपिण्डादेरुक्तं प्राग्बोधरूपकम् ॥ 266
16.m: seen as distinct from what arises from another word, is honoured as the mantra. / And that which was previously said to have the nature of consciousness with respect to seed-syllables, masses, and the like,

16.s:
tattasyaiva kuto'nyasya tatkasmādanyakalpanā /
etadarthaṃ guroryatnāllakṣaṇe tatra tatra tat // 267
16.d:
तत्तस्यैव कुतोऽन्यस्य तत्कस्मादन्यकल्पना ।
एतदर्थं गुरोर्यत्नाल्लक्षणे तत्र तत्र तत् ॥ 267
16.m: belongs to that alone; whence could it belong to another? Why then assume something else? / For this reason, in the definition of a guru, that definition has been carefully stated here and there:

16.s:
lakṣaṇaṃ kathitaṃ hyeṣa mantratantraviśāradaḥ /
tena mantrārthasaṃbodhe mantravārtikamādarāt // 268
16.d:
लक्षणं कथितं ह्येष मन्त्रतन्त्रविशारदः ।
तेन मन्त्रार्थसंबोधे मन्त्रवार्तिकमादरात् ॥ 268
16.m: 'He is skilled in mantra and tantra.' / Therefore, in understanding the meaning of mantra, the guru should by all means practice

16.s:
ūhāpohaprayogaṃ vā sarvathā gururācaret /
mantrārthavidabhāve tu sarvathā mantratanmayam // 269
16.d:
ऊहापोहप्रयोगं वा सर्वथा गुरुराचरेत् ।
मन्त्रार्थविदभावे तु सर्वथा मन्त्रतन्मयम् ॥ 269
16.m: the Mantravārtika with reverence, or the application of reasoning and refutation. / In the absence of one who knows the meaning of the mantra, however, one should by all means make a guru

16.s:
guruṃ kuryāt tadabhyāsāttatsaṃkalpamayo hyasau /
tatsamānābhisaṃjalpo yadā mantrārthabhāvanāt // 270
16.d:
गुरुं कुर्यात् तदभ्यासात्तत्संकल्पमयो ह्यसौ ।
तत्समानाभिसंजल्पो यदा मन्त्रार्थभावनात् ॥ 270
16.m: who is identified with the mantra, for through its repeated practice he consists of its conception. / When, through meditating on the mantra's meaning, the guru possesses discursive speech identical to that,

16.s:
gurorbhavettadā sarvasāmye ko bheda ucyatām /
aṃśenāpyatha vaiṣamye na tato'rthakriyā hi sā // 271
16.d:
गुरोर्भवेत्तदा सर्वसाम्ये को भेद उच्यताम् ।
अंशेनाप्यथ वैषम्ये न ततोऽर्थक्रिया हि सा ॥ 271
16.m: then tell us: since there is complete equality, what difference is there? / If, on the other hand, there were dissimilarity even in part, then that purposeful action would not occur.

16.s:
gomayātkīṭataḥ kīṭa ityevaṃ nyāyato yadā /
saṃjalpāntarato'pyarthakriyāṃ tāmeva paśyati // 272
16.d:
गोमयात्कीटतः कीट इत्येवं न्यायतो यदा ।
संजल्पान्तरतोऽप्यर्थक्रियां तामेव पश्यति ॥ 272
16.m: When, by the maxim that a scorpion [is born] from cow dung just as a scorpion [from a scorpion], / one sees the very same purposeful action even from another discursive speech,

16.s:
tadaiṣa satyasaṃjalpaḥ śiva eveti kathyate /
sa yadvakti tadeva syānmantro bhogāpavargadaḥ // 273
16.d:
तदैष सत्यसंजल्पः शिव एवेति कथ्यते ।
स यद्वक्ति तदेव स्यान्मन्त्रो भोगापवर्गदः ॥ 273
16.m: then this true speech is said to be Śiva himself; / whatever he speaks becomes the very mantra granting enjoyment and liberation.

16.s:
naiṣo'bhinavaguptasya pakṣo mantrārpitātmanaḥ /
yo'rthakriyāmāha bhinnāṃ kīṭayorapi tādṛśoḥ // 274
16.d:
नैषोऽभिनवगुप्तस्य पक्षो मन्त्रार्पितात्मनः ।
योऽर्थक्रियामाह भिन्नां कीटयोरपि तादृशोः ॥ 274
16.m: This is not the view of Abhinavagupta, whose self is surrendered to the mantra, / who states that purposeful action is distinct even between two such scorpions.

16.s:
mantrārpitamanāḥ kiṃcidvadanyattu viṣaṃ haret /
tanmantra eva śabdaḥ sa paraṃ tatra ghaṭādivat // 275
16.d:
मन्त्रार्पितमनाः किंचिद्वदन्यत्तु विषं हरेत् ।
तन्मन्त्र एव शब्दः स परं तत्र घटादिवत् ॥ 275
16.m: One whose mind is dedicated to the mantra removes poison even while saying something else; / that word is indeed the mantra itself, whereas another [word] is like 'pot' and so forth.

16.s:
kāntāsaṃbhogasaṃjalpasundaraḥ kāmukaḥ sadā /
tatsaṃskṛto'pyanyadeṣa kurvansvātmani tṛpyati // 276
16.d:
कान्तासंभोगसंजल्पसुन्दरः कामुकः सदा ।
तत्संस्कृतोऽप्यन्यदेष कुर्वन्स्वात्मनि तृप्यति ॥ 276
16.m: A lover who is always captivated by speech concerning lovemaking with a beloved woman, / being cultivated by that, remains satisfied in himself even while doing something else;

16.s:
tathā tanmantrasaṃjalpabhāvito'nyadapi bruvan /
anicchurapi tadrūpastathā kāryakaro dhruvam // 277
16.d:
तथा तन्मन्त्रसंजल्पभावितोऽन्यदपि ब्रुवन् ।
अनिच्छुरपि तद्रूपस्तथा कार्यकरो ध्रुवम् ॥ 277
16.m: similarly, one imbued with the discursive speech of that mantra, even when speaking of other things, / achieves that effect surely, being of that nature even without actively desiring it.

16.s:
vikalpayannapyekārthaṃ yato'nyadapi paśyati /
viṣāpahārimantrādītyuktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāsane // 278
16.d:
विकल्पयन्नप्येकार्थं यतोऽन्यदपि पश्यति ।
विषापहारिमन्त्रादीत्युक्तं श्रीपूर्वशासने ॥ 278
16.m: For, even while conceptualizing one object, he perceives another as well, / as in the mantra that dispels poison, etc., as stated in the holy Pūrvaśāsana.

16.s:
yadi vā viṣanāśe'pi hetubhedādvicitratā /
dhātvāpyāyādikānantakāryabhedādbhaviṣyati // 279
16.d:
यदि वा विषनाशेऽपि हेतुभेदाद्विचित्रता ।
धात्वाप्यायादिकानन्तकार्यभेदाद्भविष्यति ॥ 279
16.m: Or rather, even in the destruction of poison, there will be variety due to differences in causes, / owing to the endless differences of effects such as the replenishment of bodily elements and the like.

16.s:
tadevaṃ mantrasaṃjalpavikalpābhyāsayogataḥ /
bhāvyavastusphuṭībhāvaḥ saṃjalpahrāsayogataḥ // 280
16.d:
तदेवं मन्त्रसंजल्पविकल्पाभ्यासयोगतः ।
भाव्यवस्तुस्फुटीभावः संजल्पह्रासयोगतः ॥ 280
16.m: Therefore, in this way, through the practice of conceptual constructs of the mantra's discursive speech, / the object to be meditated upon becomes manifest through the decrease of discursive speech.

16.s:
vastveva bhāvayatyeṣa na saṃjalpamimaṃ punaḥ /
gṛhṇāti bhāsanopāyaṃ bhāte tatra tu tena kim // 281
16.d:
वस्त्वेव भावयत्येष न संजल्पमिमं पुनः ।
गृह्णाति भासनोपायं भाते तत्र तु तेन किम् ॥ 281
16.m: He meditates upon the reality alone; he no longer / grasps this discursive speech, which is the means to illumination: for what use is it once that has shone forth?

16.s:
evaṃ saṃjalpanirhrāse suparisphuṭatātmakam /
akṛttrimavimarśātma sphuredvastvavikalpakam // 282
16.d:
एवं संजल्पनिर्ह्रासे सुपरिस्फुटतात्मकम् ।
अकृत्त्रिमविमर्शात्म स्फुरेद्वस्त्वविकल्पकम् ॥ 282
16.m: Thus, when discursive speech dwindles away, the non-conceptual reality, / entirely clear and consisting of innate reflective awareness, shines forth.

16.s:
nirvikalpā ca sā saṃvidyadyathā paśyati sphuṭam /
tattathaiva tathātmatvādvastuno'pi bahiḥsthiteḥ // 283
16.d:
निर्विकल्पा च सा संविद्यद्यथा पश्यति स्फुटम् ।
तत्तथैव तथात्मत्वाद्वस्तुनोऽपि बहिःस्थितेः ॥ 283
16.m: And that non-conceptual consciousness, just as it clearly perceives [a reality], / is precisely so, because an external object also has that as its true nature.

16.s:
viśeṣatastvamāyīyaśivatābhedaśālinaḥ /
mokṣe'bhyupāyaḥ saṃjalpo bandhamokṣau tataḥ kila // 284
16.d:
विशेषतस्त्वमायीयशिवताभेदशालिनः ।
मोक्षेऽभ्युपायः संजल्पो बन्धमोक्षौ ततः किल ॥ 284
16.m: In particular, for one endowed with non-difference from Śiva-hood free of Māyā, / internal articulation is an expedient toward liberation; hence both bondage and liberation [derive] from it.

16.s:
vikalpe'pi guroḥ samyagabhinnaśivatājuṣaḥ /
avikalpakaparyantapratīkṣā nopayujyate // 285
16.d:
विकल्पेऽपि गुरोः सम्यगभिन्नशिवताजुषः ।
अविकल्पकपर्यन्तप्रतीक्षा नोपयुज्यते ॥ 285
16.m: Even when a conceptual construct arises, for a guru enjoying fully undivided Śiva-hood, / waiting for the non-conceptual terminus is of no use.

16.s:
tadvimarśasvabhāvā hi sā vācyā mantradevatā /
mahāsaṃvitsamāsannetyuktaṃ śrīgamaśāsane // 286
16.d:
तद्विमर्शस्वभावा हि सा वाच्या मन्त्रदेवता ।
महासंवित्समासन्नेत्युक्तं श्रीगमशासने ॥ 286
16.m: For that deity of the mantra, being the object denoted, has reflective awareness as its nature / and is intimate with the Great Consciousness—so it is declared in the venerable scriptures.

16.s:
nikaṭasthā yathā rājñāmanyeṣāṃ sādhayantyalam /
siddhiṃ rājopagāṃ śīghramevaṃ mantrādayaḥ parām // 287
16.d:
निकटस्था यथा राज्ञामन्येषां साधयन्त्यलम् ।
सिद्धिं राजोपगां शीघ्रमेवं मन्त्रादयः पराम् ॥ 287
16.m: Just as those standing near to kings fully accomplish for others / an accomplishment relating to kings quickly, so mantras and the rest [accomplish] the supreme [result].

16.s:
uktābhiprāyagarbhaṃ taduktaṃ śrīmālinīmate /
mantrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kasmādityukte munibhiḥ kila // 288
16.d:
उक्ताभिप्रायगर्भं तदुक्तं श्रीमालिनीमते ।
मन्त्राणां लक्षणं कस्मादित्युक्ते मुनिभिः किल ॥ 288
16.m: Containing that very intended meaning, it was said in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara, / when the sages asked: 'Why is the definition of mantras [stated]?'

16.s:
yogamekatvamicchanti vastuno'nyena vastunā /
tadvastu jñeyamityuktaṃ heyatvādiprasiddhaye // 289
16.d:
योगमेकत्वमिच्छन्ति वस्तुनोऽन्येन वस्तुना ।
तद्वस्तु ज्ञेयमित्युक्तं हेयत्वादिप्रसिद्धये ॥ 289
16.m: 'They desire yoga to be the oneness of one entity with another entity; / that entity is called the object of knowledge, in order to establish what is to be discarded and the rest.'

16.s:
tatprasiddhyai śivenoktaṃ jñānaṃ yadupavarṇitam /
sabījayogasaṃsiddhyai mantralakṣaṇamapyalam // 290
16.d:
तत्प्रसिद्ध्यै शिवेनोक्तं ज्ञानं यदुपवर्णितम् ।
सबीजयोगसंसिद्ध्यै मन्त्रलक्षणमप्यलम् ॥ 290
16.m: For that establishment, the knowledge taught by Śiva which has been described / is also fully sufficient as the definition of mantra for accomplishing yoga with seed.

16.s:
na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge'sti śāṅkare /
kriyājñānavibhedena sā ca dvedhā nigadyate // 291
16.d:
न चाधिकारिता दीक्षां विना योगेऽस्ति शाङ्करे ।
क्रियाज्ञानविभेदेन सा च द्वेधा निगद्यते ॥ 291
16.m: Nor is there qualification for Śaiva yoga without initiation; / and that is spoken of as twofold, divided into action and knowledge.

16.s:
dvividhā sā prakartavyā tena caitadudāhṛtam /
naca yogādhikāritvamekamevānayā bhavet // 292
16.d:
द्विविधा सा प्रकर्तव्या तेन चैतदुदाहृतम् ।
नच योगाधिकारित्वमेकमेवानया भवेत् ॥ 292
16.m: It should be performed as twofold, and by that this has been explained; / nor would there arise merely the qualification for yoga by this [initiation],

16.s:
api mantrādhikāritvaṃ muktiśca śivadīkṣayā /
anenaitadapi proktaṃ yogī tattvaikyasiddhaye // 293
16.d:
अपि मन्त्राधिकारित्वं मुक्तिश्च शिवदीक्षया ।
अनेनैतदपि प्रोक्तं योगी तत्त्वैक्यसिद्धये ॥ 293
16.m: but also qualification for mantra and liberation through Śiva-initiation. / By this, it is also stated that a yogin, in order to attain oneness with reality,

16.s:
mantramevāśrayenmūlaṃ nirvikalpāntamādṛtaḥ /
mantrābhyāsena bhogaṃ vā mokṣaṃ vāpi prasādhayan // 294
16.d:
मन्त्रमेवाश्रयेन्मूलं निर्विकल्पान्तमादृतः ।
मन्त्राभ्यासेन भोगं वा मोक्षं वापि प्रसाधयन् ॥ 294
16.m: should respectfully resort to the root mantra alone, which culminates in the non-conceptual, / accomplishing either enjoyment or even liberation through repeated practice of the mantra.

16.s:
tatrādhikāritālabdhyai dīkṣāṃ gṛhṇīta daiśikāt /
tena mantrajñānayogabalādyadyatprasādhayet // 295
16.d:
तत्राधिकारितालब्ध्यै दीक्षां गृह्णीत दैशिकात् ।
तेन मन्त्रज्ञानयोगबलाद्यद्यत्प्रसाधयेत् ॥ 295
16.m: To attain qualification therein, he should receive initiation from the guru; / thereby, by the power of knowledge and yoga of mantra, whatever he accomplishes,

16.s:
tatsyādasyānyatattve'pi yuktasya guruṇā śiśoḥ /
dīkṣā hyasyopayujyeta saṃskriyāyāṃ sa saṃskṛtaḥ // 296
16.d:
तत्स्यादस्यान्यतत्त्वेऽपि युक्तस्य गुरुणा शिशोः ।
दीक्षा ह्यस्योपयुज्येत संस्क्रियायां स संस्कृतः ॥ 296
16.m: that would belong to this pupil conjoined [thereto] by the guru, even in another reality-level. / For initiation is required for his purification; once purified,

16.s:
svabalenaiva bhogaṃ vā mokṣaṃ vā labhate budhaḥ /
tena vijñānayogādibalī prāk samayī bhavan // 297
16.d:
स्वबलेनैव भोगं वा मोक्षं वा लभते बुधः ।
तेन विज्ञानयोगादिबली प्राक् समयी भवन् ॥ 297
16.m: the wise one obtains either enjoyment or liberation by his own power alone. / Therefore, one who is strong through yoga of knowledge and the rest, becoming an initiate into the rule first,

16.s:
putrako vā na tāvānsyādapitu svabalocitaḥ /
yastu vijñānayogādivandhyaḥ so'ndho yathā pathi // 298
16.d:
पुत्रको वा न तावान्स्यादपितु स्वबलोचितः ।
यस्तु विज्ञानयोगादिवन्ध्यः सोऽन्धो यथा पथि ॥ 298
16.m: or a spiritual son, would not remain merely that, but would be fit for his own power. / But he who is devoid of the yoga of knowledge and the rest, like a blind man on a road,

16.s:
daiśikāyatta eva syādbhoge muktau ca sarvathā /
dīkṣā ca kevalā jñānaṃ vināpi nijamāntaram // 299
16.d:
दैशिकायत्त एव स्याद्भोगे मुक्तौ च सर्वथा ।
दीक्षा च केवला ज्ञानं विनापि निजमान्तरम् ॥ 299
16.m: would be entirely dependent upon the guru for enjoyment and for liberation. / And it was previously stated by reasoning and scripture that initiation alone,

16.s:
mocikaiveti kathitaṃ yuktyā cāgamataḥ purā /
yastu dīkṣākṛtāmevāpekṣya yojanikāṃ śiśuḥ // 300
16.d:
मोचिकैवेति कथितं युक्त्या चागमतः पुरा ।
यस्तु दीक्षाकृतामेवापेक्ष्य योजनिकां शिशुः ॥ 300
16.m: even without internal personal knowledge, is indeed liberating. / But a pupil who, relying on the conjunction effected by initiation alone,

16.s:
sphuṭībhūtyai taducitaṃ jñānaṃ yogamathāśritaḥ /
so'pi yatraiva yuktaḥ syāttanmayatvaṃ prapadyate // 301
16.d:
स्फुटीभूत्यै तदुचितं ज्ञानं योगमथाश्रितः ।
सोऽपि यत्रैव युक्तः स्यात्तन्मयत्वं प्रपद्यते ॥ 301
16.m: has then resorted to the knowledge and yoga appropriate for its manifestation, / he too attains identity with that very level where he is joined.

16.s:
gurudīkṣāmantraśāstrādhīnasarvasthitistataḥ /
duṣṭānāmeva sarveṣāṃ bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyatām // 302
16.d:
गुरुदीक्षामन्त्रशास्त्राधीनसर्वस्थितिस्ततः ।
दुष्टानामेव सर्वेषां भूतभव्यभविष्यताम् ॥ 302
16.m: Therefore, for one whose whole condition is dependent on guru, initiation, mantra, and scripture, / purification must be performed only of all the bad karmas—past, present, and future—

16.s:
karmaṇāṃ śodhanaṃ kāryaṃ bubhukṣorna śubhātmanām /
yaḥ punarlaukikaṃ bhogaṃ rājyasvargādikaṃ śiśuḥ // 303
16.d:
कर्मणां शोधनं कार्यं बुभुक्षोर्न शुभात्मनाम् ।
यः पुनर्लौकिकं भोगं राज्यस्वर्गादिकं शिशुः ॥ 303
16.m: for one desiring enjoyment, not of auspicious ones. / But for that pupil who, having renounced mundane enjoyment such as kingdom and heaven,

16.s:
tyaktvā lokottaraṃ bhogamīpsustasya śubheṣvapi /
tatra dravyamayīṃ dīkṣāṃ kurvannājyatilādikaiḥ // 304
16.d:
त्यक्त्वा लोकोत्तरं भोगमीप्सुस्तस्य शुभेष्वपि ।
तत्र द्रव्यमयीं दीक्षां कुर्वन्नाज्यतिलादिकैः ॥ 304
16.m: desires transmundane enjoyment, even regarding his auspicious [karmas]: / performing material initiation therein with ghee, sesame seeds, and the like,

16.s:
karmāsya śodhayāmīti juhuyāddaiśikottamaḥ /
jñānamayyāṃ tu dīkṣāyāṃ tadviśuddhyati sandhitaḥ // 305
16.d:
कर्मास्य शोधयामीति जुहुयाद्दैशिकोत्तमः ।
ज्ञानमय्यां तु दीक्षायां तद्विशुद्ध्यति सन्धितः ॥ 305
16.m: the excellent guru should offer oblations, thinking, 'I purify his karma.' / But in initiation of the nature of knowledge, that is purified by meditation;

16.s:
guroḥ svasaṃvidrūḍhasya balāttatprakṣayo bhavet /
yadāsyāśubhakarmāṇi śuddhāni syustadā śubham // 306
16.d:
गुरोः स्वसंविद्रूढस्य बलात्तत्प्रक्षयो भवेत् ।
यदास्याशुभकर्माणि शुद्धानि स्युस्तदा शुभम् ॥ 306
16.m: by the power of the guru established in his own consciousness, its destruction takes place. / When his inauspicious karmas are purified, then the auspicious [karma],

16.s:
svatāratamyāśrayaṇādadhvamadhye prasūtidam /
śubhapākakramopāttaphalabhogasamāptitaḥ // 307
16.d:
स्वतारतम्याश्रयणादध्वमध्ये प्रसूतिदम् ।
शुभपाकक्रमोपात्तफलभोगसमाप्तितः ॥ 307
16.m: resorting to its relative gradation, produces results midway along the path. / Through the exhaustion of the enjoyment of fruits obtained by the orderly ripening of the auspicious [karma],

16.s:
yatraiṣa yojitastatstho bhāvikarmakṣaye kṛte /
bhāvināṃ cādyadehasthadehāntaravibhedinām // 308
16.d:
यत्रैष योजितस्तत्स्थो भाविकर्मक्षये कृते ।
भाविनां चाद्यदेहस्थदेहान्तरविभेदिनाम् ॥ 308
16.m: and when future karma has been destroyed, being established wherever he has been conjoined, / and with the purification of the inauspicious portions of future [karmas] differentiating the present body from other bodies,

16.s:
aśubhāṃśaviśuddhau syādbhogasyaivānupakṣayaḥ /
bhuñjānasyāsya satataṃ bhogānmāyālayāntataḥ // 309
16.d:
अशुभांशविशुद्धौ स्याद्भोगस्यैवानुपक्षयः ।
भुञ्जानस्यास्य सततं भोगान्मायालयान्ततः ॥ 309
16.m: there would be no diminishment of enjoyment alone; / for him continuously experiencing enjoyments up to the dissolution of Māyā,

16.s:
na duḥkhaphaladaṃ dehādyadhvamadhye'pi kiṃcana /
tato māyālaye bhuktasamastasukhabhogakaḥ // 310
16.d:
न दुःखफलदं देहाद्यध्वमध्येऽपि किंचन ।
ततो मायालये भुक्तसमस्तसुखभोगकः ॥ 310
16.m: nothing, including the body, yields painful fruit even midway along the path. / Then, having experienced all pleasures and enjoyments in the dissolution of Māyā,

16.s:
niṣkale sakale vaiti layaṃ yojanikābalāt /
iti prameyaṃ kathitaṃ dīkṣā kāle guroryathā // 311
16.d:
निष्कले सकले वैति लयं योजनिकाबलात् ।
इति प्रमेयं कथितं दीक्षा काले गुरोर्यथा ॥ 311
16.m: he goes to dissolution in the partless or the partitioned by the power of conjunction. / Thus has the object of knowledge been taught, just as [it is] at the time of the guru's initiation.

17.s:
atha bhairavatādātmyadāyinīṃ prakriyāṃ bruve /
evaṃ maṇḍalakumbhāgniśiṣyasvātmasu pañcasu // 1
17.d:
अथ भैरवतादात्म्यदायिनीं प्रक्रियां ब्रुवे ।
एवं मण्डलकुम्भाग्निशिष्यस्वात्मसु पञ्चसु ॥ 1
17.m: Now I explain the ritual procedure that bestows identity with Bhairava: / having thus perceived pervasion through oneness in the five—

17.s:
gṛhītvā vyāptimaikyena nyasyādhvānaṃ ca śiṣyagam /
karmamāyāṇumalinatrayaṃ bāhau gale tathā // 2
17.d:
गृहीत्वा व्याप्तिमैक्येन न्यस्याध्वानं च शिष्यगम् ।
कर्ममायाणुमलिनत्रयं बाहौ गले तथा ॥ 2
17.m: the maṇḍala, pot, fire, disciple, and oneself—and having projected the path residing in the disciple, / the guru should cast the triad of impurities consisting of karma, Māyā, and the atomic [impurity] on the arm, throat,

17.s:
śikhāyāṃ ca kṣipetsūtragranthiyogena daiśikaḥ /
tasyātadrūpatābhānaṃ malo granthiḥ sa kīrtyate // 3
17.d:
शिखायां च क्षिपेत्सूत्रग्रन्थियोगेन दैशिकः ।
तस्यातद्रूपताभानं मलो ग्रन्थिः स कीर्त्यते ॥ 3
17.m: and crest-knot through knotting the cord. / The appearance of non-identity [with Śiva] is called the impurity, the knot;

17.s:
itipratītidārḍhyārthaṃ bahirgranthyupakalpanam /
bāhū karmāspadaṃ viṣṇurmāyātmā galasaṃśritaḥ // 4
17.d:
इतिप्रतीतिदार्ढ्यार्थं बहिर्ग्रन्थ्युपकल्पनम् ।
बाहू कर्मास्पदं विष्णुर्मायात्मा गलसंश्रितः ॥ 4
17.m: to strengthen this conviction, an external knot is constructed. / The two arms are the seat of karma; Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of Māyā, resides in the throat;

17.s:
adhovahā śikhāṇutvaṃ tenetthaṃ kalpanā kṛtā /
naraśaktiśivākhyasya trayasya bahubhedatām // 5
17.d:
अधोवहा शिखाणुत्वं तेनेत्थं कल्पना कृता ।
नरशक्तिशिवाख्यस्य त्रयस्य बहुभेदताम् ॥ 5
17.m: the downward-flowing crest-knot is the atomic state; thus this conception has been made. / In order to express the manifold differentiation of the triad known as man, power, and Śiva,

17.s:
vaktuṃ tristriguṇaṃ sūtraṃ granthaye parikalpayet /
tejojalānnatritayaṃ tredhā pratyekamapyadaḥ // 6
17.d:
वक्तुं त्रिस्त्रिगुणं सूत्रं ग्रन्थये परिकल्पयेत् ।
तेजोजलान्नत्रितयं त्रेधा प्रत्येकमप्यदः ॥ 6
17.m: one should fashion the cord ninefold for knotting. / The triad of fire, water, and earth is also threefold, each one of these;

17.s:
śrutyante ke'pyataḥ śuklakṛṣṇaraktaṃ prapedire /
tato'gnau tarpitāśeṣamantre cidvyomamātrake // 7
17.d:
श्रुत्यन्ते केऽप्यतः शुक्लकृष्णरक्तं प्रपेदिरे ।
ततोऽग्नौ तर्पिताशेषमन्त्रे चिद्व्योममात्रके ॥ 7
17.m: hence some in the Upaniṣads adopted white, black, and red. / Then, in the fire where all mantras have been gratified, in the mere ether of consciousness,

17.s:
sāmānyarūpe tattvānāṃ kramācchuddhiṃ samācaret /
tatra svamantrayogena dharāmāvāhayetpurā // 8
17.d:
सामान्यरूपे तत्त्वानां क्रमाच्छुद्धिं समाचरेत् ।
तत्र स्वमन्त्रयोगेन धरामावाहयेत्पुरा ॥ 8
17.m: which has a general form, one should perform the purification of the reality-levels in succession. / There, by employing its own mantra, one should first invoke the earth;

17.s:
iṣṭvā puṣpādibhiḥ sarpistilādyairatha tarpayet /
tattattvavyāpikāṃ paścānmāyātattvādhidevatām // 9
17.d:
इष्ट्वा पुष्पादिभिः सर्पिस्तिलाद्यैरथ तर्पयेत् ।
तत्तत्त्वव्यापिकां पश्चान्मायातत्त्वाधिदेवताम् ॥ 9
17.m: having worshiped with flowers and the like, one should then gratify with ghee, sesame seeds, and the like. / Afterward, having invoked, worshiped, and gratified with its own mantra the power of Māyā,

17.s:
māyāśaktiṃ svamantreṇāvāhyābhyarcya pratarpayet /
āvāhane mātṛkārṇaṃ mālinyarṇaṃ ca pūjane // 10
17.d:
मायाशक्तिं स्वमन्त्रेणावाह्याभ्यर्च्य प्रतर्पयेत् ।
आवाहने मातृकार्णं मालिन्यर्णं च पूजने ॥ 10
17.m: which is the presiding deity of the reality-level of Māyā and the pervader of each respective reality-level— / one should use the syllable of Mātṛkā in invocation, and the syllable of Mālinī in worship,

17.s:
kuryāditi guruḥ prāha svarūpāpyāyanadvayāt /
tāro varṇo'tha saṃbuddhipadaṃ tvāmityataḥ param // 11
17.d:
कुर्यादिति गुरुः प्राह स्वरूपाप्यायनद्वयात् ।
तारो वर्णोऽथ संबुद्धिपदं त्वामित्यतः परम् ॥ 11
17.m: so the guru said, because of the two: one's own nature and nourishment. / Then the syllable OM, then the word in the vocative case, and after this the word 'you' (tvām);

17.s:
uttamaikayutaṃ karmapadaṃ dīpakamapyataḥ /
tabhyaṃ nāma caturthyantaṃ tato'pyucitadīpakam // 12
17.d:
उत्तमैकयुतं कर्मपदं दीपकमप्यतः ।
तभ्यं नाम चतुर्थ्यन्तं ततोऽप्युचितदीपकम् ॥ 12
17.m: then the word for the object of action joined with the first-person singular, then the illuminator; / then the name in the dative case, and then the appropriate illuminator—

17.s:
ityūhamantrayogena tattatkarma pravartayet /
āvāhanānantaraṃ hi karma sarvaṃ nigadyate // 13
17.d:
इत्यूहमन्त्रयोगेन तत्तत्कर्म प्रवर्तयेत् ।
आवाहनानन्तरं हि कर्म सर्वं निगद्यते ॥ 13
17.m: by employing the mantra thus adapted, one should perform each respective rite. / For every rite is indeed declared to come after invocation.

17.s:
āvāhanaṃ ca saṃbodhaḥ svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ /
bhāvasyāhaṃmayasvātmatādātmyāveśyamānatā // 14
17.d:
आवाहनं च संबोधः स्वस्वभावव्यवस्थितेः ।
भावस्याहंमयस्वात्मतादात्म्यावेश्यमानता ॥ 14
17.m: And invocation is awakening to abiding in one's essential nature, / the causing of an entity to enter into identity with one's own self, which is full of 'I'.

17.s:
śāktī bhūmiśca saivoktā yasyāṃ mukhyāsti pūjyatā /
abhātatvādabhedācca nahyasau nṛśivātmanoḥ // 15
17.d:
शाक्ती भूमिश्च सैवोक्ता यस्यां मुख्यास्ति पूज्यता ।
अभातत्वादभेदाच्च नह्यसौ नृशिवात्मनोः ॥ 15
17.m: That itself is declared to be the plane of power, on which the principal worshipfulness rests; / for it does not belong to the self of man or Śiva, due to unmanifestness and non-difference.

17.s:
jaḍābhāseṣu tattveṣu saṃvitsthityai tato guruḥ /
āvāhanavibhaktiṃ prāk kṛtvā turyavibhaktitaḥ // 16
17.d:
जडाभासेषु तत्त्वेषु संवित्स्थित्यै ततो गुरुः ।
आवाहनविभक्तिं प्राक् कृत्वा तुर्यविभक्तितः ॥ 16
17.m: Therefore, for the sake of establishing consciousness in the reality-levels that appear insentient, / the guru, having first made the case of invocation, by means of the fourth case...

17.s:
namaskārāntatāyogātpūrṇāṃ sattāṃ prakalpayet /
tataḥ pūrṇasvabhāvatvaṃ tadrūpodrekayogataḥ // 17
17.d:
नमस्कारान्ततायोगात्पूर्णां सत्तां प्रकल्पयेत् ।
ततः पूर्णस्वभावत्वं तद्रूपोद्रेकयोगतः ॥ 17
17.m: By conjunction with an ending in salutation (namaḥ), he should project full being; / thence, a nature of fullness arises through conjunction with the exuberance of its form.

17.s:
dhyeyodreko bhaveddhyātṛprahvībhāvavaśādyataḥ /
āvāhyeṣṭvā pratarpyeti śrīsvacchande nirūpitam // 18
17.d:
ध्येयोद्रेको भवेद्ध्यातृप्रह्वीभाववशाद्यतः ।
आवाह्येष्ट्वा प्रतर्प्येति श्रीस्वच्छन्दे निरूपितम् ॥ 18
17.m: Since the exuberance of the object of meditation occurs through the meditator's becoming humbled, / having invoked, worshipped, and fully satisfied, so it has been explained in the venerable Svacchanda.

17.s:
anenaiva pathāneyamityasmadguravo jaguḥ /
paratvena tu yatpūjyaṃ tatsvatantracidātmakam // 19
17.d:
अनेनैव पथानेयमित्यस्मद्गुरवो जगुः ।
परत्वेन तु यत्पूज्यं तत्स्वतन्त्रचिदात्मकम् ॥ 19
17.m: By this very path it is to be led, so our gurus declared; / but that which is to be worshipped as transcendent consists of autonomous consciousness.

17.s:
anavacchitprakāśatvānna prakāśyaṃ tu kutracit /
tasya hyetatprapūjyatvadhyeyatvādi yadullaset // 20
17.d:
अनवच्छित्प्रकाशत्वान्न प्रकाश्यं तु कुत्रचित् ।
तस्य ह्येतत्प्रपूज्यत्वध्येयत्वादि यदुल्लसेत् ॥ 20
17.m: Because it is consciousness that does not terminate its own light, it is nowhere an object of illumination; / for whatever manifestation it may have as being worthy of worship, of meditation, and so forth,

17.s:
tasyaiva tatsvatantratvaṃ yātidurghaṭakāritā /
saṃbodharūpe tattasmin kathaṃ saṃbodhanā bhavet // 21
17.d:
तस्यैव तत्स्वतन्त्रत्वं यातिदुर्घटकारिता ।
संबोधरूपे तत्तस्मिन् कथं संबोधना भवेत् ॥ 21
17.m: that is its very absolute autonomy, bringing about what is exceedingly difficult to accomplish. / How could an address (vocative) apply to that which is itself the form of awakened consciousness?

17.s:
prakāśanāyāṃ na syātprakāśasya prakāśatā /
saṃbodhanavibhaktyaiva vinā karmādiśaktitām // 22
17.d:
प्रकाशनायां न स्यात्प्रकाशस्य प्रकाशता ।
संबोधनविभक्त्यैव विना कर्मादिशक्तिताम् ॥ 22
17.m: In the act of illuminating, there can be no further illuminating of luminosity itself. / Only through the case of address (vocative), without the role of an accusative object or other cases,

17.s:
svātantryāttaṃ darśayituṃ tatrohamimamācaret /
devamāvāhayāmīti tato devāya dīpakam // 23
17.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यात्तं दर्शयितुं तत्रोहमिममाचरेत् ।
देवमावाहयामीति ततो देवाय दीपकम् ॥ 23
17.m: he should make this contextual adaptation (ūha) in order to display it through its absolute autonomy: / 'I invoke the deity (devam)', and then the illuminator 'to the deity (devāya)'.

17.s:
prāgyuktyā pūrṇatādāyi namaḥsvāhādikaṃ bhavet /
nutiḥ pūrṇatvamagnīndusaṃghaṭṭāpyāyatā param // 24
17.d:
प्राग्युक्त्या पूर्णतादायि नमःस्वाहादिकं भवेत् ।
नुतिः पूर्णत्वमग्नीन्दुसंघट्टाप्यायता परम् ॥ 24
17.m: According to the previous reasoning, words such as namaḥ and svāhā bestow fullness; / praise is fullness, while replenishment through the union of fire and moon is supreme.

17.s:
āpyāyakaṃ ca procchālaṃ vauṣaḍādi pradīpayet /
tatra bāhye'pi tādātmyaprasiddhaṃ karma codyate // 25
17.d:
आप्यायकं च प्रोच्छालं वौषडादि प्रदीपयेत् ।
तत्र बाह्येऽपि तादात्म्यप्रसिद्धं कर्म चोद्यते ॥ 25
17.m: And vauṣaṭ and the like, which replenish and surge upward, he should kindle; / there, even externally, an accusative object established in identity is employed.

17.s:
yadi karmapadaṃ tanno gururabhyūhayetkvacit /
anābhāsitatadvastubhāsanāya niyujyate // 26
17.d:
यदि कर्मपदं तन्नो गुरुरभ्यूहयेत्क्वचित् ।
अनाभासिततद्वस्तुभासनाय नियुज्यते ॥ 26
17.m: If there is an accusative word, the guru should never contextually adapt it there; / a mantra is applied to illuminate an entity that has not been made manifest.

17.s:
mantraḥ kiṃ tena tatra syātsphuṭaṃ yatrāvabhāsi tat /
tena prokṣaṇasaṃsekajapādividhiṣu dhruvam // 27
17.d:
मन्त्रः किं तेन तत्र स्यात्स्फुटं यत्रावभासि तत् ।
तेन प्रोक्षणसंसेकजपादिविधिषु ध्रुवम् ॥ 27
17.m: What would it effect in a situation where that is already clearly manifest? / Therefore, in rites such as sprinkling, consecrating with water, recitation, and the like, certainly,

17.s:
tatkarmābhyūhanaṃ kuryātpratyuta vyavadhātṛtām /
bahistathātmatābhāve kāryaṃ karmapadohanam // 28
17.d:
तत्कर्माभ्यूहनं कुर्यात्प्रत्युत व्यवधातृताम् ।
बहिस्तथात्मताभावे कार्यं कर्मपदोहनम् ॥ 28
17.m: supplying that accusative object would rather cause obstruction; / contextual adaptation of an accusative word is to be made only when its state of being externally real is absent,

17.s:
tṛptāvāhutihutabhukpāśaploṣacchidādiṣu /
yatroddiṣṭe vidhau paścāttadanantaiḥ kriyātmakaiḥ // 29
17.d:
तृप्तावाहुतिहुतभुक्पाशप्लोषच्छिदादिषु ।
यत्रोद्दिष्टे विधौ पश्चात्तदनन्तैः क्रियात्मकैः ॥ 29
17.m: in rites of satisfying, offering oblations, feeding the fire, scorching bonds, severing, and so forth. / Where, after the rite is enjoined, it is to be accomplished by its endless parts

17.s:
aṃśaiḥ sādhyaṃ na tatroho dīkṣaṇādividhiṣviva /
tataḥ śiṣyasya tattattvasthāne'streṇa pratāḍanam // 30
17.d:
अंशैः साध्यं न तत्रोहो दीक्षणादिविधिष्विव ।
ततः शिष्यस्य तत्तत्त्वस्थानेऽस्त्रेण प्रताडनम् ॥ 30
17.m: consisting of actions, there is no contextual adaptation there, as in the rites of initiation and the like. / Then, striking [the disciple] with the Astra mantra at the location of that particular tattva,

17.s:
kṛtvātha śivahastena hṛdayaṃ parimarśayet /
tataḥ svanāḍīmārgeṇa hṛdayaṃ prāpya vai śiśoḥ // 31
17.d:
कृत्वाथ शिवहस्तेन हृदयं परिमर्शयेत् ।
ततः स्वनाडीमार्गेण हृदयं प्राप्य वै शिशोः ॥ 31
17.m: and then touching the heart with the hand of Śiva, / the guru should then reach the heart of the child by the path of his own channel (nāḍī).

17.s:
śiṣyātmanā sahaikatvaṃ gatvādāya ca taṃ hṛdā /
puṭitaṃ haṃsarūpākhyaṃ tatra saṃhāramudrayā // 32
17.d:
शिष्यात्मना सहैकत्वं गत्वादाय च तं हृदा ।
पुटितं हंसरूपाख्यं तत्र संहारमुद्रया ॥ 32
17.m: Attaining oneness with the disciple's soul, and seizing it, / enclosed by the heart, named as the form of the Haṃsa, by means of the mudrā of dissolution (saṃhāra),

17.s:
kuryādātmīyahṛdayasthitamapyavabhāsakam /
śiṣyadehasya tejobhī raśmimātrāviyogataḥ // 33
17.d:
कुर्यादात्मीयहृदयस्थितमप्यवभासकम् ।
शिष्यदेहस्य तेजोभी रश्मिमात्रावियोगतः ॥ 33
17.m: he should make it illuminate even though situated in his own heart, / by rays consisting of light, without detachment from the body of the disciple.

17.s:
svabandhasthānacalanāt svatantrasthānalābhataḥ /
svakarmāparatantratvātsarvatrotpattimarhati // 34
17.d:
स्वबन्धस्थानचलनात् स्वतन्त्रस्थानलाभतः ।
स्वकर्मापरतन्त्रत्वात्सर्वत्रोत्पत्तिमर्हति ॥ 34
17.m: Because of moving from its place of bondage, obtaining an autonomous abode, / and not being dependent on its own karma, it is worthy of emergence everywhere.

17.s:
tenātmahṛdayānītaṃ prākkṛtvā pudgalaṃ tataḥ /
māyāyāṃ taddharātattvaśarīrāṇyasya saṃsṛjet // 35
17.d:
तेनात्महृदयानीतं प्राक्कृत्वा पुद्गलं ततः ।
मायायां तद्धरातत्त्वशरीराण्यस्य संसृजेत् ॥ 35
17.m: Having therefore first brought the individual soul (pudgala) into his own heart, then, / in Māyā, he should fashion for it bodies made of the earth tattva.

17.s:
tatrāsya garbhādhānaṃ ca yuktaṃ puṃsavanādibhiḥ /
garbhaniṣkrāmaparyantairekāṃ kurvīta saṃskriyām // 36
17.d:
तत्रास्य गर्भाधानं च युक्तं पुंसवनादिभिः ।
गर्भनिष्क्रामपर्यन्तैरेकां कुर्वीत संस्क्रियाम् ॥ 36
17.m: There, he should perform as a single purification (saṃskāra) its conception, / along with the rite for producing a male (puṃsavana) and others, up to emergence from the womb.

17.s:
jananaṃ bhogabhoktṛtvaṃ militvaikātha saṃskriyā /
tato'sya teṣu bhogeṣu kuryāttanmayatāṃ layam // 37
17.d:
जननं भोगभोक्तृत्वं मिलित्वैकाथ संस्क्रिया ।
ततोऽस्य तेषु भोगेषु कुर्यात्तन्मयतां लयम् ॥ 37
17.m: Birth and the status of experiencing enjoyment together form another single purification; / then he should effect its absorption and identification in those enjoyments.

17.s:
tatastattattvapāśānāṃ vicchedaṃ samupācaret /
saṃskārāṇāṃ catuṣke'sminnaparāṃ ca parāparām // 38
17.d:
ततस्तत्तत्त्वपाशानां विच्छेदं समुपाचरेत् ।
संस्काराणां चतुष्केऽस्मिन्नपरां च परापराम् ॥ 38
17.m: Then he should carry out the severing of the bonds of that tattva. / In this quartet of purifications, he should employ in succession Aparā, Parāparā,

17.s:
mantrāṇāṃ pañcadaśakaṃ parāṃ vā yojayetkramāt /
pivanyādyaṣṭakaṃ śastrādikaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ parā tathā // 39
17.d:
मन्त्राणां पञ्चदशकं परां वा योजयेत्क्रमात् ।
पिवन्याद्यष्टकं शस्त्रादिकं षट्कं परा तथा ॥ 39
17.m: the group of fifteen mantras, or Parā: / the group of eight beginning with Pivanī, the group of six beginning with the Weapon, and Parā—

17.s:
iti pañcadaśaite syuḥ kramāllīnatvasaṃskṛtau /
aparāmantramuktvā prāgamukātmana ityatha // 40
17.d:
इति पञ्चदशैते स्युः क्रमाल्लीनत्वसंस्कृतौ ।
अपरामन्त्रमुक्त्वा प्रागमुकात्मन इत्यथ ॥ 40
17.m: these are the fifteen in succession for the purification of absorption. / Having first recited the Aparā mantra, saying 'of such-and-such a soul',

17.s:
garbhādhānaṃ karomīti punarmantraṃ tameva ca /
svāhāntamuccarandadyādāhutitritayaṃ guruḥ // 41
17.d:
गर्भाधानं करोमीति पुनर्मन्त्रं तमेव च ।
स्वाहान्तमुच्चरन्दद्यादाहुतित्रितयं गुरुः ॥ 41
17.m: and saying 'I perform the conception', reciting once more that same mantra / ending in svāhā, the guru should offer three oblations.

17.s:
paraṃ parāparāmantramamukātmana ityatha /
jātasya bhogabhoktṛtvaṃ karomyatha parāparām // 42
17.d:
परं परापरामन्त्रममुकात्मन इत्यथ ।
जातस्य भोगभोक्तृत्वं करोम्यथ परापराम् ॥ 42
17.m: Then, reciting the Parāparā mantra, and saying 'of such-and-such a soul / who is born, I perform the status of experiencing enjoyment', and then the Parāparā,

17.s:
ante svāheti proccārya vitarettisra āhutīḥ /
uccārya pivanīmantramamukātmana ityatha // 43
17.d:
अन्ते स्वाहेति प्रोच्चार्य वितरेत्तिस्र आहुतीः ।
उच्चार्य पिवनीमन्त्रममुकात्मन इत्यथ ॥ 43
17.m: uttering svāhā at the end, he should bestow three oblations. / Reciting the Pivanī mantra, and saying 'of such-and-such a soul

17.s:
bhoge layaṃ karomīti punarmantraṃ tameva ca /
svāhāntamāhutīstisro dadyādājyatilādibhiḥ // 44
17.d:
भोगे लयं करोमीति पुनर्मन्त्रं तमेव च ।
स्वाहान्तमाहुतीस्तिस्रो दद्यादाज्यतिलादिभिः ॥ 44
17.m: I perform absorption in enjoyment', and once more that same mantra / ending in svāhā, he should offer three oblations of clarified butter, sesame seeds, and the like.

17.s:
eṣa eva vamanyādau vidhiḥ pañcadaśāntake /
pūrvaṃ parātmakaṃ mantramamukātmana ityatha // 45
17.d:
एष एव वमन्यादौ विधिः पञ्चदशान्तके ।
पूर्वं परात्मकं मन्त्रममुकात्मन इत्यथ ॥ 45
17.m: This very rule applies to the group ending with the fifteenth, beginning with Vamanī. / Having first recited the mantra whose nature is Parā, saying 'of such-and-such a soul

17.s:
pāśācchedaṃ karomīti parāmantraḥ punastataḥ /
huṃ svāhā phaṭ samuccārya dadyāttisro'pyathāhutīḥ // 46
17.d:
पाशाच्छेदं करोमीति परामन्त्रः पुनस्ततः ।
हुं स्वाहा फट् समुच्चार्य दद्यात्तिस्रोऽप्यथाहुतीः ॥ 46
17.m: I perform the severing of the bond', then the Parā mantra again, / uttering 'huṃ svāhā phaṭ', he should also offer three oblations.

17.s:
saṃskārāṇāṃ catuṣke'sminye mantrāḥ kathitā mayā /
teṣu karmapadātpūrvaṃ dharātattvapadaṃ vadet // 47
17.d:
संस्काराणां चतुष्केऽस्मिन्ये मन्त्राः कथिता मया ।
तेषु कर्मपदात्पूर्वं धरातत्त्वपदं वदेत् ॥ 47
17.m: Among these four purifications, in the mantras I have declared, / before the accusative word he should recite the word for the earth tattva.

17.s:
tato dharātattvapatimāmantryeṣṭvā pratarpya ca /
śivābhimānasaṃrabdho gururevaṃ samādiśet // 48
17.d:
ततो धरातत्त्वपतिमामन्त्र्येष्ट्वा प्रतर्प्य च ।
शिवाभिमानसंरब्धो गुरुरेवं समादिशेत् ॥ 48
17.m: Then, having addressed the lord of the earth tattva, worshipped, and fully satisfied him, / filled with the proud identification with Śiva, the guru should command thus:

17.s:
tattveśvara tvayā nāsya putrakasya śivājñayā /
pratibandhaḥ prakartavyo yātuḥ padamanāmayam // 49
17.d:
तत्त्वेश्वर त्वया नास्य पुत्रकस्य शिवाज्ञया ।
प्रतिबन्धः प्रकर्तव्यो यातुः पदमनामयम् ॥ 49
17.m: 'O Lord of the Tattva, by the command of Śiva, no obstacle should be made by you / to this spiritual son who is going to the painless realm.'

17.s:
tato yadi samīheta dharātattvāntarālagam /
pṛthak śodhayituṃ mantrī bhuvanādyadhvapañcakam // 50
17.d:
ततो यदि समीहेत धरातत्त्वान्तरालगम् ।
पृथक् शोधयितुं मन्त्री भुवनाद्यध्वपञ्चकम् ॥ 50
17.m: Then, if the mantra-knower desires to purify separately / the fivefold path of worlds and so on situated within the earth tattva,

17.s:
aparāmantrataḥ prāgvattisrastisrastadāhutīḥ /
dadyātpuraṃ śodhayāmītyūhayuktaṃ prasannadhīḥ // 51
17.d:
अपरामन्त्रतः प्राग्वत्तिस्रस्तिस्रस्तदाहुतीः ।
दद्यात्पुरं शोधयामीत्यूहयुक्तं प्रसन्नधीः ॥ 51
17.m: with a serene mind, he should offer three oblations each by means of the Aparā mantra as before, / accompanied by the adaptation: 'I purify the city.'

17.s:
evaṃ kalāmantrapadavarṇeṣvapi vicakṣaṇaḥ /
tisrastisro hutīrdadyāt pṛthak sāmastyato'pivā // 52
17.d:
एवं कलामन्त्रपदवर्णेष्वपि विचक्षणः ।
तिस्रस्तिस्रो हुतीर्दद्यात् पृथक् सामस्त्यतोऽपिवा ॥ 52
17.m: Likewise, regarding the divisions (kalā), mantras, words (pada), and letters (varṇa), the discerning [guru] / should offer three oblations each, either separately or collectively.

17.s:
tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ dattvā parayā vauṣaḍantayā /
aparāmantrataḥ śiṣyamuddhṛtyātmahṛdaṃ nayet // 53
17.d:
ततः पूर्णाहुतिं दत्त्वा परया वौषडन्तया ।
अपरामन्त्रतः शिष्यमुद्धृत्यात्महृदं नयेत् ॥ 53
17.m: Then, having offered the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti) with the Parā mantra ending in vauṣaṭ, / extracting the disciple with the Aparā mantra, he should bring him to his own heart.

17.s:
yadā tvekena śuddhena tadantarbhāvacintanāt /
na pṛthak śodhayettattvanāthasaṃśravaṇātparam // 54
17.d:
यदा त्वेकेन शुद्धेन तदन्तर्भावचिन्तनात् ।
न पृथक् शोधयेत्तत्त्वनाथसंश्रवणात्परम् ॥ 54
17.m: When, however, through meditating on their inclusion within that which is purified as one, / he does not purify separately after invoking the lord of the tattva,

17.s:
tadā pūrṇāṃ vitīryāṇumutkṣipyātmani yojayet /
tātsthyātmasaṃsthyayogāya tayaivāparayāhutīḥ // 55
17.d:
तदा पूर्णां वितीर्याणुमुत्क्षिप्यात्मनि योजयेत् ।
तात्स्थ्यात्मसंस्थ्ययोगाय तयैवापरयाहुतीः ॥ 55
17.m: then, offering the full oblation and raising the individual soul, he should unite it in himself. / In order to bring about its residing therein and resting in the self, with that very Aparā mantra

17.s:
sakarmapadayā dadyāditi kecittu manvate /
anye tu guravaḥ prāhurbhāvanāmayamīdṛśam // 56
17.d:
सकर्मपदया दद्यादिति केचित्तु मन्वते ।
अन्ये तु गुरवः प्राहुर्भावनामयमीदृशम् ॥ 56
17.m: he should offer oblations containing the accusative word—so some think. / Other gurus, however, declared that this is of the nature of imaginative contemplation (bhāvanā);

17.s:
nātra bāhyāhutirdeyā daiśikasya pṛthak punaḥ /
dadyādvā yadi no doṣaḥ syādupāyaḥ sa bhāvane // 57
17.d:
नात्र बाह्याहुतिर्देया दैशिकस्य पृथक् पुनः ।
दद्याद्वा यदि नो दोषः स्यादुपायः स भावने ॥ 57
17.m: an external oblation is not to be given here separately by the preceptor; / or if he should give it, there is no fault: it is a means for imaginative contemplation.

17.s:
evaṃ prāktanatātsthyātmasaṃsthatve yojayedguruḥ /
tataḥ śiṣyahṛdaṃ neyaḥ sa ātmā tāvato'dhvanaḥ // 58
17.d:
एवं प्राक्तनतात्स्थ्यात्मसंस्थत्वे योजयेद्गुरुः ।
ततः शिष्यहृदं नेयः स आत्मा तावतोऽध्वनः ॥ 58
17.m: Thus the guru should unite [it] into its prior state of residing therein and resting in the self. / Then that soul, purified of that portion of the path,

17.s:
śuddhastaddārḍhyasiddhyai ca pūrṇā syātparayā punaḥ /
mahāpāśupataṃ pūrvaṃ vilomasya viśuddhaye // 59
17.d:
शुद्धस्तद्दार्ढ्यसिद्ध्यै च पूर्णा स्यात्परया पुनः ।
महापाशुपतं पूर्वं विलोमस्य विशुद्धये ॥ 59
17.m: is to be led to the heart of the disciple; and for the attainment of firmness therein, there should again be a full oblation with Parā. / Saying first: 'I offer the oblation to the Great Pāśupata Weapon for the purification of what is inverted',

17.s:
juhomi punarastreṇa vauṣaḍanta iti kṣipet /
punaḥ pūrṇāṃ tato māyāmabhyarcyātha visarjayet // 60
17.d:
जुहोमि पुनरस्त्रेण वौषडन्त इति क्षिपेत् ।
पुनः पूर्णां ततो मायामभ्यर्च्याथ विसर्जयेत् ॥ 60
17.m: ending in vauṣaṭ, he should cast it with the Astra mantra. / Then again offering the full oblation, having worshipped Māyā, he should then dismiss her.

17.s:
dharātattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ sajjalena śuddharūpiṇā /
bhāvayenmiśritaṃ vāri śuddhiyogyaṃ tato bhavet // 61
17.d:
धरातत्त्वं विशुद्धं सज्जलेन शुद्धरूपिणा ।
भावयेन्मिश्रितं वारि शुद्धियोग्यं ततो भवेत् ॥ 61
17.m: One should contemplate the earth tattva, having been purified, as mingled with water whose nature is pure; / thence the water becomes suitable for purification.

17.s:
tathā tattatpurātattvamiśraṇāduttarottaram /
sarvā śivībhavettattvāvalī śuddhānyathā pṛthak // 62
17.d:
तथा तत्तत्पुरातत्त्वमिश्रणादुत्तरोत्तरम् ।
सर्वा शिवीभवेत्तत्त्वावली शुद्धान्यथा पृथक् ॥ 62
17.m: Likewise, by mixing with the preceding tattva consecutively, / the whole series of tattvas, being purified, becomes identified with Śiva; otherwise, [they remain] separate.

17.s:
pṛthaktvaṃ ca malo māyābhidhānastasya saṃbhave /
karmakṣaye'pi no muktirbhavedvidyeśvarādivat // 63
17.d:
पृथक्त्वं च मलो मायाभिधानस्तस्य संभवे ।
कर्मक्षयेऽपि नो मुक्तिर्भवेद्विद्येश्वरादिवत् ॥ 63
17.m: And separateness is the impurity named Māyā; when it exists, / even on the exhaustion of karma, there would be no liberation, as in the case of the lords of wisdom and the like.

17.s:
tato'pi jalatattvasya vahnau vyomni cidātmake /
āhvānādyakhilaṃ yāvattejasyasya vimaśraṇam // 64
17.d:
ततोऽपि जलतत्त्वस्य वह्नौ व्योम्नि चिदात्मके ।
आह्वानाद्यखिलं यावत्तेजस्यस्य विमश्रणम् ॥ 64
17.m: Then also, of the water-tattwa in the fire, in the sky whose nature is consciousness, / everything from invocation onward up to its reflective awareness in fire [should be performed].

17.s:
evaṃ kramātkalātattve śuddhe pāśaṃ bhujāśritam /
chindyātkalā hi sā kiṃcitkartṛtvonmīlanātmikā // 65
17.d:
एवं क्रमात्कलातत्त्वे शुद्धे पाशं भुजाश्रितम् ।
छिन्द्यात्कला हि सा किंचित्कर्तृत्वोन्मीलनात्मिका ॥ 65
17.m: In this way, when the principle of kalā has been purified in succession, one should sever the bond resting on the arm; / for kalā has the nature of unfolding limited agency. // 65

17.s:
karmākhyamalajṛmbhātmā taṃ ca granthiṃ srugagragam /
pūrṇāhutyā samaṃ vahnimantratejasi nirdahet // 66
17.d:
कर्माख्यमलजृम्भात्मा तं च ग्रन्थिं स्रुगग्रगम् ।
पूर्णाहुत्या समं वह्निमन्त्रतेजसि निर्दहेत् ॥ 66
17.m: And that knot, whose essence is the expansion of the impurity named karma, placed on the tip of the ladle, / he should burn completely together with the final oblation in the radiant energy of the fire-mantra. // 66

17.s:
mantro hi viśvarūpaḥ sannupāśrayavaśāttathā /
vyaktarūpastato vahnau pāśaploṣavidhāyakaḥ // 67
17.d:
मन्त्रो हि विश्वरूपः सन्नुपाश्रयवशात्तथा ।
व्यक्तरूपस्ततो वह्नौ पाशप्लोषविधायकः ॥ 67
17.m: For the mantra, being universal in form, likewise has an manifest form / by virtue of the support; therefore, in the fire, it effects the burning of the bonds. // 67

17.s:
pluṣṭo līnasvabhāvo'sau pāśastaṃ prati śambhuvat /
parameśamahātejaḥśeṣamātratvamaśnute // 68
17.d:
प्लुष्टो लीनस्वभावोऽसौ पाशस्तं प्रति शम्भुवत् ।
परमेशमहातेजःशेषमात्रत्वमश्नुते ॥ 68
17.m: Burnt, its nature dissolved, this bond regarding him, like Śambhu, / attains to being nothing but the remnant of the supreme Lord's great radiant energy. // 68

17.s:
karmapāśe'tra hotavye pūrṇayāsya śubhāśubham /
aśubhaṃ vā bhavadbhūtaṃ bhāvi vātha samastakam // 69
17.d:
कर्मपाशेऽत्र होतव्ये पूर्णयास्य शुभाशुभम् ।
अशुभं वा भवद्भूतं भावि वाथ समस्तकम् ॥ 69
17.m: Here, when the bond of karma is to be offered with the full oblation, its auspicious and inauspicious [effects], / or inauspicious, present, past, or future, or all [of them together], // 69

17.s:
dahāmi phaṭtrayaṃ vauṣaḍiti pūrṇāṃ vinikṣipet /
evaṃ māyāntasaṃśuddhau kaṇṭhapāśaṃ ca homayet // 70
17.d:
दहामि फट्त्रयं वौषडिति पूर्णां विनिक्षिपेत् ।
एवं मायान्तसंशुद्धौ कण्ठपाशं च होमयेत् ॥ 70
17.m: he should cast the full oblation, reciting: 'I burn, phaṭ, phaṭ, phaṭ, vauṣaṭ.' / Thus, upon the complete purification up to māyā, he should also offer the bond of the throat. // 70

17.s:
pūrṇasya tasya māyākhyaṃ pāśabhedaprathātmakam /
dahāmi phaṭtrayaṃ vauṣaḍiti pūrṇāṃ kṣipedguruḥ // 71
17.d:
पूर्णस्य तस्य मायाख्यं पाशभेदप्रथात्मकम् ।
दहामि फट्त्रयं वौषडिति पूर्णां क्षिपेद्गुरुः ॥ 71
17.m: Saying, 'I burn his [bond] named māyā, of the nature of the spread of differentiated bonds, of the full one, phaṭ, phaṭ, phaṭ, vauṣaṭ,' / the guru should cast the full oblation. // 71

17.s:
nirbījā yadi kāryā tu tadātraivāparāṃ kṣipet /
pūrṇāṃ samayapāśākhyabījadāhapadānvitām // 72
17.d:
निर्बीजा यदि कार्या तु तदात्रैवापरां क्षिपेत् ।
पूर्णां समयपाशाख्यबीजदाहपदान्विताम् ॥ 72
17.m: If, however, [an initiation] without seed is to be performed, then right here he should cast another / full oblation, accompanied by the words for burning the seed called the bond of the pledge. // 72

17.s:
gurau deve tathā śāstre bhaktiḥ kāryāsya nahyasau /
samayaḥ śaktipātasya svabhāvo hyeṣa no pṛthak // 73
17.d:
गुरौ देवे तथा शास्त्रे भक्तिः कार्यास्य नह्यसौ ।
समयः शक्तिपातस्य स्वभावो ह्येष नो पृथक् ॥ 73
17.m: Devotion to the guru, the deity, and the scripture must be maintained by him; for this is not / a pledge [imposed from outside], but the very nature of the descent of power, not something separate. // 73

17.s:
māyānte śuddhimāyāte vāgīśī yā purābhavat /
māyā śaktimayī saiva vidyāśaktitvamaśnute // 74
17.d:
मायान्ते शुद्धिमायाते वागीशी या पुराभवत् ।
माया शक्तिमयी सैव विद्याशक्तित्वमश्नुते ॥ 74
17.m: When purity is attained up to māyā, she who was previously Vāgīśī, / that very Māyā, consisting of power, attains the state of Vidyāśakti. // 74

17.s:
tacchuddhavidyāmāhūya vidyāśaktiṃ niyojayet /
evaṃ krameṇa saṃśuddhe sadāśivapade'pyalam // 75
17.d:
तच्छुद्धविद्यामाहूय विद्याशक्तिं नियोजयेत् ।
एवं क्रमेण संशुद्धे सदाशिवपदेऽप्यलम् ॥ 75
17.m: Having invoked her in Śuddhavidyā, he should unite Vidyāśakti; / thus, when the state of Sadāśiva also has been sufficiently purified in succession, // 75

17.s:
śikhāṃ granthiyutāṃ chittvā malamāṇavakaṃ dahet /
yato'dhikārabhogākhyau dvau pāśau tu sadāśive // 76
17.d:
शिखां ग्रन्थियुतां छित्त्वा मलमाणवकं दहेत् ।
यतोऽधिकारभोगाख्यौ द्वौ पाशौ तु सदाशिवे ॥ 76
17.m: having severed the tuft joined with the knot, he should burn the āṇava impurity; / for in Sadāśiva there are two bonds, named authority and enjoyment. // 76

17.s:
ityuktyāṇavapāśo'tra māyīyastu niśāvadhiḥ /
śiṣyo yathocitaṃ snāyādācāmeddaiśikaḥ svayam // 77
17.d:
इत्युक्त्याणवपाशोऽत्र मायीयस्तु निशावधिः ।
शिष्यो यथोचितं स्नायादाचामेद्दैशिकः स्वयम् ॥ 77
17.m: By this statement, here the āṇava bond [extends up to Sadāśiva], while the māyīya [bond] extends up to the night [of māyā]. / The disciple should bathe as appropriate, and the teacher should perform the sipping of water himself. // 77

17.s:
āṇavākhye vinirdagdhe hyadhovāhiśikhāmale /
tataḥ prāguktasakalaprameyaṃ paricintayan // 78
17.d:
आणवाख्ये विनिर्दग्धे ह्यधोवाहिशिखामले ।
ततः प्रागुक्तसकलप्रमेयं परिचिन्तयन् ॥ 78
17.m: When the impurity of the downward-flowing tuft, called āṇava, has been burned completely, / he then, contemplating the entire objective reality previously spoken of, // 78

17.s:
śiṣyadehādimātmīyadehaprāṇādiyojitam /
kṛtvātmadehaprāṇāderviśvamantaranusmaret // 79
17.d:
शिष्यदेहादिमात्मीयदेहप्राणादियोजितम् ।
कृत्वात्मदेहप्राणादेर्विश्वमन्तरनुस्मरेत् ॥ 79
17.m: having united the disciple's body and so forth with his own body, vital breath, and so forth, / should call to mind the universe inside his own body, vital breath, and so forth. // 79

17.s:
uktaprakriyayā caivaṃ dṛḍhabuddhirananyadhīḥ /
prāṇasthaṃ deśakālādhvayugaṃ prāṇaṃ ca śaktigam // 80
17.d:
उक्तप्रक्रियया चैवं दृढबुद्धिरनन्यधीः ।
प्राणस्थं देशकालाध्वयुगं प्राणं च शक्तिगम् ॥ 80
17.m: And in this way, by the prescribed procedure, with firm intellect and undivided mind, / [he contemplates] the pair of paths of space and time residing in the breath, and the breath residing in power; // 80

17.s:
tāṃ ca saṃvidgatāṃ śuddhāṃ saṃvidaṃ śivarūpiṇīm /
śiṣyasaṃvidabhinnāṃ ca mantravahnyādyabhedinīm // 81
17.d:
तां च संविद्गतां शुद्धां संविदं शिवरूपिणीम् ।
शिष्यसंविदभिन्नां च मन्त्रवह्न्याद्यभेदिनीम् ॥ 81
17.m: and that [power] residing in pure consciousness, consciousness whose form is Śiva, / non-different from the disciple's consciousness, and not different from the fire, the mantra, and so forth; // 81

17.s:
dhyāyan prāgvatprayogeṇa śivaṃ sakalaniṣkalam /
dvyātmakaṃ vā kṣipetpūrṇāṃ praśāntakaraṇena tu // 82
17.d:
ध्यायन् प्राग्वत्प्रयोगेण शिवं सकलनिष्कलम् ।
द्व्यात्मकं वा क्षिपेत्पूर्णां प्रशान्तकरणेन तु ॥ 82
17.m: meditating as before through the application upon Śiva as composite and impartite, / or dual in nature, he should cast the full oblation with tranquil instrument. // 82

17.s:
uktaṃ traiśirase tantre sarvasaṃpūraṇātmakam /
mūlādudayagatyā tu śivenduparisaṃplutam // 83
17.d:
उक्तं त्रैशिरसे तन्त्रे सर्वसंपूरणात्मकम् ।
मूलादुदयगत्या तु शिवेन्दुपरिसंप्लुतम् ॥ 83
17.m: It is stated in the Traiśirasa Tantra: 'whose essence is the complete filling of everything, / rising by the path of arising from the base, inundated with Śiva's moon, // 83

17.s:
janmāntamadhyakuharamūlasrotaḥsamutthitam /
śivārkaraśmibhistīvraiḥ kṣubdhaṃ jñānāmṛtaṃ tu yat // 84
17.d:
जन्मान्तमध्यकुहरमूलस्रोतःसमुत्थितम् ।
शिवार्करश्मिभिस्तीव्रैः क्षुब्धं ज्ञानामृतं तु यत् ॥ 84
17.m: arisen from the root-current in the central cavity up to the end of birth, / the nectar of knowledge which is agitated by the intense rays of the sun of Śiva— // 84

17.s:
tena saṃtarpayetsamyak praśāntakaraṇena tu /
śūnyadhāmābjamadhyasthaprabhākiraṇabhāsvaraḥ // 85
17.d:
तेन संतर्पयेत्सम्यक् प्रशान्तकरणेन तु ।
शून्यधामाब्जमध्यस्थप्रभाकिरणभास्वरः ॥ 85
17.m: with that he should satisfy thoroughly, with a tranquil instrument.' / Radiant with beams of light residing in the center of the lotus of the void-abode, // 85

17.s:
ādheyādhāraniḥspandabodhaśāstraparigrahaḥ /
janmādheyaprapañcaikasphoṭasaṃghaṭṭaghaṭṭanaḥ // 86
17.d:
आधेयाधारनिःस्पन्दबोधशास्त्रपरिग्रहः ।
जन्माधेयप्रपञ्चैकस्फोटसंघट्टघट्टनः ॥ 86
17.m: embracing the scripture of consciousness motionless in the supported and the support, / striking the clash of the single burst of the world that is the content of birth, // 86

17.s:
mūlasthānātsamārabhya kṛtvā someśamantagam /
khamivātiṣṭhate yāvatpraśāntaṃ tāvaducyate // 87
17.d:
मूलस्थानात्समारभ्य कृत्वा सोमेशमन्तगम् ।
खमिवातिष्ठते यावत्प्रशान्तं तावदुच्यते ॥ 87
17.m: beginning from the root place and making it reach the end of the lord of the moon, / as long as he remains like space, so long it is said to be tranquil. // 87

17.s:
uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca srucamāpūrya sarpiṣā /
kṛtvā śiṣyaṃ tathātmasthaṃ mūlamantramanusmaran // 88
17.d:
उक्तं श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे च स्रुचमापूर्य सर्पिषा ।
कृत्वा शिष्यं तथात्मस्थं मूलमन्त्रमनुस्मरन् ॥ 88
17.m: And it is stated in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra: 'Filling the ladle with ghee, / and placing the disciple in oneself, recollecting the root mantra, // 88

17.s:
śivaṃ śaktiṃ tathātmānaṃ śiṣyaṃ sarpistathānalam /
ekīkurvañchanairgaccheddvādaśāntamananyadhīḥ // 89
17.d:
शिवं शक्तिं तथात्मानं शिष्यं सर्पिस्तथानलम् ।
एकीकुर्वञ्छनैर्गच्छेद्द्वादशान्तमनन्यधीः ॥ 89
17.m: unifying Śiva, power, himself, the disciple, the ghee, and the fire, / he should go slowly to the dvādaśānta with undivided mind. // 89

17.s:
tatra kumbhakamāsthāya dhyāyansakalaniṣkalam /
tiṣṭhettāvadanudvigno yāvadājyakṣayo bhvet // 90
17.d:
तत्र कुम्भकमास्थाय ध्यायन्सकलनिष्कलम् ।
तिष्ठेत्तावदनुद्विग्नो यावदाज्यक्षयो भ्वेत् ॥ 90
17.m: Having adopted breath retention there, meditating on the composite and impartite, / he should remain unagitated as long as the ghee is consumed.' // 90

17.s:
evaṃ yuktaḥ pare tattve guruṇā śivamūrtinā /
na bhūyaḥ paśutāmeti dagdhamāyānibandhanaḥ // 91
17.d:
एवं युक्तः परे तत्त्वे गुरुणा शिवमूर्तिना ।
न भूयः पशुतामेति दग्धमायानिबन्धनः ॥ 91
17.m: Joined thus to the supreme reality by the guru, who is the embodiment of Śiva, / with the fetter of māyā burned away, he does not again lapse into soulhood. // 91

17.s:
dehapāte punaḥ prepsedyadi tattveṣu kutracit /
bhogān samastavyastatvabhedairante paraṃ padam // 92
17.d:
देहपाते पुनः प्रेप्सेद्यदि तत्त्वेषु कुत्रचित् ।
भोगान् समस्तव्यस्तत्वभेदैरन्ते परं पदम् ॥ 92
17.m: If, at the fall of the body, he should again desire enjoyments in some of the principles / through the divisions of collective and individual states, and at the end the supreme state, // 92

17.s:
tadā tattattvabhūmau tu tatsaṃkhyāyāmananyadhīḥ /
punaryojanikāṃ kuryātpūrṇāhutyantareṇa tu // 93
17.d:
तदा तत्तत्त्वभूमौ तु तत्संख्यायामनन्यधीः ।
पुनर्योजनिकां कुर्यात्पूर्णाहुत्यन्तरेण तु ॥ 93
17.m: then on the level of each respective principle, in that number, with undivided mind, / he should perform a re-union by means of a full oblation. // 93

17.s:
muktipradā bhogamokṣapradā vā yā prakīrtitā /
dīkṣā sā syātsabījatvanirbījātmatayā dvidhā // 94
17.d:
मुक्तिप्रदा भोगमोक्षप्रदा वा या प्रकीर्तिता ।
दीक्षा सा स्यात्सबीजत्वनिर्बीजात्मतया द्विधा ॥ 94
17.m: That initiation which is proclaimed as bestowing liberation or bestowing enjoyment and liberation / is twofold: possessing seed or being without seed. // 94

17.s:
bāle nirjñātamaraṇe tvaśakte vā jarādibhiḥ /
kāryā nirbījikā dīkṣā śaktipātabalodaye // 95
17.d:
बाले निर्ज्ञातमरणे त्वशक्ते वा जरादिभिः ।
कार्या निर्बीजिका दीक्षा शक्तिपातबलोदये ॥ 95
17.m: For a child, for one whose death is known [to be near], or for one incapable due to old age and the like, / an initiation without seed should be performed when the power of the descent of power has arisen. // 95

17.s:
nirbījāyāṃ sāmayāṃstu pāśānapi viśodhayet /
kṛtanirbījadīkṣastu devāgnigurubhaktibhāk // 96
17.d:
निर्बीजायां सामयांस्तु पाशानपि विशोधयेत् ।
कृतनिर्बीजदीक्षस्तु देवाग्निगुरुभक्तिभाक् ॥ 96
17.m: In the [initiation] without seed, however, he should purify even the bonds consisting of pledges. / But one who has received the initiation without seed possesses devotion to the deity, fire, and guru; // 96

17.s:
iyataiva śivaṃ yāyāt sadyo bhogān vibhujya vā /
śrīmaddīkṣottare coktaṃ cāre ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule // 97
17.d:
इयतैव शिवं यायात् सद्यो भोगान् विभुज्य वा ।
श्रीमद्दीक्षोत्तरे चोक्तं चारे षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुले ॥ 97
17.m: by this much alone he would attain Śiva, either immediately or having experienced enjoyments. / And it is stated in the venerable Dīkṣottara: 'In the movement of thirty-six fingers, // 97

17.s:
tattvānyāpādamūrdhāntaṃ bhuvanāni tyajetkramāt /
tuṭimātraṃ niṣkalaṃ tadadehaṃ tadahaṃparam // 98
17.d:
तत्त्वान्यापादमूर्धान्तं भुवनानि त्यजेत्क्रमात् ।
तुटिमात्रं निष्कलं तददेहं तदहंपरम् ॥ 98
17.m: he should successively abandon the principles and worlds from foot to crown; / that impartite [state] of merely a moment, bodiless, is beyond the ego. // 98

17.s:
śaktyā tatra kṣipāmyenamiti dhyāyaṃstu dīkṣayet /
sabījāyāṃ tu dīkṣāyāṃ samayānna viśodhayet // 99
17.d:
शक्त्या तत्र क्षिपाम्येनमिति ध्यायंस्तु दीक्षयेत् ।
सबीजायां तु दीक्षायां समयान्न विशोधयेत् ॥ 99
17.m: Meditating, "I cast him there by means of power," he should initiate.' / In the initiation with seed, however, he should not purify the pledges. // 99

17.s:
viśeṣastvayametasyāṃ yāvajjīvaṃ śiśorguruḥ /
śeṣavṛttyai śuddhatattvasṛṣṭiṃ kurvīta pūrṇayā // 100
17.d:
विशेषस्त्वयमेतस्यां यावज्जीवं शिशोर्गुरुः ।
शेषवृत्त्यै शुद्धतत्त्वसृष्टिं कुर्वीत पूर्णया ॥ 100
17.m: This, however, is the distinction in this case: for the duration of the child's life, the guru, / for the functioning of the remainder, should bring about the creation of pure principles by means of the full oblation. // 100

17.s:
abhinnācchivasaṃbodhajaladheryugapatsphurat /
pūrṇāṃ kṣipaṃstattvajālaṃ dhyāyedbhārūpakaṃ sṛtam // 101
17.d:
अभिन्नाच्छिवसंबोधजलधेर्युगपत्स्फुरत् ।
पूर्णां क्षिपंस्तत्त्वजालं ध्यायेद्भारूपकं सृतम् ॥ 101
17.m: Pouring the full oblation, he should meditate on the network of principles emitted as light-formed, / pulsing simultaneously from the ocean of consciousness that is non-different from Śiva. // 101

17.s:
viśuddhatattvasṛṣṭiṃ vā kuryātkumbhābhiṣecanāt /
tathā dhyānabalādeva yadvā pūrṇābhiṣecanaiḥ // 102
17.d:
विशुद्धतत्त्वसृष्टिं वा कुर्यात्कुम्भाभिषेचनात् ।
तथा ध्यानबलादेव यद्वा पूर्णाभिषेचनैः ॥ 102
17.m: Or he may bring about the creation of purified principles by consecration from the pot, / likewise through the power of meditation alone, or by full consecrations. // 102

17.s:
pṛthivī sthirarūpāsya śivarūpeṇa bhāvitā /
sthirīkaroti tāmeva bhāvanāmiti śuddhyati // 103
17.d:
पृथिवी स्थिररूपास्य शिवरूपेण भाविता ।
स्थिरीकरोति तामेव भावनामिति शुद्ध्यति ॥ 103
17.m: Earth, having a stable form, cultivated by him as having the form of Śiva, / stabilizes that very contemplation; thus it becomes purified. // 103

17.s:
jalamāpyāyayatyenāṃ tejo bhāsvaratāṃ nayet /
marudānandasaṃsparśaṃ vyoma vaitatyamāvahet // 104
17.d:
जलमाप्याययत्येनां तेजो भास्वरतां नयेत् ।
मरुदानन्दसंस्पर्शं व्योम वैतत्यमावहेत् ॥ 104
17.m: Water replenishes it; fire brings it to radiance; / wind brings about the touch of bliss; space brings about vastness. // 104

17.s:
evaṃ tanmātravargo'pi śivatāmaya iṣyate /
parānandamahāvyāptiraśeṣamalavicyutiḥ // 105
17.d:
एवं तन्मात्रवर्गोऽपि शिवतामय इष्यते ।
परानन्दमहाव्याप्तिरशेषमलविच्युतिः ॥ 105
17.m: In this way the group of subtle elements also is held to consist of Śiva-nature, / being the great pervasion of supreme bliss and the fall of all impurities without remainder. // 105

17.s:
śive gantṛtvamādānamupādeyaśivastutiḥ /
śivāmodabharāsvādadarśanasparśanānyalam // 106
17.d:
शिवे गन्तृत्वमादानमुपादेयशिवस्तुतिः ।
शिवामोदभरास्वाददर्शनस्पर्शनान्यलम् ॥ 106
17.m: Movement toward Śiva, taking up what is to be accepted, praising Śiva, / savoring the mass of Śiva's fragrance, seeing, touching, // 106

17.s:
tadākarṇanamityevamindriyāṇāṃ viśuddhatā /
saṃkalpādhyavasāmānāḥ prakāśo raktisaṃsthitī // 107
17.d:
तदाकर्णनमित्येवमिन्द्रियाणां विशुद्धता ।
संकल्पाध्यवसामानाः प्रकाशो रक्तिसंस्थिती ॥ 107
17.m: and hearing that: such is the complete purity of the sense organs. / The fact that resolution, ascertainment, pride, illumination, attachment, and stabilization // 107

17.s:
śivātmatvena yatseyaṃ śuddhatā mānasādike /
niyamo rañjanaṃ kartṛbhāvaḥ kalanayā saha // 108
17.d:
शिवात्मत्वेन यत्सेयं शुद्धता मानसादिके ।
नियमो रञ्जनं कर्तृभावः कलनया सह ॥ 108
17.m: are possessed of the nature of Śiva—that is this purity in the mind and so forth. / Restriction, coloring, agency together with measurement, // 108

17.s:
vedanaṃ heyavastvaṃśaviṣaye suptakalpatā /
itthaṃ śivaikyarūḍhasya ṣaṭkañcukagaṇo'pyayam // 109
17.d:
वेदनं हेयवस्त्वंशविषये सुप्तकल्पता ।
इत्थं शिवैक्यरूढस्य षट्कञ्चुकगणोऽप्ययम् ॥ 109
17.m: experience, and a state resembling sleep with regard to the domain of things to be rejected: / in this way, for one established in unity with Śiva, even this group of six cuirasses // 109

17.s:
śuddha eva pumān prāptaśivabhāvo viśuddhyati /
vidyeśādiṣu tattveṣu naiva kācidaśuddhatā // 110
17.d:
शुद्ध एव पुमान् प्राप्तशिवभावो विशुद्ध्यति ।
विद्येशादिषु तत्त्वेषु नैव काचिदशुद्धता ॥ 110
17.m: is pure indeed; the person who has attained the state of Śiva becomes thoroughly pure. / In principles such as Vidyeśa, there is no impurity whatsoever. // 110

17.s:
ityevaṃ śuddhatattvānāṃ sṛṣṭyā śiṣyo'pi tanmayaḥ /
bhaveddhyetatsūcitaṃ śrīmālinīvijayottare // 111
17.d:
इत्येवं शुद्धतत्त्वानां सृष्ट्या शिष्योऽपि तन्मयः ।
भवेद्ध्येतत्सूचितं श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे ॥ 111
17.m:
In this way, through the emanation of the pure principles, the disciple also becomes identical with that;
for this has been indicated in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara: // 111

17.s:
bandhamokṣāvubhāvetāvindriyāṇi jagurbudhāḥ /
nigṛhītāni bandhāya vimuktāni vimuktaye // 112
17.d:
बन्धमोक्षावुभावेताविन्द्रियाणि जगुर्बुधाः ।
निगृहीतानि बन्धाय विमुक्तानि विमुक्तये ॥ 112
17.m:
