"The wise have proclaimed both these—bondage and liberation—to be the senses:
restrained, they lead to bondage; liberated, they lead to liberation. // 112

17.s:
etāni vyāpake bhāve yadā syurmanasā saha /
muktāni kvāpi viṣaye rodhādbandhāya tāni tu // 113
17.d:
एतानि व्यापके भावे यदा स्युर्मनसा सह ।
मुक्तानि क्वापि विषये रोधाद्बन्धाय तानि तु ॥ 113
17.m:
When these, along with the mind, are engaged in the all-pervasive reality,
they are liberated; but because of obstruction in any [limited] object, they lead to bondage." // 113

17.s:
ityevaṃ dvividho bhāvaḥ śuddhāśuddhaprabhedataḥ /
indriyāṇāṃ samākhyātaḥ siddhayogīśvare mate // 114
17.d:
इत्येवं द्विविधो भावः शुद्धाशुद्धप्रभेदतः ।
इन्द्रियाणां समाख्यातः सिद्धयोगीश्वरे मते ॥ 114
17.m:
In this way, the twofold nature of the senses according to the division between pure and impure
has been taught in the doctrine of the Siddhayogīśvarī[mata]. // 114

17.s:
śrīmān vidyāgurustvāha pramāṇastutidarśane /
samastamantrairdīkṣāyāṃ niyamastveṣa kathyate // 115
17.d:
श्रीमान् विद्यागुरुस्त्वाह प्रमाणस्तुतिदर्शने ।
समस्तमन्त्रैर्दीक्षायां नियमस्त्वेष कथ्यते ॥ 115
17.m:
The venerable guru of the Vidyā, however, said in the Pramāṇastutidarśana:
"This rule is proclaimed in initiation performed with all mantras: // 115

17.s:
māyāntaśuddhau sarvāḥ syuḥ kriyā hyaparayā sadā /
dvyātmayā sakalānte tu niṣkale parayaiva tu // 116
17.d:
मायान्तशुद्धौ सर्वाः स्युः क्रिया ह्यपरया सदा ।
द्व्यात्मया सकलान्ते तु निष्कले परयैव तु ॥ 116
17.m:
In the purification up to māyā, all actions should always be performed with the lower [mantra];
with the two-fold [intermediate mantra] up to the composite [level]; but in the partless [realm], only with the supreme [mantra]. // 116

17.s:
īśānte ca pivanyādi sakalānte'ṅgapañcakam /
ityevaṃvidhimālocya karma kuryādgurūttamaḥ // 117
17.d:
ईशान्ते च पिवन्यादि सकलान्तेऽङ्गपञ्चकम् ।
इत्येवंविधिमालोच्य कर्म कुर्याद्गुरूत्तमः ॥ 117
17.m:
And up to Īśāna, [the mantras] beginning with pivani; at the end of the composite [level], the group of five limbs."—
Having reflected on such a rule, the best of gurus should perform the rite. // 117

17.s:
purādhvani hutīnāṃ yā saṃkhyeyaṃ tattvavarṇayoḥ /
tāmeva dviguṇīkuryātpadādhvani caturguṇām // 118
17.d:
पुराध्वनि हुतीनां या संख्येयं तत्त्ववर्णयोः ।
तामेव द्विगुणीकुर्यात्पदाध्वनि चतुर्गुणाम् ॥ 118
17.m:
Whatever is the count of oblations in the path of the cities for the principles and the phonemes,
one should double that in the path of the words, and quadruple it [in the next]. // 118

17.s:
kramānmantrakalāmārge dviguṇā dviguṇā kramāt /
yāvattritattvasaṃśuddhau syādviṃśatiguṇā tataḥ // 119
17.d:
क्रमान्मन्त्रकलामार्गे द्विगुणा द्विगुणा क्रमात् ।
यावत्त्रितत्त्वसंशुद्धौ स्याद्विंशतिगुणा ततः ॥ 119
17.m:
Progressively in the path of mantras and kalās, it is doubled and doubled again in sequence,
until, in the purification of the three principles, it becomes twentyfold from that. // 119

17.s:
pratikarma bhavetṣaṣṭirāhutīnāṃ tritattvake /
ekatattve śataṃ prāhurāhutīnāṃ tu sāṣṭakam // 120
17.d:
प्रतिकर्म भवेत्षष्टिराहुतीनां त्रितत्त्वके ।
एकतत्त्वे शतं प्राहुराहुतीनां तु साष्टकम् ॥ 120
17.m:
For each rite in the triad of principles, there should be sixty oblations;
for a single principle, however, they state one hundred and eight oblations. // 120

17.s:
vilomakarmaṇā sākaṃ yāḥ pūrṇāhutayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
tāsāṃ sarvādhvasaṃśuddhau saṃkhyānyatvaṃ na kiṃcana // 121
17.d:
विलोमकर्मणा साकं याः पूर्णाहुतयः स्मृताः ।
तासां सर्वाध्वसंशुद्धौ संख्यान्यत्वं न किंचन ॥ 121
17.m:
As for the full oblations that are prescribed together with the reverse ritual action,
in their case, there is no difference in number across the purification of all the paths. // 121

17.s: ityeṣā kathitā dīkṣā jananādisamanvitā // 122
17.d: इत्येषा कथिता दीक्षा जननादिसमन्विता ॥ 122
17.m: Thus has this initiation endowed with [the rites of] birth and so forth been proclaimed. // 122

18.s:
atha saṃkṣiptadīkṣeyaṃ śivatāpattidocyate /
na rajo nādhivāso'tra na bhūkṣetraparigrahaḥ /
yatra tatra pradeśe tu pūjayitvā guruḥ śivam // 1
18.d:
अथ संक्षिप्तदीक्षेयं शिवतापत्तिदोच्यते ।
न रजो नाधिवासोऽत्र न भूक्षेत्रपरिग्रहः ।
यत्र तत्र प्रदेशे तु पूजयित्वा गुरुः शिवम् ॥ 1

18.s:
adhvānaṃ manasā dhyātvā dīkṣayettattvapāragaḥ /
jananādivihīnāṃ tu yena yenādhvanā guruḥ // 2
18.d:
अध्वानं मनसा ध्यात्वा दीक्षयेत्तत्त्वपारगः ।
जननादिविहीनां तु येन येनाध्वना गुरुः ॥ 2
18.m:
and contemplating the path with his mind, the guru who has crossed to the farther shore of the principles should initiate [him].
Devoid of [the rites of] birth and so forth, through whatever path the guru // 2

18.s:
kuryātsa ekatattvāntāṃ śivabhāvaikabhāvitaḥ /
parāmantrastato'syeti tattvaṃ saṃśodhayāmyatha // 3
18.d:
कुर्यात्स एकतत्त्वान्तां शिवभावैकभावितः ।
परामन्त्रस्ततोऽस्येति तत्त्वं संशोधयाम्यथ ॥ 3
18.m:
should perform it, terminating in a single principle, infused solely with the state of Śiva;
from that, [using] the Parā mantra: "Now I purify the principle belonging to him, // 3

18.s:
svāheti pratitattvaṃ syācchuddhe pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet /
evaṃ mantrāntaraiḥ kuryātsamastairathavoktavat // 4
18.d:
स्वाहेति प्रतितत्त्वं स्याच्छुद्धे पूर्णाहुतिं क्षिपेत् ।
एवं मन्त्रान्तरैः कुर्यात्समस्तैरथवोक्तवत् ॥ 4
18.m:
svāhā!"—such should be done for each principle; when it is purified, he should offer the full oblation.
In this way he may perform it with other mantras, or with all of them as described. // 4

18.s:
parāsaṃpuṭitaṃ nāma svāhāntaṃ prathamāntakam /
śataṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭaṃ vā tena śaktyaiva homayet // 5
18.d:
परासंपुटितं नाम स्वाहान्तं प्रथमान्तकम् ।
शतं सहस्रं साष्टं वा तेन शक्त्यैव होमयेत् ॥ 5
18.m:
[Reciting] the name enveloped by Parā, ending in svāhā and with the nominative ending,
one should offer into the fire with that very power: one hundred, one thousand, or one hundred and eight times. // 5

18.s:
tataḥ pūrṇeti saṃśodhyahīnamuttamamīdṛśam /
dīkṣākarmoditaṃ tatra tatra śāstre maheśinā // 6
18.d:
ततः पूर्णेति संशोध्यहीनमुत्तममीदृशम् ।
दीक्षाकर्मोदितं तत्र तत्र शास्त्रे महेशिना ॥ 6
18.m:
Then, having [offered] the full oblation, this highest initiation rite, devoid of that which is to be purified,
has been proclaimed here and there in the scripture by the Great Lord. // 6

18.s:
pratyekaṃ mātṛkāyugmavarṇaistattvāni śodhayet /
yadi vā piṇḍamantreṇa sarvamantreṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ // 7
18.d:
प्रत्येकं मातृकायुग्मवर्णैस्तत्त्वानि शोधयेत् ।
यदि वा पिण्डमन्त्रेण सर्वमन्त्रेष्वयं विधिः ॥ 7
18.m:
One should purify the principles individually with the pairs of phonemes of the Mātṛkā,
or else with the piṇḍa-mantra; this rule applies to all mantras. // 7

18.s:
yathā yathā ca svabhyastajñānastanmayatātmakaḥ /
gurustathā tathā kuryāt saṃkṣiptaṃ karma nānyathā // 8
18.d:
यथा यथा च स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानस्तन्मयतात्मकः ।
गुरुस्तथा तथा कुर्यात् संक्षिप्तं कर्म नान्यथा ॥ 8
18.m:
To whatever extent the guru has mastered knowledge and has become identical with that [reality],
to that extent he should perform the condensed rite, not otherwise. // 8

18.s:
śrībrahmayāmale coktaṃ saṃkṣipte'pi hi bhāvayet /
vyāptiṃ sarvādhvasāmānyāṃ kiṃtu yāge na vistaraḥ // 9
18.d:
श्रीब्रह्मयामले चोक्तं संक्षिप्तेऽपि हि भावयेत् ।
व्याप्तिं सर्वाध्वसामान्यां किंतु यागे न विस्तरः ॥ 9
18.m:
And in the venerable Brahmayāmala it is said: "Even in a condensed [rite], one should indeed contemplate
the pervasive presence common to all the paths; however, in the sacrifice there is no elaboration." // 9

18.s:
atanmayībhūtamiti vikṣiptaṃ karma sandadhat /
kramāttādātmyametīti vikṣiptaṃ vidhimācaret // 10
18.d:
अतन्मयीभूतमिति विक्षिप्तं कर्म सन्दधत् ।
क्रमात्तादात्म्यमेतीति विक्षिप्तं विधिमाचरेत् ॥ 10
18.m:
Maintaining the rite in an expanded form because he has not yet become identical with that [reality],
one should perform the expanded procedure, [reflecting] that through succession he attains identity with it. // 10

18.s:
saṃkṣipto vidhirukto'yaṃ kṛpayā yaḥ śivoditaḥ /
dīkṣottare kairaṇe ca tatra tatrāpi śāsane // 11
18.d:
संक्षिप्तो विधिरुक्तोऽयं कृपया यः शिवोदितः ।
दीक्षोत्तरे कैरणे च तत्र तत्रापि शासने ॥ 11
18.m:
This condensed procedure has been declared out of grace, which was taught by Śiva
in the Dīkṣottara, in the Kiraṇa, and in various other teachings. // 11

19.s:
atha sadyaḥsamutkrāntipradā dīkṣā nirūpyate /
tatkṣaṇāccopabhogādvā dehapāte śivaṃ vrajet /
ityuktyā mālinīśāstre sūcitāsau maheśinā // 1
19.d:
अथ सद्यःसमुत्क्रान्तिप्रदा दीक्षा निरूप्यते ।
तत्क्षणाच्चोपभोगाद्वा देहपाते शिवं व्रजेत् ।
इत्युक्त्या मालिनीशास्त्रे सूचितासौ महेशिना ॥ 1
19.m:
Now the initiation that bestows immediate departure is set forth.
"Either immediately or from enjoyment, at the fall of the body he reaches Śiva"—
by this statement it was indicated by the Great Lord in the Mālinī text. // 1

19.s:
dehapāte samīpasthe śaktipātasphuṭatvataḥ /
āsādya śāṃkarīṃ dīkṣāṃ tasmāddīkṣākṣaṇātparam // 2
19.d:
देहपाते समीपस्थे शक्तिपातस्फुटत्वतः ।
आसाद्य शांकरीं दीक्षां तस्माद्दीक्षाक्षणात्परम् ॥ 2
19.m:
When the fall of the body is imminent, because of the manifestation of descent of power,
having received the initiation of Śaṅkara, immediately after that moment of initiation // 2

19.s:
śivaṃ vrajedityartho'tra pūrvāparavivecanāt /
vyākhyātaḥ śrīmatāsmākaṃ guruṇā śambhumūrtinā // 3
19.d:
शिवं व्रजेदित्यर्थोऽत्र पूर्वापरविवेचनात् ।
व्याख्यातः श्रीमतास्माकं गुरुणा शम्भुमूर्तिना ॥ 3
19.m:
he goes to Śiva—this is the meaning here, established by examining the context,
as explained by our venerable guru, an embodiment of Śambhu. // 3

19.s:
yadā hyāsannamaraṇe śaktipātaḥ prajāyate /
tatra mande'tha gurvādisevayāyuḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet // 4
19.d:
यदा ह्यासन्नमरणे शक्तिपातः प्रजायते ।
तत्र मन्देऽथ गुर्वादिसेवयायुः क्षयं व्रजेत् ॥ 4
19.m:
For when descent of power occurs at imminent death,
if it is weak there, then through service to the guru and so forth, his lifespan may be exhausted; // 4

19.s:
athavā bandhumitrādidvārā sāsya vibhoḥ patet /
pūrvaṃ vā samayī naiva parāṃ dīkṣāmavāptavān // 5
19.d:
अथवा बन्धुमित्रादिद्वारा सास्य विभोः पतेत् ।
पूर्वं वा समयी नैव परां दीक्षामवाप्तवान् ॥ 5
19.m:
or it may fall upon him from the all-pervading Lord through the medium of kin, friends, and others;
or previously he was an initiate into the rule who had not obtained the supreme initiation; // 5

19.s:
āptadīkṣo'pi vā prāṇāñjihāsuḥ kleśavarjitam /
antyāngurustadā kuryātsadya+utkrāntidīkṣaṇam // 6
19.d:
आप्तदीक्षोऽपि वा प्राणाञ्जिहासुः क्लेशवर्जितम् ।
अन्त्यान्गुरुस्तदा कुर्यात्सद्य+उत्क्रान्तिदीक्षणम् ॥ 6
19.m:
or, even though he has received initiation, he wishes to abandon his life-breaths free of affliction—
then, in his final moments, the guru should perform the initiation of immediate departure. // 6

19.s:
natvapakvamale nāpi śeṣakārmikavigrahe /
kuryādutkramaṇaṃ śrīmadgahvare ca nirūpitam // 7
19.d:
नत्वपक्वमले नापि शेषकार्मिकविग्रहे ।
कुर्यादुत्क्रमणं श्रीमद्गह्वरे च निरूपितम् ॥ 7
19.m:
Not, however, when the impurity is unripened, nor when karmic residues remain for the body,
should one perform departure, as explained in the venerable Gahvara: // 7

19.s:
dṛṣṭvā śiṣyaṃ jarāgrastaṃ vyādhinā paripīḍitam /
utkramayya tatastvenaṃ paratattve niyojayet // 8
19.d:
दृष्ट्वा शिष्यं जराग्रस्तं व्याधिना परिपीडितम् ।
उत्क्रमय्य ततस्त्वेनं परतत्त्वे नियोजयेत् ॥ 8
19.m:
"Having seen a disciple seized by old age or severely afflicted by disease,
having then caused him to depart, one should unite him with the supreme principle." // 8

19.s:
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatve kāmacāravidhānataḥ /
pūrvoktamarthajātaṃ śrīśambhunātra nirūpitam // 9
19.d:
विशेषणविशेष्यत्वे कामचारविधानतः ।
पूर्वोक्तमर्थजातं श्रीशम्भुनात्र निरूपितम् ॥ 9
19.m:
Because of the rule of acting at will regarding whether this is a qualifier or the thing qualified,
the entire meaning stated before has been determined here by the venerable Śambhu[nātha]. // 9

19.s:
vidhiṃ pūrvoditaṃ sarvaṃ kṛtvā samayaśuddhitaḥ /
kṣurikāmasya vinyasyejjvalantīṃ marmakartarīm // 10
19.d:
विधिं पूर्वोदितं सर्वं कृत्वा समयशुद्धितः ।
क्षुरिकामस्य विन्यस्येज्ज्वलन्तीं मर्मकर्तरीम् ॥ 10
19.m:
Having performed all the procedure previously stated up to the purification of the rule,
he should place upon him the kṣurikā, the blazing cutter of vital spots. // 10

19.s:
kṛtvā pūrvoditaṃ nyāsaṃ kālānalasamaprabham /
saṃhṛtikramataḥ sārdhaṃ sṛkchindiyugalena tu // 11
19.d:
कृत्वा पूर्वोदितं न्यासं कालानलसमप्रभम् ।
संहृतिक्रमतः सार्धं सृक्छिन्दियुगलेन तु ॥ 11
19.m:
Having performed the previously stated placement of mantras, radiant as the fire of time,
according to the order of reabsorption, together with the pair "sṛk-chindi", // 11

19.s:
āgneyīṃ dhāraṇāṃ kṛtvā sarvamarmapratāpanīm /
pūrayedvāyunā dehamaṅguṣṭhānmastakāntakam // 12
19.d:
आग्नेयीं धारणां कृत्वा सर्वमर्मप्रतापनीम् ।
पूरयेद्वायुना देहमङ्गुष्ठान्मस्तकान्तकम् ॥ 12
19.m:
and having executed the fiery retention that scorches all the vital spots,
he should fill the body with air from the big toe to the head. // 12

19.s:
tamutkṛṣya tato'ṅguṣṭhādūrdhvāntaṃ vakṣyamāṇayā /
kṛntenmarmāṇi randhrāntāt kālarātryā visarjayet // 13
19.d:
तमुत्कृष्य ततोऽङ्गुष्ठादूर्ध्वान्तं वक्ष्यमाणया ।
कृन्तेन्मर्माणि रन्ध्रान्तात् कालरात्र्या विसर्जयेत् ॥ 13
19.m:
Having drawn that [breath] up from the big toe to the summit by the means to be explained,
he should sever the vital spots, and release [the breath] through the aperture by means of Kālarātrī. // 13

19.s:
anena kramayogena yojito hutivarjitaḥ /
samayyapyeti tāṃ dīkṣāmiti śrīmālinīmate // 14
19.d:
अनेन क्रमयोगेन योजितो हुतिवर्जितः ।
समय्यप्येति तां दीक्षामिति श्रीमालिनीमते ॥ 14
19.m:
United by this sequential method, devoid of fire-oblations,
even an initiate into the rule attains that initiation; thus is it in the doctrine of the venerable Mālinī. // 14

19.s:
ṣoḍaśādhāraṣaṭcakralakṣyatrayakhapañcakāt /
kvacidanyataratrātha prāguktapaśukarmavat // 15
19.d:
षोडशाधारषट्चक्रलक्ष्यत्रयखपञ्चकात् ।
क्वचिदन्यतरत्राथ प्रागुक्तपशुकर्मवत् ॥ 15
19.m:
From the sixteen supports, the six centres, the three targets, or the five spaces,
in any one of them, just as in the previously described rite for the bound soul, // 15

19.s:
praviśya mūlaṃ kandādeśchindannaikyavibhāvanāt /
pūrṇāhutiprayogeṇa sveṣṭe dhāmni niyojayet // 16
19.d:
प्रविश्य मूलं कन्दादेश्छिन्दन्नैक्यविभावनात् ।
पूर्णाहुतिप्रयोगेण स्वेष्टे धाम्नि नियोजयेत् ॥ 16
19.m:
having entered the root of the bulb and so on, severing [bonds] through the contemplation of oneness,
by the application of the full oblation he should unite [him] with the desired abode. // 16

19.s:
jñānatriśūlaṃ saṃdīptaṃ dīptacakratrayojjvalam /
cintayitvāmunā tasya vedanaṃ bodhanaṃ bhramam // 17
19.d:
ज्ञानत्रिशूलं संदीप्तं दीप्तचक्रत्रयोज्ज्वलम् ।
चिन्तयित्वामुना तस्य वेदनं बोधनं भ्रमम् ॥ 17
19.m:
Having visualised the blazing trident of knowledge, radiant with three glowing wheels,
with it he should cause the piercing, awakening, rotating, // 17

19.s:
dīpanaṃ tāḍanaṃ todaṃ calanaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ /
kandādicakragaṃ kuryādviśeṣeṇa hṛdambuje // 18
19.d:
दीपनं ताडनं तोदं चलनं च पुनः पुनः ।
कन्दादिचक्रगं कुर्याद्विशेषेण हृदम्बुजे ॥ 18
19.m:
kindling, striking, pricking, and shaking of him again and again,
operating in the centres beginning with the bulb, especially in the lotus of the heart. // 18

19.s:
dvādaśānte tataḥ kṛtvā binduyugmagate kṣipet /
nirlakṣye vā pare dhāmni saṃyuktaḥ parameśvaraḥ // 19
19.d:
द्वादशान्ते ततः कृत्वा बिन्दुयुग्मगते क्षिपेत् ।
निर्लक्ष्ये वा परे धाम्नि संयुक्तः परमेश्वरः ॥ 19
19.m:
Then, having brought [him] to the twelve-finger space, he should project [him] into that which has reached the pair of drops,
or into the supreme targetless abode, united [with it], the Supreme Lord. // 19

19.s:
na tasya kuryātsaṃskāraṃ kaṃcidityāha gahvare /
devaḥ kimasya pūrṇasya śrāddhādyairiti bhāvitaḥ // 20
19.d:
न तस्य कुर्यात्संस्कारं कंचिदित्याह गह्वरे ।
देवः किमस्य पूर्णस्य श्राद्धाद्यैरिति भावितः ॥ 20
19.m:
"One should not perform any post-mortem rite for him," thus said the Lord in the Gahvara;
meditated upon as full, what need has he of ancestral rites and the like? // 20

19.s:
śrīmaddīkṣottare tveṣa vidhirvahnipuṭīkṛtaḥ /
haṃsaḥ pumānadhastasya rudrabindusamanvitaḥ // 21
19.d:
श्रीमद्दीक्षोत्तरे त्वेष विधिर्वह्निपुटीकृतः ।
हंसः पुमानधस्तस्य रुद्रबिन्दुसमन्वितः ॥ 21
19.m:
In the venerable Dīkṣottara, however, this procedure is enveloped in fire:
haṃsa is the soul; below it, accompanied by the drop of Rudra. // 21

19.s:
śiṣyadehe niyojyaitadanudvagnaḥ śataṃ japet /
utkramyordhvanimeṣeṇa śiṣya itthaṃ paraṃ vrajet // 22
19.d:
शिष्यदेहे नियोज्यैतदनुद्वग्नः शतं जपेत् ।
उत्क्रम्योर्ध्वनिमेषेण शिष्य इत्थं परं व्रजेत् ॥ 22
19.m:
Having applied this into the disciple's body, untroubled, he should recite it one hundred times;
departing in the upward twinkling of an eye, the disciple thus reaches the Supreme. // 22

19.s:
eṣa eva vidhiḥ śrīmatsiddhayogīśvarīmate /
iyamutkrāmaṇī dīkṣā kartavyā yogino guroḥ // 23
19.d:
एष एव विधिः श्रीमत्सिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ।
इयमुत्क्रामणी दीक्षा कर्तव्या योगिनो गुरोः ॥ 23
19.m:
This very rule is found in the venerable Siddhayogīśvarīmata.
This initiation causing yogic transition is to be performed by a guru who is a yogi;

19.s:
anabhyastaprāṇacāraḥ kathamenāṃ kariṣyati /
vakṣyamāṇāṃ brahmavidyāṃ sakalāṃ niṣkalombhitām // 24
19.d:
अनभ्यस्तप्राणचारः कथमेनां करिष्यति ।
वक्ष्यमाणां ब्रह्मविद्यां सकलां निष्कलोम्भिताम् ॥ 24
19.m:
How will one who has not mastered the movement of the breath perform this?
Or he may recite repeatedly into his ear the Brahmavidyā to be described,

19.s:
karṇe'sya vā paṭhedbhūyo bhūyo vāpyatha pāṭhayet /
svayaṃ ca karma kurvīta tattvaśuddhyādikaṃ guruḥ // 25
19.d:
कर्णेऽस्य वा पठेद्भूयो भूयो वाप्यथ पाठयेत् ।
स्वयं च कर्म कुर्वीत तत्त्वशुद्ध्यादिकं गुरुः ॥ 25
19.m:
Which is qualified and interwoven with the unqualified, or cause it to be recited,
And the guru himself should perform the ritual such as the purification of the levels of reality;

19.s:
mantrakriyābalātpūrṇāhutyetthaṃ yojayetpare /
yogābhyāsamakṛtvāpi sadya+utkrāntidāṃ guruḥ // 26
19.d:
मन्त्रक्रियाबलात्पूर्णाहुत्येत्थं योजयेत्परे ।
योगाभ्यासमकृत्वापि सद्य+उत्क्रान्तिदां गुरुः ॥ 26
19.m:
Through the power of mantra and action, he should thus unite [him] with the Supreme by the final oblation.
Even without practicing yoga, the guru, granting immediate yogic transition,

19.s:
jñānamantrakriyādhyānabalātkartuṃ bhavetprabhuḥ /
anayotkramyate śiṣyo balādevaikakaṃ kṣaṇam // 27
19.d:
ज्ञानमन्त्रक्रियाध्यानबलात्कर्तुं भवेत्प्रभुः ।
अनयोत्क्रम्यते शिष्यो बलादेवैककं क्षणम् ॥ 27
19.m:
Would be capable of performing [it] through the power of knowledge, mantra, action, and meditation.
By this [means] the disciple is forcibly caused to undergo yogic transition in a single moment.

19.s:
kālasyollaṅghya bhogo hi kṣaṇiko'syāstu kiṃ tataḥ /
sadya+utkrāntidā cānyā yasyāṃ pūrṇāhutiṃ tadā // 28
19.d:
कालस्योल्लङ्घ्य भोगो हि क्षणिकोऽस्यास्तु किं ततः ।
सद्य+उत्क्रान्तिदा चान्या यस्यां पूर्णाहुतिं तदा ॥ 28
19.m:
Indeed, having transcended [the power] of Time, his momentary enjoyment may come to pass; what then?
And another [rite] grants immediate yogic transition, in which [the guru] should offer the final oblation

19.s:
dadyādyadāsya prāṇāḥ syurdhruvaṃ niṣkramaṇecchavaḥ /
vināpi kriyayā bhāvibrahmavidyābalādguruḥ // 29
19.d:
दद्याद्यदास्य प्राणाः स्युर्ध्रुवं निष्क्रमणेच्छवः ।
विनापि क्रियया भाविब्रह्मविद्याबलाद्गुरुः ॥ 29
19.m:
At that very time when his breaths certainly desire to depart.
Even without ritual action, by the power of the imminent Brahmavidyā, the guru,

19.s:
karṇajāpaprayogeṇa tattvakañcukajālataḥ /
niḥsārayanyathābhīṣṭe sakale niṣkale dvaye // 30
19.d:
कर्णजापप्रयोगेण तत्त्वकञ्चुकजालतः ।
निःसारयन्यथाभीष्टे सकले निष्कले द्वये ॥ 30
19.m:
By the application of whispering into the ear, extracting [him] from the snare of the cuirasses of the levels of reality,
Should gradually unite the soul, as desired, in the qualified, in the unqualified, in both,

19.s:
tattve vā yatra kutrāpi yojayetpudgalaṃ kramāt /
samayī putrako vāpi paṭhedvidyāmimāṃ tathā // 31
19.d:
तत्त्वे वा यत्र कुत्रापि योजयेत्पुद्गलं क्रमात् ।
समयी पुत्रको वापि पठेद्विद्यामिमां तथा ॥ 31
19.m:
Or in any level of reality whatever.
Likewise, an initiate into the rule or a spiritual son may recite this vidyā;

19.s:
tatpāṭhāttu samayyuktāṃ rudrāṃśāpattimaśnute /
etau jape cādhyayane yasmādadhikṛtāvubhau // 32
19.d:
तत्पाठात्तु समय्युक्तां रुद्रांशापत्तिमश्नुते ।
एतौ जपे चाध्ययने यस्मादधिकृतावुभौ ॥ 32
19.m:
And through that recitation, he attains the status of being a portion of Rudra as stated for an initiate into the rule,
Because both of these are authorized in recitation and study,

19.s:
nādhyāpanopadeśe vā sa eṣo'dhyayanādṛte /
paṭhatostvanayorvastusvabhāvāttasya sā gatiḥ // 33
19.d:
नाध्यापनोपदेशे वा स एषोऽध्ययनादृते ।
पठतोस्त्वनयोर्वस्तुस्वभावात्तस्य सा गतिः ॥ 33
19.m:
Not in teaching or instructing. This [result comes about] simply from study;
Yet, when the two recite, that destiny comes to him by the intrinsic nature of reality.

19.s:
yathā niṣiddhabhūtādikarmā mantraṃ smaransvayam /
āviṣṭe'pi kvacinnaiti lopaṃ kartṛtvavarjanāt // 34
19.d:
यथा निषिद्धभूतादिकर्मा मन्त्रं स्मरन्स्वयम् ।
आविष्टेऽपि क्वचिन्नैति लोपं कर्तृत्ववर्जनात् ॥ 34
19.m:
Just as one performing a forbidden act concerning spirits, remembering the mantra himself,
Does not incur transgression even when possessed, because he lacks agency;

19.s:
yathā ca vācayañśāstraṃ samayī śūnyaveśmani /
na lupyate tadantaḥsthaprāṇivargopakārataḥ // 35
19.d:
यथा च वाचयञ्शास्त्रं समयी शून्यवेश्मनि ।
न लुप्यते तदन्तःस्थप्राणिवर्गोपकारतः ॥ 35
19.m:
And just as an initiate into the rule reading a scripture in an empty house
Does not incur transgression, because of benefiting the hosts of living beings dwelling therein;

19.s:
tathā svayaṃ paṭhanneṣa vidyāṃ vastusvabhāvataḥ /
tasminmukte na lupyeta yato kiṃcitkaro'tra saḥ // 36
19.d:
तथा स्वयं पठन्नेष विद्यां वस्तुस्वभावतः ।
तस्मिन्मुक्ते न लुप्येत यतो किंचित्करोऽत्र सः ॥ 36
19.m:
So this [initiate], reciting the vidyā himself, by the intrinsic nature of reality,
Would not incur transgression when that [person] is liberated, since he does nothing in this regard.

19.s: nanu cādīkṣitāgre sa noccarecchāstrapaddhatim // 37
19.d: ननु चादीक्षिताग्रे स नोच्चरेच्छास्त्रपद्धतिम् ॥ 37
19.m: [Objection:] But surely he should not recite the textual procedure of the scripture in front of an uninitiated person!

19.s:
hanta kuḍyāgrato'pyasya niṣedhastvatha kathyate /
paryudāsena yaḥ śrotumavadhārayituṃ kṣamaḥ // 38
19.d:
हन्त कुड्याग्रतोऽप्यस्य निषेधस्त्वथ कथ्यते ।
पर्युदासेन यः श्रोतुमवधारयितुं क्षमः ॥ 38
19.m:
[Reply:] Well, if you say the prohibition applies even in front of a wall,
It is by excluding [inanimates]: one who is capable of hearing and understanding—

19.s:
sa evātra niṣiddho no kuḍyakīṭapatatriṇaḥ /
tarhi pāṣāṇatulyo'sau vilīnendriyavṛttikaḥ // 39
19.d:
स एवात्र निषिद्धो नो कुड्यकीटपतत्रिणः ।
तर्हि पाषाणतुल्योऽसौ विलीनेन्द्रियवृत्तिकः ॥ 39
19.m:
Only such a person is prohibited here, not walls, worms, or birds.
[Objection:] Then that one, whose sense-faculties have dissolved, is equal to a stone;

19.s:
tasyāgre paṭhatastasya niṣedhollaṅghanā katham /
sa tu vastusvabhāvena galitākṣo'pi budhyate // 40
19.d:
तस्याग्रे पठतस्तस्य निषेधोल्लङ्घना कथम् ।
स तु वस्तुस्वभावेन गलिताक्षोऽपि बुध्यते ॥ 40
19.m:
How can there be a transgression of the prohibition for one reciting in front of him?
[Reply:] But, by the intrinsic nature of reality, even with senses failed, he awakens,

19.s:
akṣānapekṣayaivāntaścicchaktyā svaprakāśayā /
prāgdehaṃ kila tityakṣurnottaraṃ cādhitaṣṭhivān // 41
19.d:
अक्षानपेक्षयैवान्तश्चिच्छक्त्या स्वप्रकाशया ।
प्राग्देहं किल तित्यक्षुर्नोत्तरं चाधितष्ठिवान् ॥ 41
19.m:
Without depending on the sense-organs at all, inwardly, by the power of consciousness luminous by itself.
Indeed, wishing to abandon his former body, and not yet having assumed the subsequent one,

19.s:
madhye prabodhakabalāt pratibudhyet pudgalaḥ /
mantrāḥ śabdamayāḥ śuddhavimarśātmatayā svayam // 42
19.d:
मध्ये प्रबोधकबलात् प्रतिबुध्येत् पुद्गलः ।
मन्त्राः शब्दमयाः शुद्धविमर्शात्मतया स्वयम् ॥ 42
19.m:
In between, through the strength of the awakener, the soul may awaken.
Mantras consist of sound; of their own accord, being of the nature of pure reflective awareness,

19.s:
arthātmanā cāvabhāntastadarthapratibodhakāḥ /
tenāsya galitākṣasya prabodho jāyate svayam // 43
19.d:
अर्थात्मना चावभान्तस्तदर्थप्रतिबोधकाः ।
तेनास्य गलिताक्षस्य प्रबोधो जायते स्वयम् ॥ 43
19.m:
And appearing as objects, they awaken [the awareness of] their object.
Therefore, the awakening of this person whose sense-faculties have failed arises spontaneously,

19.s:
svacitsamānajātīyamantrāmarśanasaṃnidheḥ /
yathā hyalpajavo vāyuḥ sajātīyavimiśritaḥ // 44
19.d:
स्वचित्समानजातीयमन्त्रामर्शनसंनिधेः ।
यथा ह्यल्पजवो वायुः सजातीयविमिश्रितः ॥ 44
19.m:
From the presence of the reflective grasp of a mantra that is of the same class as one's own consciousness.
For just as a slow wind, mixed with [a wind] of the same class,

19.s:
javī tathātmā saṃsuptāmarśo'pyevaṃ prabudhyate /
prabuddhaḥ sa ca saṃjāto na cādīkṣita ucyate // 45
19.d:
जवी तथात्मा संसुप्तामर्शोऽप्येवं प्रबुध्यते ।
प्रबुद्धः स च संजातो न चादीक्षित उच्यते ॥ 45
19.m:
Becomes swift, so the self, even when its reflective awareness is asleep, awakens in this way.
And having become awakened, he is not called uninitiated;

19.s:
dīkṣā hi nāma saṃskāro na tvanyatso'sti cāsya hi /
ata eva nijaṃ śāstraṃ paṭhati kvāpi sāmaye // 46
19.d:
दीक्षा हि नाम संस्कारो न त्वन्यत्सोऽस्ति चास्य हि ।
अत एव निजं शास्त्रं पठति क्वापि सामये ॥ 46
19.m:
For initiation is indeed a purification, not anything else, and that is present for him.
Therefore, if an initiate into the rule recites his scripture somewhere,

19.s:
tacchrutvā ko'pi dhanyaścenmucyate nāsya sā kṣatiḥ /
śāstranindāṃ maiṣa kārṣīddvayoḥ pātityadāyinīm // 47
19.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा कोऽपि धन्यश्चेन्मुच्यते नास्य सा क्षतिः ।
शास्त्रनिन्दां मैष कार्षीद्द्वयोः पातित्यदायिनीम् ॥ 47
19.m:
And hearing that, some fortunate person is liberated, that is no fault for him;
[The prohibition,] ‘One should not recite before an uninitiated person,’ is intended solely for this: ‘Let him not revile the scripture, which causes the downfall of both.’

19.s:
ityevaṃparametannādīkṣitāgre paṭhediti /
yathā ca samayī kāṣṭhe loṣṭe vā mantrayojanām // 48
19.d:
इत्येवंपरमेतन्नादीक्षिताग्रे पठेदिति ।
यथा च समयी काष्ठे लोष्टे वा मन्त्रयोजनाम् ॥ 48
19.m:
And just as an initiate into the rule applying a mantra upon a piece of wood or a clod of earth,
Does not incur transgression when it moves, just so is it here;

19.s:
kurvaṃstasmiṃścalatyeti na lopaṃ tadvadatra hi /
yato'sya pratyayaprāptiprepsoḥ samayinastathā // 49
19.d:
कुर्वंस्तस्मिंश्चलत्येति न लोपं तद्वदत्र हि ।
यतोऽस्य प्रत्ययप्राप्तिप्रेप्सोः समयिनस्तथा ॥ 49
19.m:
Because when he has engaged [in it] naturally in this way, desiring to attain verification,
There is indeed no harm when that [person] is liberated.

19.s:
pravṛttasya svabhāvena tasminmukte na vai kṣatiḥ /
sādhakastu sadā sādhye phale niyatiyantraṇāt // 50
19.d:
प्रवृत्तस्य स्वभावेन तस्मिन्मुक्ते न वै क्षतिः ।
साधकस्तु सदा साध्ये फले नियतियन्त्रणात् ॥ 50
19.m: The adept, however, is always bound by the restriction of the result to be accomplished;

19.s:
makṣikāśrutamantro'pi prāyaścittaucitīṃ caret /
itthaṃ sadyaḥsamutkrāntiryoktā tāmājñayā guroḥ // 51
19.d:
मक्षिकाश्रुतमन्त्रोऽपि प्रायश्चित्तौचितीं चरेत् ।
इत्थं सद्यःसमुत्क्रान्तिर्योक्ता तामाज्ञया गुरोः ॥ 51
19.m:
Even if the mantra is heard by a fly, he should perform an appropriate expiation.
Thus has immediate yogic transition been explained; by command of the guru,

19.s:
samayyādirapi proktakāle proktārthasiddhaye /
svayaṃ kuryātsamabhyastaprāṇacāragamāgamaḥ // 52
19.d:
समय्यादिरपि प्रोक्तकाले प्रोक्तार्थसिद्धये ।
स्वयं कुर्यात्समभ्यस्तप्राणचारगमागमः ॥ 52
19.m:
Even an initiate into the rule or others, at the stated time, to achieve the stated purpose,
May perform it himself, having thoroughly mastered the coming and going of the movement of the breath;

19.s:
akṛtādhikṛtirvāpi guruḥ samayaśuddhaye /
adhastanapadāvastho natu jñāneddhacetanaḥ // 53
19.d:
अकृताधिकृतिर्वापि गुरुः समयशुद्धये ।
अधस्तनपदावस्थो नतु ज्ञानेद्धचेतनः ॥ 53
19.m:
Or a guru who has not [yet] performed authorization, for the purification of the rule,
Remaining at a lower stage, but not one whose consciousness is kindled by knowledge.

19.s:
itīyaṃ sadya+utkrāntiḥ sūcitā mālinīmate /
svayaṃ vā guruṇā vātha kāryatvena maheśinā // 54
19.d:
इतीयं सद्य+उत्क्रान्तिः सूचिता मालिनीमते ।
स्वयं वा गुरुणा वाथ कार्यत्वेन महेशिना ॥ 54
19.m:
Thus this immediate yogic transition has been indicated in the Mālinīvijayottara,
As something to be performed either by oneself or by the guru, by the Great Lord.

19.s:
sarvaṃ bhogaṃ virūpaṃ tu matvā dehaṃ tyajedyadi /
tadā tena krameṇāśu yojitaḥ samayī śivaḥ // 55
19.d:
सर्वं भोगं विरूपं तु मत्वा देहं त्यजेद्यदि ।
तदा तेन क्रमेणाशु योजितः समयी शिवः ॥ 55
19.m:
If, having considered all enjoyment to be deformed, he abandons the body,
Then, through that method, the initiate into the rule, united [with reality], quickly becomes Śiva.

19.s: ukteyaṃ sadya+utkrāntiryā gopyā prāṇavadbudhaiḥ // 56
19.d: उक्तेयं सद्य+उत्क्रान्तिर्या गोप्या प्राणवद्बुधैः ॥ 56
19.m: This immediate yogic transition has been spoken of, which should be guarded by the wise like their own life-breath.

20.m: Now I explain initiation that grants reassurance to ignorant people.

20.s:
trikoṇe vahnisadane vahnivarṇojjvale'bhitaḥ /
vāyavyapuranirdhūte kare savye sujājvale // 2
20.d:
त्रिकोणे वह्निसदने वह्निवर्णोज्ज्वलेऽभितः ।
वायव्यपुरनिर्धूते करे सव्ये सुजाज्वले ॥ 2
20.m:
In a triangle, in the abode of fire, blazing all around with the color of fire,
Agitated by the city of wind, in the right hand brightly blazing,

20.s:
bījaṃ kiṃcidgṛhītvaitattathaiva hṛdayāntare /
kare ca dahyamānaṃ saccintayettajjapaikayuk // 3
20.d:
बीजं किंचिद्गृहीत्वैतत्तथैव हृदयान्तरे ।
करे च दह्यमानं सच्चिन्तयेत्तज्जपैकयुक् ॥ 3
20.m:
Taking a seed, he should meditate upon it as burning in that very way within the heart
And in the hand, engaged solely in its recitation.

Afflicted by the burning succession of the sound phaṭ inflamed by fire,
The seed becomes seedless, incapable of producing its own sprout;

20.s:
taptaṃ naitatprarohāya tenaiva pratyayena tu /
malamāyākhyakarmāṇi mantradhyānakriyābalāt // 5
20.d:
तप्तं नैतत्प्ररोहाय तेनैव प्रत्ययेन तु ।
मलमायाख्यकर्माणि मन्त्रध्यानक्रियाबलात् ॥ 5
20.m:
Heated, it is not [fit] for sprouting. By that very verification,
The karmas called impurity and māyā, through the power of mantra, meditation, and ritual action,

20.s:
dagdhāni na svakāryāya nirbījapratyayaṃ tvimam /
sa śrīmānsuprasanno me śaṃbhunātho nyarūpayat // 6
20.d:
दग्धानि न स्वकार्याय निर्बीजप्रत्ययं त्विमम् ।
स श्रीमान्सुप्रसन्नो मे शंभुनाथो न्यरूपयत् ॥ 6
20.m:
Are burnt and are not [fit] for their own effect. This verification through the seedless,
The venerable Śambhunātha, highly pleased, explained to me.

20.s:
bījasyāpyatra kāryā ca yojanā kṛpayā guroḥ /
yato dīkṣā sudīptatvātsthāvarāṇyapi mocayet // 7
20.d:
बीजस्याप्यत्र कार्या च योजना कृपया गुरोः ।
यतो दीक्षा सुदीप्तत्वात्स्थावराण्यपि मोचयेत् ॥ 7
20.m:
And here, even for a seed, [such] application is to be done through the guru's compassion;
Because initiation, due to its intense radiance, liberates even immobile beings.

20.s:
yo gururjapahomārcādhyānasiddhatvamātmani /
jñātvā dīkṣāṃ carettasya dīkṣā sapratyayā smṛtā // 8
20.d:
यो गुरुर्जपहोमार्चाध्यानसिद्धत्वमात्मनि ।
ज्ञात्वा दीक्षां चरेत्तस्य दीक्षा सप्रत्यया स्मृता ॥ 8
20.m:
Which guru, having recognized in himself attainment through recitation, fire-sacrifice, worship, and meditation,
Performs initiation—his initiation is taught as accompanied by verification.

20.s:
avadhūte nirācāre tattvajñe natvayaṃ vidhiḥ /
sācāraiḥ kriyate dīkṣā yā dṛṣṭapratyayānvitā // 9
20.d:
अवधूते निराचारे तत्त्वज्ञे नत्वयं विधिः ।
साचारैः क्रियते दीक्षा या दृष्टप्रत्ययान्विता ॥ 9
20.m:
However, this rule does not apply to an avadhūta, free from conventional conduct, who knows reality.
Initiation is performed by those observing conventional conduct, accompanied by visible verification.

20.s:
nirācāreṇa dīkṣāyāṃ pratyayastu na gadyate /
jñānaṃ svapratyayaṃ yasmānna phalāntaramarhati // 10
20.d:
निराचारेण दीक्षायां प्रत्ययस्तु न गद्यते ।
ज्ञानं स्वप्रत्ययं यस्मान्न फलान्तरमर्हति ॥ 10
20.m:
Verification is not spoken of in the initiation [performed] by one free from conventional conduct,
Because knowledge is self-verifying, as it requires no other result;

20.s:
dhyānādi tu phalātsādhyamiti siddhāmatoditam /
tulāśuddhiparīkṣāṃ vā kuryātpratyayayoginīm // 11
20.d:
ध्यानादि तु फलात्साध्यमिति सिद्धामतोदितम् ।
तुलाशुद्धिपरीक्षां वा कुर्यात्प्रत्यययोगिनीम् ॥ 11
20.m:
dhyānādi tu phalātsādhyamiti siddhāmatoditam
tulāśuddhiparīkṣāṃ vā kuryātpratyayayoginīm // 11

20.s:
yathā śrītantrasadbhāve kathitā parameśinā /
śrīpūrvaśāstre'pyeṣā ca sūcitā parameśinā // 12
20.d:
यथा श्रीतन्त्रसद्भावे कथिता परमेशिना ।
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रेऽप्येषा च सूचिता परमेशिना ॥ 12
20.m:
As taught by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Tantrasadbhāva,
And this has also been indicated by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra,

20.s:
ānanda udbhavaḥ kampo nidrā ghūrṇiśca pañcamī /
ityevaṃvadatā śaktitāratamyābhidhāyinā // 13
20.d:
आनन्द उद्भवः कम्पो निद्रा घूर्णिश्च पञ्चमी ।
इत्येवंवदता शक्तितारतम्याभिधायिना ॥ 13
20.m:
By stating: ‘Bliss, rising up, trembling, sleep, and swirling as the fifth,’
Expressing the gradation of [descent of] power.

20.s:
udbhavo laghubhāvena dehagrahatirohiteḥ /
deho hi pārthivo mukhyastadā mukhyatvamujjhati // 14
20.d:
उद्भवो लघुभावेन देहग्रहतिरोहितेः ।
देहो हि पार्थिवो मुख्यस्तदा मुख्यत्वमुज्झति ॥ 14
20.m:
Rising up is [caused] by lightness, because the seizure of the body is veiled;
For the physical body is predominantly earthy, and then it abandons that predominance.

20.s:
bhāvilāghavamantreṇa śiṣyaṃ dhyātvā samutplutam /
karmāṇi tatrāśeṣāṇi pūrvoktānyācaredguruḥ // 15
uktā seyaṃ tulāśuddhidīkṣā pratyayadāyinī /
20.d:
भाविलाघवमन्त्रेण शिष्यं ध्यात्वा समुत्प्लुतम् ।
कर्माणि तत्राशेषाणि पूर्वोक्तान्याचरेद्गुरुः ॥ 15
उक्ता सेयं तुलाशुद्धिदीक्षा प्रत्ययदायिनी ।
20.m:
Visualising the disciple who has leaped up by the mantra of future lightness, / the guru should perform completely all the rites mentioned before. // 15
This is declared to be the initiation of balance-testing, which bestows direct conviction.

21.s: parokṣasaṃsthitasyātha dīkṣākarma nigadyate // 1
21.d: परोक्षसंस्थितस्याथ दीक्षाकर्म निगद्यते ॥ 1
21.m: Now the ritual of initiation for one who is absent is expounded: // 1

21.s:
bhuktimuktiprasiddhyarthaṃ nīyate sadguruṃ prati /
ityasminmālinīvākye pratiḥ sāṃmukhyāvācakaḥ // 2
21.d:
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं नीयते सद्गुरुं प्रति ।
इत्यस्मिन्मालिनीवाक्ये प्रतिः सांमुख्यावाचकः ॥ 2
21.m: In the statement of the Mālinīvijayottara: 'He is led toward the true guru for the sake of attaining enjoyment and liberation', / the preposition 'toward' signifies facing towards. // 2

21.s:
sāṃmukhyaṃ cāsya śiṣyasya tatkṛpāspadatātmakam /
tamārādhyeti vacanaṃ kṛpāhetūpalakṣaṇam // 3
21.d:
सांमुख्यं चास्य शिष्यस्य तत्कृपास्पदतात्मकम् ।
तमाराध्येति वचनं कृपाहेतूपलक्षणम् ॥ 3
21.m: And this disciple's facing towards consists in being the receptacle of his grace; / the phrase 'having propitiated him' points to the cause of grace. // 3

21.s:
tatsaṃbandhāttataḥ kaścittatkṣaṇādapavṛjyate /
ityasyāyamapi hyartho mālinīvākyasanmaṇeḥ // 4
21.d:
तत्संबन्धात्ततः कश्चित्तत्क्षणादपवृज्यते ।
इत्यस्यायमपि ह्यर्थो मालिनीवाक्यसन्मणेः ॥ 4
21.m: Therefore, by connection with him, someone is liberated at that very moment: / this too is indeed the meaning of that fine jewel of a passage from the Mālinīvijayottara. // 4

21.s:
tatkṣaṇāditi nāsyāsti yiyāsādikṣaṇāntaram /
kiṃtvevameva karuṇānighnastaṃ gururuddharet // 5
21.d:
तत्क्षणादिति नास्यास्ति यियासादिक्षणान्तरम् ।
किंत्वेवमेव करुणानिघ्नस्तं गुरुरुद्धरेत् ॥ 5
21.m: By 'at that very moment' [is meant that] for him there is no subsequent moment of desiring to go and so forth; / rather, precisely thus, yielding to compassion, the guru should deliver him: // 5

21.s:
gurusevākṣīṇatanordīkṣāmaprāpya pañcatām /
gatasyātha svayaṃ mṛtyukṣaṇoditatathāruceḥ // 6
21.d:
गुरुसेवाक्षीणतनोर्दीक्षामप्राप्य पञ्चताम् ।
गतस्याथ स्वयं मृत्युक्षणोदिततथारुचेः ॥ 6
21.m: For one whose body is emaciated from service to the guru, who has met his death without receiving initiation, / or in whom such an inclination arose spontaneously at the moment of death; // 6

21.s:
athavādharatantrādidīkṣāsaṃskārabhāginaḥ /
prāptasāmayikasyātha parāṃ dīkṣāmavindataḥ // 7
21.d:
अथवाधरतन्त्रादिदीक्षासंस्कारभागिनः ।
प्राप्तसामयिकस्याथ परां दीक्षामविन्दतः ॥ 7
21.m: or for one who had undergone the purificatory rite of initiation according to a lower tantra, / or who had become an initiate into the rule but had not obtained the supreme initiation; // 7

21.s:
ḍimbāhatasya yogeśībhakṣitasyābhicārataḥ /
mṛtasya guruṇā yantratantrādinihatasya vā // 8
21.d:
डिम्बाहतस्य योगेशीभक्षितस्याभिचारतः ।
मृतस्य गुरुणा यन्त्रतन्त्रादिनिहतस्य वा ॥ 8
21.m: or for one killed in a riot, devoured by mistress-yoginīs, killed by sorcery, / or slain by a guru through magical diagrams, tantras, and so forth; // 8

21.s:
bhraṣṭasvasamayasyātha dīkṣāṃ prāptavato'pyalam /
bandhubhāryāsuhṛtputragāḍhābhyarthanayogataḥ // 9
21.d:
भ्रष्टस्वसमयस्याथ दीक्षां प्राप्तवतोऽप्यलम् ।
बन्धुभार्यासुहृत्पुत्रगाढाभ्यर्थनयोगतः ॥ 9
21.m: or for one who has fallen from his own rule, even though he had received initiation sufficiently, / by virtue of intense entreaty from kin, wife, friends, and son; // 9

21.s:
svayaṃ tadviṣayotpannakaruṇābalato'pi vā /
vijñātatanmukhāyātaśaktipātāṃśadharmaṇaḥ // 10
21.d:
स्वयं तद्विषयोत्पन्नकरुणाबलतोऽपि वा ।
विज्ञाततन्मुखायातशक्तिपातांशधर्मणः ॥ 10
21.m: or by the force of compassion arisen spontaneously with regard to him, / whose characteristic mark of a share of descent of power arriving through that channel is discerned— // 10

21.s:
gururdīkṣāṃ mṛtoddhārīṃ kurvīta śivadāyinīm /
śrīmṛtyuñjayasiddhādau taduktaṃ parameśinā // 11
21.d:
गुरुर्दीक्षां मृतोद्धारीं कुर्वीत शिवदायिनीम् ।
श्रीमृत्युञ्जयसिद्धादौ तदुक्तं परमेशिना ॥ 11
21.m: for him the guru should perform the deliverance of the dead, an initiation conferring Śivahood; / so it has been stated by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Mṛtyuñjayasiddha and elsewhere: // 11

21.s:
adīkṣite nṛpatyādāvalase patite mṛte /
bālāturastrīvṛddhe ca mṛtoddhāraṃ prakalpayet // 12
21.d:
अदीक्षिते नृपत्यादावलसे पतिते मृते ।
बालातुरस्त्रीवृद्धे च मृतोद्धारं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 12
21.m: 'For the uninitiated, such as a king, for the indolent, the fallen, the dead, / and for a child, an invalid, a woman, and the aged, one should perform the deliverance of the dead.' // 12

21.s:
vidhiḥ sarvaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ sa tu saṃkṣipta iṣyate /
gurvādipūjārahito bāhye bhogāya sā yataḥ // 13
21.d:
विधिः सर्वः पूर्वमुक्तः स तु संक्षिप्त इष्यते ।
गुर्वादिपूजारहितो बाह्ये भोगाय सा यतः ॥ 13
21.m: The entire procedure has been stated before, but here it is prescribed in an abridged form, / devoid of the worship of the guru and others, because externally that is for enjoyment. // 13

21.s:
adhivāsacarukṣetraṃ śayyāmaṇḍalakalpane /
nopayogyatra tacchiṣyasaṃskriyāsvapnadṛṣṭaye // 14
21.d:
अधिवासचरुक्षेत्रं शय्यामण्डलकल्पने ।
नोपयोग्यत्र तच्छिष्यसंस्क्रियास्वप्नदृष्टये ॥ 14
21.m: The perfuming rite, the sacrificial porridge, the sacred site, the preparation of the bed and the mandala / are of no use here for the purpose of the disciple's purificatory rite and seeing dreams; // 14

21.s:
mantrasaṃnidhisaṃtṛptiyogāyātra tu maṇḍalam /
bhūyodine ca devārcā sākṣānnāsyopakāri tat // 15
21.d:
मन्त्रसंनिधिसंतृप्तियोगायात्र तु मण्डलम् ।
भूयोदिने च देवार्चा साक्षान्नास्योपकारि तत् ॥ 15
21.m: rather, the mandala here is for the purpose of the presence and contentment of the mantras, / and the worship of the deity on the following day does not directly assist him. // 15

21.s:
kriyopakaraṇasthānamaṇḍalākṛtimantrataḥ /
dhyānayogaikatadbhaktijñānatanmayabhāvataḥ // 16
21.d:
क्रियोपकरणस्थानमण्डलाकृतिमन्त्रतः ।
ध्यानयोगैकतद्भक्तिज्ञानतन्मयभावतः ॥ 16
21.m: Through ritual action, paraphernalia, sacred place, mandala, effigy, and mantra, / through meditation, yoga, exclusive devotion to him, knowledge, and becoming identical with that: // 16

21.s:
tatpraviṣṭasya kasyāpi śiṣyāṇāṃ ca gurostathā /
ekādaśaite kathitāḥ saṃnidhānāya hetavaḥ // 17
21.d:
तत्प्रविष्टस्य कस्यापि शिष्याणां च गुरोस्तथा ।
एकादशैते कथिताः संनिधानाय हेतवः ॥ 17
21.m: for anyone who has entered into that, for the disciples, and likewise for the guru, / these eleven are stated to be the causes for bringing about presence. // 17

21.s:
uttarottaramutkṛṣṭāstathā vyāmiśraṇāvaśāt /
kriyātibhūyasī puṣpādyuttamaṃ lakṣaṇānvitam // 18
21.d:
उत्तरोत्तरमुत्कृष्टास्तथा व्यामिश्रणावशात् ।
क्रियातिभूयसी पुष्पाद्युत्तमं लक्षणान्वितम् ॥ 18
21.m: They are progressively superior, and likewise according to combinations: / ritual action is exceedingly extensive; flowers and the rest should be excellent and endowed with auspicious marks; // 18

21.s:
ekaliṅgādi ca sthānaṃ yatrātmā saṃprasīdati /
maṇḍalaṃ tritriśūlābjacakraṃ yanmantramaṇḍale // 19
21.d:
एकलिङ्गादि च स्थानं यत्रात्मा संप्रसीदति ।
मण्डलं त्रित्रिशूलाब्जचक्रं यन्मन्त्रमण्डले ॥ 19
21.m: the place should be a single-liṅga site or the like where the self becomes serene; / the mandala is the wheel of three tridents and lotuses, which, in the assembly of mantras, // 19

21.s:
anāhūte'pi dṛṣṭaṃ satsamayitvaprasādhanam /
taduktaṃ mālinītantre siddhaṃ samayamaṇḍalam // 20
21.d:
अनाहूतेऽपि दृष्टं सत्समयित्वप्रसाधनम् ।
तदुक्तं मालिनीतन्त्रे सिद्धं समयमण्डलम् ॥ 20
21.m: even if uninvoked, once seen, brings about the status of an initiate into the rule; / it is declared in the Mālinītantra to be the accomplished mandala of the rule, // 20

21.s:
yena saṃdṛṣṭamātreti siddhamātrapadadvayāt /
ākṛtirdīptarūpā yā mantrastadvatsudīptikaḥ // 21
21.d:
येन संदृष्टमात्रेति सिद्धमात्रपदद्वयात् ।
आकृतिर्दीप्तरूपा या मन्त्रस्तद्वत्सुदीप्तिकः ॥ 21
21.m: from the pair of words 'merely seen by whom' and 'merely accomplished'; / the effigy is radiant, and the mantra is likewise brilliant. // 21

21.s:
śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭamato neha kathitaṃ vistarātpunaḥ /
kṛtvā maṇḍalamabhyarcya tatra devaṃ kuśairatha // 22
21.d:
शिष्टं स्पष्टमतो नेह कथितं विस्तरात्पुनः ।
कृत्वा मण्डलमभ्यर्च्य तत्र देवं कुशैरथ ॥ 22
21.m: The rest is clear, so it is not stated here at length again. / Having made the mandala and worshipped the deity there with kuśa grass, // 22

21.s:
gomayenākṛtiṃ kuryācchiṣyavattāṃ nidhāpayet /
tatastasyāṃ śodhyamekamadhvānaṃ vyāptibhāvanāt // 23
21.d:
गोमयेनाकृतिं कुर्याच्छिष्यवत्तां निधापयेत् ।
ततस्तस्यां शोध्यमेकमध्वानं व्याप्तिभावनात् ॥ 23
21.m: one should make an effigy with cow-dung and have it laid out like the disciple; / then, having projected into it, up to the end of material nature, one path to be purified // 23

21.s:
prakṛtyantaṃ vinikṣipya punarenaṃ vidhiṃ caret /
mahājālaprayogeṇa sarvasmādadhvamadhyataḥ // 24
21.d:
प्रकृत्यन्तं विनिक्षिप्य पुनरेनं विधिं चरेत् ।
महाजालप्रयोगेण सर्वस्मादध्वमध्यतः ॥ 24
21.m: by means of the contemplation of pervasion, one should again perform this rite: / through the application of the great net, from the midst of all paths, // 24

21.s:
cittamākṛṣya tatrasthaṃ kuryāttadvidhirucyate /
mūlādhārādudetya prasṛtasuvitatānantanāḍyadhvadaṇḍaṃ vīryeṇākramya nāsāgaganaparigataṃ vikṣipan vyāptumīṣṭe /
yāvaddhūmābhirāmapracitataraśikhājālakenādhvacakraṃ saṃchādyābhīṣṭajīvānayanamiti mahājālanāmā prayogaḥ // 25
21.d:
चित्तमाकृष्य तत्रस्थं कुर्यात्तद्विधिरुच्यते ।
मूलाधारादुदेत्य प्रसृतसुविततानन्तनाड्यध्वदण्डं वीर्येणाक्रम्य नासागगनपरिगतं विक्षिपन् व्याप्तुमीष्टे ।
यावद्धूमाभिरामप्रचिततरशिखाजालकेनाध्वचक्रं संछाद्याभीष्टजीवानयनमिति महाजालनामा प्रयोगः ॥ 25
21.m: having drawn the mind and established it there, one should act; its procedure is stated: / Rising from the root-foundation, pervading with power the staff of the path of countless channels fully extended and spreading out, cast forth and encompassing the nasal sky, it is capable of pervading; / completely covering the wheel of the paths with a multitude of flames densely gathered and charming like smoke, until the desired soul is brought back: such is the application named the great net. // 25

21.s:
etenācchādanīyaṃ vrajati paravaśaṃ saṃmukhīnatvamādau pañcādānīyate cetsakalamatha tato'pyadhvamadhyādyatheṣṭam /
ākṛṣṭāvuddhṛtau vā mṛtajanaviṣaye karṣaṇīye'tha jīve yogaḥ śrīśaṃbhunāthāgamaparigamito jālanāmā mayoktaḥ // 26
21.d:
एतेनाच्छादनीयं व्रजति परवशं संमुखीनत्वमादौ पञ्चादानीयते चेत्सकलमथ ततोऽप्यध्वमध्याद्यथेष्टम् ।
आकृष्टावुद्धृतौ वा मृतजनविषये कर्षणीयेऽथ जीवे योगः श्रीशंभुनाथागमपरिगमितो जालनामा मयोक्तः ॥ 26
21.m: By this, that which is to be covered falls under another's power and becomes facing [the guru] first; / afterwards, if it is brought, the whole is then brought at will from the midst of the path: / whether in attracting or in delivering, when a dead person's soul is to be drawn, / this yoga named the net, transmitted from the tradition of the venerable Śambhunātha, has been declared by me. // 26

21.s:
ciravighaṭite senāyugmeyathāmilite punarhayagajanaraṃ svāṃ svāṃ jātiṃ rasādabhidhāvati /
karaṇapavanairnāḍīcakraistathaiva samāgatairnijanijarasādekībhāvyaṃ svajālavaśīkṛtaiḥ // 27
21.d:
चिरविघटिते सेनायुग्मेयथामिलिते पुनर्हयगजनरं स्वां स्वां जातिं रसादभिधावति ।
करणपवनैर्नाडीचक्रैस्तथैव समागतैर्निजनिजरसादेकीभाव्यं स्वजालवशीकृतैः ॥ 27
21.m: Just as when two armies long separated are reunited, / the horses, elephants, and men run each to their own kind out of innate affinity, / exactly so, through the sense-organs, breaths, and wheels of channels brought together, / oneness is to be attained through their respective affinities, brought under the power of one's own net. // 27

21.s:
mahājālasamākṛṣṭo jīvo vijñānaśālinā /
svaḥpretatiryaṅnirayāṃstadaivaiṣa vimuñcati // 28
21.d:
महाजालसमाकृष्टो जीवो विज्ञानशालिना ।
स्वःप्रेततिर्यङ्निरयांस्तदैवैष विमुञ्चति ॥ 28
21.m: Drawn by the great net by one endowed with insight, / the soul immediately abandons the heavenly realms, the ghost realm, animal births, and hells. // 28

21.s:
tajjñānamantrayogāptaḥ puruṣaścaiṣa kṛtrimam /
yogīva sādhyahṛdayāttadā tādātmyamujjhati // 29
21.d:
तज्ज्ञानमन्त्रयोगाप्तः पुरुषश्चैष कृत्रिमम् ।
योगीव साध्यहृदयात्तदा तादात्म्यमुज्झति ॥ 29
21.m: And this person, reached by that knowledge and yoga of mantras, / then casts off identification, like a yogin [withdrawing] an artificial [body] from the heart of the person to be mastered. // 29

21.s:
sthāvarādidaśāścitrāstatsalokasamīpatāḥ /
tyajecceti na citraṃ sa evaṃ yaḥ karmaṇāpi vā // 30
21.d:
स्थावरादिदशाश्चित्रास्तत्सलोकसमीपताः ।
त्यजेच्चेति न चित्रं स एवं यः कर्मणापि वा ॥ 30
21.m: It is no wonder that he abandons the various states of immobility and so forth, / or the states of sharing their worlds and proximity to them, which had been produced by past karma. // 30

21.s:
adhikāriśarīratvānmānuṣye tu śarīragaḥ /
na tadā mucyate dehāddehānte tu śivaṃ vrajet // 31
21.d:
अधिकारिशरीरत्वान्मानुष्ये तु शरीरगः ।
न तदा मुच्यते देहाद्देहान्ते तु शिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 31
21.m: However, when existing in a human body, because it is an embodiment qualified for spiritual practice, / he is not released from the body at that time, but at the end of the body he goes to Śiva. // 31

21.s:
tasmindehe tu kāpyasya jāyate śāṅkarī parā /
bhaktirūhācca vijñānādācāryādvāpyasevitāt // 32
21.d:
तस्मिन्देहे तु काप्यस्य जायते शाङ्करी परा ।
भक्तिरूहाच्च विज्ञानादाचार्याद्वाप्यसेवितात् ॥ 32
21.m: In that body, however, there arises in him some supreme devotion to Śaṅkara, / either from reasoning, from insight, or from a master who was not previously served. // 32

21.s:
taddehasaṃsthito'pyeṣa jīvo jālabalādimam /
dārbhādidehaṃ vyāpnoti svādhiṣṭhityāpyacetayan // 33
21.d:
तद्देहसंस्थितोऽप्येष जीवो जालबलादिमम् ।
दार्भादिदेहं व्याप्नोति स्वाधिष्ठित्याप्यचेतयन् ॥ 33
21.m: Even while residing in that body, this soul, by the power of the net, / pervades this body made of darbha grass and the like, without being consciously aware through its own presiding presence. // 33

21.s:
yogamantrakriyājñānabhūyobalavaśātpunaḥ /
manuṣyadehamapyeṣa tadaivāśu vimuñcati // 34
21.d:
योगमन्त्रक्रियाज्ञानभूयोबलवशात्पुनः ।
मनुष्यदेहमप्येष तदैवाशु विमुञ्चति ॥ 34
21.m: Yet, by virtue of the abundant power of yoga, mantra, ritual action, and knowledge, / he also abandons that human body immediately. // 34

21.s:
suptakalpo'pyadeho'pi yo jīvaḥ so'pi jālataḥ /
ākṛṣṭo dārbhamāyāti dehaṃ phalamayaṃ ca vā // 35
21.d:
सुप्तकल्पोऽप्यदेहोऽपि यो जीवः सोऽपि जालतः ।
आकृष्टो दार्भमायाति देहं फलमयं च वा ॥ 35
21.m: Even that soul which is like one asleep and bodiless, / drawn by the net, enters a body made of darbha grass or made of fruit. // 35

21.s:
jātīphalādi yatkiṃcittena vā dehakalpanā /
antarbahirdvayaucityāttadatrotkṛṣṭamucyate // 36
21.d:
जातीफलादि यत्किंचित्तेन वा देहकल्पना ।
अन्तर्बहिर्द्वयौचित्यात्तदत्रोत्कृष्टमुच्यते ॥ 36
21.m: Or the fashioning of the body may be done with whatever is available, such as nutmeg; / because of its suitability both internally and externally, that is said to be superior here. // 36

21.s:
tato jālakramānītaḥ sa jīvaḥ suptavatsthitaḥ /
manoviśiṣṭadehādisāmagrīprāptyabhāvataḥ // 37
21.d:
ततो जालक्रमानीतः स जीवः सुप्तवत्स्थितः ।
मनोविशिष्टदेहादिसामग्रीप्राप्त्यभावतः ॥ 37
21.m: Then, brought by the method of the net, that soul remains like one asleep, / due to the absence of obtaining the aggregate of mind, qualified body, and the like: // 37

21.s:
na spandate na jānāti na vakti na kilecchati /
tādṛśasyaiva saṃskārān sarvān prāgvatprakalpayet // 38
21.d:
न स्पन्दते न जानाति न वक्ति न किलेच्छति ।
तादृशस्यैव संस्कारान् सर्वान् प्राग्वत्प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 38
21.m: it does not stir, does not know, does not speak, nor indeed does it desire; / for one of such a nature, one should perform all the purificatory rites as before. // 38

21.s:
nirbījadīkṣāyogena sarvaṃ kṛtvā puroditam /
vidhiṃ yojanikāṃ pūrṇāhutyā sākaṃ kṣipecca tam // 39
21.d:
निर्बीजदीक्षायोगेन सर्वं कृत्वा पुरोदितम् ।
विधिं योजनिकां पूर्णाहुत्या साकं क्षिपेच्च तम् ॥ 39
21.m: Having performed all the procedure stated before by means of seedless initiation, / one should cast it along with the full oblation into the conjoining rite. // 39

21.s:
dārbhādidehe mantrāgnāvarpite pūrṇayā saha /
muktapāśaḥ śivaṃ yāti punarāvṛttivarjitaḥ // 40
21.d:
दार्भादिदेहे मन्त्राग्नावर्पिते पूर्णया सह ।
मुक्तपाशः शिवं याति पुनरावृत्तिवर्जितः ॥ 40
21.m: When the body of darbha grass and the rest is offered into the mantra-fire together with the full oblation, / freed from bonds, he goes to Śiva, never to return again. // 40

21.s:
sapratyayā tviyaṃ yatra spandate darbhajā tanuḥ /
tatra prāṇamanomantrārpaṇayogāttathā bhavet // 41
21.d:
सप्रत्यया त्वियं यत्र स्पन्दते दर्भजा तनुः ।
तत्र प्राणमनोमन्त्रार्पणयोगात्तथा भवेत् ॥ 41
21.m: However, this [rite] produces direct conviction where the body made of darbha vibrates; / there, that happens by virtue of the offering of vital breath, mind, and mantra. // 41

21.s:
sābhyāsasya tadapyuktaṃ balāśvāsi na tatkṛte /
mṛtoddhāroditaireva yathāsaṃbhūti hetubhiḥ // 42
21.d:
साभ्यासस्य तदप्युक्तं बलाश्वासि न तत्कृते ।
मृतोद्धारोदितैरेव यथासंभूति हेतुभिः ॥ 42
21.m: That too has been stated for one who has practiced, inspiring confidence through power; it is not [required] for his sake, / but according to feasibility, through the causes stated for the deliverance of the dead. // 42

21.s:
jīvatparokṣadīkṣāpi kāryā nirbījikā tu sā /
tasyāṃ darbhākṛtiprāyakalpane jālayogataḥ // 43
21.d:
जीवत्परोक्षदीक्षापि कार्या निर्बीजिका तु सा ।
तस्यां दर्भाकृतिप्रायकल्पने जालयोगतः ॥ 43
21.m: Initiation in absentia for a living person must also be performed, but it should be seedless. / In that ritual, when fashioning an effigy composed primarily of kuśa grass, by means of an energetic net,

21.s:
saṃkalpamātreṇākarṣo jīvasya mṛtibhītitaḥ /
śiṣṭaṃ prāgvatkuśādyutthākāraviploṣavarjitam // 44
21.d:
संकल्पमात्रेणाकर्षो जीवस्य मृतिभीतितः ।
शिष्टं प्राग्वत्कुशाद्युत्थाकारविप्लोषवर्जितम् ॥ 44
21.m: the extraction of the soul is accomplished by mere intention, due to the fear of death. / The rest is as before, except for burning the effigy made of kuśa and the like.

21.s:
pārimityādanaiśvaryātsādhye niyatiyantraṇāt /
jālākṛṣṭirvinābhyāsaṃ rāgadveṣānna jāyate // 45
21.d:
पारिमित्यादनैश्वर्यात्साध्ये नियतियन्त्रणात् ।
जालाकृष्टिर्विनाभ्यासं रागद्वेषान्न जायते ॥ 45
21.m: Because of limitation and lack of sovereignty over the object of attainment due to the constraint of fate, / extraction by the net does not take place without practice, because of attachment and aversion.

21.s:
parokṣa evātulyābhirdīkṣābhiryadi dīkṣitaḥ /
tatrottaraṃ syādbalavatsaṃskārāya tvadhastanam // 46
21.d:
परोक्ष एवातुल्याभिर्दीक्षाभिर्यदि दीक्षितः ।
तत्रोत्तरं स्याद्बलवत्संस्काराय त्वधस्तनम् ॥ 46
21.m: If a person is initiated in absentia by unequal initiations, / then the subsequent one would be dominant, whereas the lower one serves for residual purification.

21.s:
bhuktiyojanikāyāṃ tu bhūyobhirgurubhistathā /
kṛtāyāṃ bhogavaicitryaṃ hetuvaicitryayogataḥ // 47
21.d:
भुक्तियोजनिकायां तु भूयोभिर्गुरुभिस्तथा ।
कृतायां भोगवैचित्र्यं हेतुवैचित्र्ययोगतः ॥ 47
21.m: When, however, an integration for enjoyment is performed by many gurus, / there is diversity of enjoyment due to the combination of diverse causes.

21.s:
parokṣadīkṣaṇe māyottīrṇe bhogāya yojayet /
bhogānīpsā durlabhā hi satī vā bhogahānaye // 48
21.d:
परोक्षदीक्षणे मायोत्तीर्णे भोगाय योजयेत् ।
भोगानीप्सा दुर्लभा हि सती वा भोगहानये ॥ 48
21.m: In initiation in absentia, when māyā has been transcended, one should integrate him for enjoyment; / for the absence of desire for enjoyment is rare, or [if present] it leads to the abandonment of enjoyment.

21.s:
uktaṃ hi svānyasaṃvittyoḥ svasaṃvidbalavattarā /
bādhakatve bādhikāsau sāmyaudāsīnyayostathā // 49
21.d:
उक्तं हि स्वान्यसंवित्त्योः स्वसंविद्बलवत्तरा ।
बाधकत्वे बाधिकासौ साम्यौदासीन्ययोस्तथा ॥ 49
21.m: For it is stated: between one's own consciousness and that of another, one's own consciousness is more powerful; / in case of obstruction it is the obstructor, and likewise in neutrality and equivalence.

21.s:
śrīmān dharmaśivo'pyāha pārokṣyāṃ karmapaddhatau /
parokṣadīkṣaṇe samyak pūrṇāhutividhau yadi // 50
21.d:
श्रीमान् धर्मशिवोऽप्याह पारोक्ष्यां कर्मपद्धतौ ।
परोक्षदीक्षणे सम्यक् पूर्णाहुतिविधौ यदि ॥ 50
21.m: The venerable Dharmaśiva also stated in his ritual manual on rites in absentia: / "In initiation in absentia, during the rite of the full oblation, if properly performed,

21.s:
agniściṭiciṭāśabdaṃ sadhūmaṃ pratimuñcati /
dhatte nīlāmbudacchāyāṃ muhurjvalati śāmyati // 51
21.d:
अग्निश्चिटिचिटाशब्दं सधूमं प्रतिमुञ्चति ।
धत्ते नीलाम्बुदच्छायां मुहुर्ज्वलति शाम्यति ॥ 51
21.m: the fire emits a crackling sound accompanied by smoke, / assumes the hue of a dark cloud, and flares up repeatedly and subsides;

21.s:
vistaro ghorarūpaśca mahīṃ dhāvati cāpyadhaḥ /
dhvāṃkṣādyaśravyaśabdo vā tadā taṃ lakṣayedguruḥ // 52
21.d:
विस्तरो घोररूपश्च महीं धावति चाप्यधः ।
ध्वांक्षाद्यश्रव्यशब्दो वा तदा तं लक्षयेद्गुरुः ॥ 52
21.m: or if it spreads terribly, runs downward along the ground, / or produces inauspicious sounds like the screeching of crows, then the guru should discern him [as tainted].

21.s:
brahmahatyādibhiḥ pāpaistatsaṅgaiścopapātakaiḥ /
tadā tasya na kartavyā dīkṣāsminnakṛte vidhau // 53
21.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादिभिः पापैस्तत्सङ्गैश्चोपपातकैः ।
तदा तस्य न कर्तव्या दीक्षास्मिन्नकृते विधौ ॥ 53
21.m: If he is tainted by sins such as slaying a brahmin and minor sins connected with them, / then his initiation must not be performed until this rite is carried out:

21.s:
navātmā phaṭpuṭāntaḥsthaḥ punaḥ pañcaphaḍanvitaḥ /
amukasyeti pāpāni dahāmyanu phaḍaṣṭakam // 54
21.d:
नवात्मा फट्पुटान्तःस्थः पुनः पञ्चफडन्वितः ।
अमुकस्येति पापानि दहाम्यनु फडष्टकम् ॥ 54
21.m: the Navātman mantra enclosed between two Phaṭ syllables, joined again with five Phaṭs, / followed by: 'I burn away the sins of so-and-so,' with eight Phaṭs—

21.s:
iti sāhasriko homaḥ kartavyastilataṇḍulaiḥ /
ante pūrṇā ca dātavyā tato'smai dīkṣayā guruḥ // 55
21.d:
इति साहस्रिको होमः कर्तव्यस्तिलतण्डुलैः ।
अन्ते पूर्णा च दातव्या ततोऽस्मै दीक्षया गुरुः ॥ 55
21.m: a thousand oblations should be made in this way with sesame seeds and unhusked rice, / and at the end the full oblation should be offered. Then the guru, through initiation,

21.s:
parayojanaparyantaṃ kuryāttattvaviśodhanam /
pratyakṣe'pi sthitasyāṇoḥ pāpino bhagavanmayīm // 56
21.d:
परयोजनपर्यन्तं कुर्यात्तत्त्वविशोधनम् ।
प्रत्यक्षेऽपि स्थितस्याणोः पापिनो भगवन्मयीम् ॥ 56
21.m: should perform the purification of the tattvas up to the supreme integration. / Even in the case of a sinner present in person who has received

21.s:
śaktiṃ prāptavato jyeṣṭhāmevameva vidhiṃ caret /
yadi vā daiśikaḥ samyaṅ na dīptastasya tatpurā // 57
21.d:
शक्तिं प्राप्तवतो ज्येष्ठामेवमेव विधिं चरेत् ।
यदि वा दैशिकः सम्यङ् न दीप्तस्तस्य तत्पुरा ॥ 57
21.m: the elder power of the Lord, one should perform this very rite; / or if the master is not thoroughly illuminated, then before that

21.s:
prāyaścittaistathā dānaiḥ prāṇāyāmaiśca śodhanam /
kṛtvā vidhimimāṃ cāpi dīkṣāṃ kuryādaśaṅkitaḥ // 58
21.d:
प्रायश्चित्तैस्तथा दानैः प्राणायामैश्च शोधनम् ।
कृत्वा विधिमिमां चापि दीक्षां कुर्यादशङ्कितः ॥ 58
21.m: having performed purification through expiations, gifts, and breath-controls, / and having carried out this rite, he may perform the initiation without hesitation.

21.s:
sarvathā vartamāno'pi tattvavinmocayetpaśūn /
icchayaiva śivaḥ sākṣāttasmāttaṃ pūjayetsadā // 59
21.d:
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि तत्त्वविन्मोचयेत्पशून् ।
इच्छयैव शिवः साक्षात्तस्मात्तं पूजयेत्सदा ॥ 59
21.m: No matter how he behaves, one who knows the reality can liberate bound souls / by mere will, as he is Śiva manifest; therefore, one should always worship him.

21.s:
śāṭhyaṃ tatra na kāryaṃ ca tatkṛtvādho vrajecchiśuḥ /
na punaḥ kīrtayettasya pāpaṃ kīrtayitā vrajet // 60
21.d:
शाठ्यं तत्र न कार्यं च तत्कृत्वाधो व्रजेच्छिशुः ।
न पुनः कीर्तयेत्तस्य पापं कीर्तयिता व्रजेत् ॥ 60
21.m: No deceit should be practiced toward him; by committing it, a novice falls low. / Nor should one recount that [initiate's] sin again; he who recounts it would go

21.s:
nirayaṃ varjayettasmāditi dīkṣottare vidhiḥ /
eṣā parokṣadīkṣā dvidhoditā jīvaditarabhedena // 61
21.d:
निरयं वर्जयेत्तस्मादिति दीक्षोत्तरे विधिः ।
एषा परोक्षदीक्षा द्विधोदिता जीवदितरभेदेन ॥ 61
21.m: to hell, and therefore he should avoid it." Such is the rule in the Dīkṣottara. / This initiation in absentia has thus been described as two-fold, divided between the living and the deceased.

22.s: liṅgoddhārākhyāmatha vacmaḥ śivaśāsanaikanirdiṣṭām // 1
22.d: लिङ्गोद्धाराख्यामथ वच्मः शिवशासनैकनिर्दिष्टाम् ॥ 1
22.m: Now we explain the Extraction of Religious Insignia, taught solely in the Śaiva dispensation.

22.s:
uktaṃ śrīmālinītantre kila pārthivadhāraṇām /
uktvā yo yojito yatra sa tasmānna nivartate // 2
22.d:
उक्तं श्रीमालिनीतन्त्रे किल पार्थिवधारणाम् ।
उक्त्वा यो योजितो यत्र स तस्मान्न निवर्तते ॥ 2
22.m: It is indeed stated in the venerable Mālinītantra, after teaching the concentration on the earth element: / 'He who is integrated into whatever level does not return from that.'

22.s:
yogyatāvaśasaṃjātā yasya yatraiva śāsanā /
sa tatraiva niyoktavyo dīkṣākāle tatastvasau // 3
22.d:
योग्यतावशसंजाता यस्य यत्रैव शासना ।
स तत्रैव नियोक्तव्यो दीक्षाकाले ततस्त्वसौ ॥ 3
22.m: Whosoever, according to his capacity, receives instruction on whatever level, / should be integrated at that very level at the time of initiation; thereafter,

22.s:
phalaṃ sarvaṃ samāsādya śive yukto'pavṛjyate /
ayukto'pyūrdhvasaṃśuddhiṃ saṃprāpya bhuvaneśataḥ // 4
22.d:
फलं सर्वं समासाद्य शिवे युक्तोऽपवृज्यते ।
अयुक्तोऽप्यूर्ध्वसंशुद्धिं संप्राप्य भुवनेशतः ॥ 4
22.m: having attained all fruit, when united with Śiva he is liberated. / Even if not united, having attained higher purification from the Lord of the world,

22.s:
śuddhaḥ śivatvamāyāti dagdhasaṃsārabandhanaḥ /
uktvā puṃdhāraṇāṃ coktametadvaidāntikaṃ mayā // 5
22.d:
शुद्धः शिवत्वमायाति दग्धसंसारबन्धनः ।
उक्त्वा पुंधारणां चोक्तमेतद्वैदान्तिकं मया ॥ 5
22.m: purified, his bonds of transmigratory existence burnt away, he attains the state of Śiva. / Having taught the concentration on the Puruṣa, it was also said: 'This Vedāntic doctrine was taught by Me

22.s:
kapilāya purā proktaṃ prathame paṭale tathā /
anena kramayogena saṃprāptaḥ paramaṃ padam // 6
22.d:
कपिलाय पुरा प्रोक्तं प्रथमे पटले तथा ।
अनेन क्रमयोगेन संप्राप्तः परमं पदम् ॥ 6
22.m: to Kapila in ancient times in the first chapter.' Likewise, / having reached the supreme abode through this sequential method,

22.s:
na bhūyaḥ paśutāmeti śuddhe svātmani tiṣṭhati /
ato hi dhvanyate'rtho'yaṃ śivatattvādhareṣvapi // 7
22.d:
न भूयः पशुतामेति शुद्धे स्वात्मनि तिष्ठति ।
अतो हि ध्वन्यतेऽर्थोऽयं शिवतत्त्वाधरेष्वपि ॥ 7
22.m: he does not return to soulhood, but abides in his pure Self. / For this reason, this meaning is implied: even for one who has been integrated

22.s:
tattveṣu yojitasyāsti punaruddharaṇīyatā /
samastaśāstrakathitavastuvaiviktyadāyinaḥ // 8
22.d:
तत्त्वेषु योजितस्यास्ति पुनरुद्धरणीयता ।
समस्तशास्त्रकथितवस्तुवैविक्त्यदायिनः ॥ 8
22.m: into tattvas lower than the Śiva-tattva, there is the necessity of being extracted again. / Because it bestows discrimination regarding the reality taught in all scriptures,

22.s:
śivāgamasya sarvebhyo'pyāgamebhyo viśiṣṭatā /
śivajñānena ca vinā bhūyo'pi paśutodbhavaḥ // 9
22.d:
शिवागमस्य सर्वेभ्योऽप्यागमेभ्यो विशिष्टता ।
शिवज्ञानेन च विना भूयोऽपि पशुतोद्भवः ॥ 9
22.m: the Śaiva revelation is superior to all other revelations; / and without the knowledge of Śiva, soulhood arises once again.

22.s:
kramaśca śaktisaṃpāto malahāniryiyāsutā /
dīkṣā bodho heyahānirupādeyalayātmatā // 10
22.d:
क्रमश्च शक्तिसंपातो मलहानिर्यियासुता ।
दीक्षा बोधो हेयहानिरुपादेयलयात्मता ॥ 10
22.m: The sequence is: descent of power, destruction of impurity, desire to transcend, / initiation, awakening, abandonment of the avoidable, absorption into the acceptable,

22.s:
bhogyatvapāśavatyāgaḥ patikartṛtvasaṃkṣayaḥ /
svātmasthitiścetyevaṃ hi darśanāntarasaṃsthiteḥ // 11
22.d:
भोग्यत्वपाशवत्यागः पतिकर्तृत्वसंक्षयः ।
स्वात्मस्थितिश्चेत्येवं हि दर्शनान्तरसंस्थितेः ॥ 11
22.m: relinquishing the nature of an object of enjoyment and bondage, dissolution of the agency of lower lords, / and abiding in one's own Self. Thus, indeed, for one situated in another system,

22.s:
proktamuddharaṇīyatvaṃ śivaśaktīritasya hi /
atha vaiṣṇavabauddhāditantrāntādharavartinām // 12
22.d:
प्रोक्तमुद्धरणीयत्वं शिवशक्तीरितस्य हि ।
अथ वैष्णवबौद्धादितन्त्रान्ताधरवर्तिनाम् ॥ 12
22.m: the necessity of extraction is stated when impelled by the power of Śiva. / Now, for those abiding in lower levels ending with the Vaiṣṇava and Buddhist Tantras,

22.s:
yadā śivārkaraśmyoghairvikāsi hṛdayāmbujam /
liṅgoddhṛtistadā pūrvaṃ dīkṣākarma tataḥ param // 13
22.d:
यदा शिवार्करश्म्योघैर्विकासि हृदयाम्बुजम् ।
लिङ्गोद्धृतिस्तदा पूर्वं दीक्षाकर्म ततः परम् ॥ 13
22.m: when the lotus of the heart blossoms through the rays of the sun of Śiva, / the extraction of religious insignia comes first, and the rite of initiation after that.

22.s:
prāgliṅgāntarasaṃstho'pi dīkṣātaḥ śivatāṃ vrajet /
tatropavāsya taṃ cānyadine sādhāramantrataḥ // 14
22.d:
प्राग्लिङ्गान्तरसंस्थोऽपि दीक्षातः शिवतां व्रजेत् ।
तत्रोपवास्य तं चान्यदिने साधारमन्त्रतः ॥ 14
22.m: Even one previously established in other religious insignia attains Śivahood through initiation. / There, having made him fast, and having worshipped the Lord on a bare plot

22.s:
sthaṇḍile pūjayitveśaṃ śrāvayettasya vartanīm /
eṣa prāgabhavalliṅgī coditastvadhunā tvayā // 15
22.d:
स्थण्डिले पूजयित्वेशं श्रावयेत्तस्य वर्तनीम् ।
एष प्रागभवल्लिङ्गी चोदितस्त्वधुना त्वया ॥ 15
22.m: on the next day with the universal mantra, he should recite his procedure [to the Lord]: / 'Formerly this man bore external insignia, but now he has been prompted by You,

22.s:
prasannena tadetasmai kuru samyaganugraham /
svaliṅgatyāgaśaṅkotthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ ca māsya bhūt // 16
22.d:
प्रसन्नेन तदेतस्मै कुरु सम्यगनुग्रहम् ।
स्वलिङ्गत्यागशङ्कोत्थं प्रायश्चित्तं च मास्य भूत् ॥ 16
22.m: who are gracious; therefore, grant him complete grace. / May no expiation arise for him out of fear of abandoning his own insignia;

22.s:
acirāttvanmayībhūya bhogaṃ mokṣaṃ prapadyatām /
evamastvityathājñāṃ ca gṛhīrvā vratamasya tat // 17
22.d:
अचिरात्त्वन्मयीभूय भोगं मोक्षं प्रपद्यताम् ।
एवमस्त्वित्यथाज्ञां च गृहीर्वा व्रतमस्य तत् ॥ 17
22.m: becoming identical with You without delay, may he attain enjoyment and liberation!' / Having thus received the command: 'So be it!', he should take his ascetic vow,

22.s:
apāsyāmbhasi nikṣipya snapayedanurūpataḥ /
snātaṃ saṃprokṣayedarghapātrāmbhobhiranantaram // 18
22.d:
अपास्याम्भसि निक्षिप्य स्नपयेदनुरूपतः ।
स्नातं संप्रोक्षयेदर्घपात्राम्भोभिरनन्तरम् ॥ 18
22.m: discard it, cast it into water, and bathe him according to the rule. / When he has bathed, he should immediately sprinkle him with water from the guest-offering vessel;

22.s:
pañcagavyaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ tatastasmai samarpayet /
tatastaṃ baddhanetraṃ ca praveśya praṇipātayet // 19
22.d:
पञ्चगव्यं दन्तकाष्ठं ततस्तस्मै समर्पयेत् ।
ततस्तं बद्धनेत्रं च प्रवेश्य प्रणिपातयेत् ॥ 19
22.m: then he should offer him the five products of the cow and a tooth-stick. / Then, leading him in with his eyes bound, he should make him prostrate.

22.s:
praṇavo mātṛkā māyā vyomavyāpī ṣaḍakṣaraḥ /
bahurūpo'tha netrākhyaḥ sapta sādhāraṇā amī // 20
22.d:
प्रणवो मातृका माया व्योमव्यापी षडक्षरः ।
बहुरूपोऽथ नेत्राख्यः सप्त साधारणा अमी ॥ 20
22.m: The Praṇava, the Mātṛkā, the Māyā, the Vyomavyāpin, the six-syllabled, / the Bahurūpa, and the Netra—these are the seven universal mantras.

22.s:
teṣāṃ madhyādekatamaṃ mantramasmai samarpayet /
so'pyahorātramevainaṃ japedalpabhugapyabhuk // 21
22.d:
तेषां मध्यादेकतमं मन्त्रमस्मै समर्पयेत् ।
सोऽप्यहोरात्रमेवैनं जपेदल्पभुगप्यभुक् ॥ 21
22.m: He should impart one among these mantras to him. / And he should recite this very mantra for a day and night, eating little or fasting.

22.s:
mantramasmai samarpyātha sādhāravidhisaṃskṛte /
vahnau tarpitatanmantre vrataśuddhiṃ samācaret // 22
22.d:
मन्त्रमस्मै समर्प्याथ साधारविधिसंस्कृते ।
वह्नौ तर्पिततन्मन्त्रे व्रतशुद्धिं समाचरेत् ॥ 22
22.m: Having imparted the mantra to him, he should then perform the purification of his vow / in a fire consecrated with the universal rite, in which that mantra has been propitiated.

22.s:
pūjitenaiva mantreṇa kṛtvā nāmāsya saṃpuṭam /
prāyaścittaṃ śodhayāmi phaṭsvāhetyūhayogataḥ // 23
22.d:
पूजितेनैव मन्त्रेण कृत्वा नामास्य संपुटम् ।
प्रायश्चित्तं शोधयामि फट्स्वाहेत्यूहयोगतः ॥ 23
22.m: Using the very mantra that was worshipped, having enclosed his name within it, / by applying the adaptation: 'I purify the expiation, Phaṭ Svāhā,'

22.s:
śataṃ sahasraṃ vā hutvā punaḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ tathā /
prayogādvauṣaḍantāṃ ca kṣiptvāhūya vrateśvaram // 24
22.d:
शतं सहस्रं वा हुत्वा पुनः पूर्णाहुतिं तथा ।
प्रयोगाद्वौषडन्तां च क्षिप्त्वाहूय व्रतेश्वरम् ॥ 24
22.m: having offered a hundred or a thousand oblations, and likewise the full oblation / ending in Vauṣaṭ by application, and having invoked the Lord of Vows,

22.s:
tāro vrateśvarāyeti namaścetyenamarcayet /
śrāvayecca tvayā nāsya kāryaṃ kiṃcicchivājñayā // 25
22.d:
तारो व्रतेश्वरायेति नमश्चेत्येनमर्चयेत् ।
श्रावयेच्च त्वया नास्य कार्यं किंचिच्छिवाज्ञया ॥ 25
22.m:
With 'Oṃ to the Lord of Observances, namaḥ,' he should worship him,
and proclaim: 'By the command of Śiva, you have nothing more to do with him.'

22.s:
tato vrateśvarastarpyaḥ svāhāntena tataśca saḥ /
kṣamayitvā visṛjyaḥ syāttato'gneśca visarjanam // 26
22.d:
ततो व्रतेश्वरस्तर्प्यः स्वाहान्तेन ततश्च सः ।
क्षमयित्वा विसृज्यः स्यात्ततोऽग्नेश्च विसर्जनम् ॥ 26
22.m:
Then the Lord of Observances should be propitiated with svāhā at the end,
and having begged his pardon, he should be dismissed; then follows the dismissal of the fire.

22.s:
tacchrāvaṇaṃ ca devāya kṣamasveti visarjanam /
tatastṛtīyadivase prāgvatsarvo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ // 27
22.d:
तच्छ्रावणं च देवाय क्षमस्वेति विसर्जनम् ।
ततस्तृतीयदिवसे प्राग्वत्सर्वो विधिः स्मृतः ॥ 27
22.m:
Proclaiming that to the Lord with 'Pardon!' constitutes the dismissal.
Then on the third day, the entire procedure is taught as before,

22.s:
adhivāsādikaḥ sveṣṭadīkṣākarmāvasānakaḥ /
prāgliṅgināṃ mokṣadīkṣā sādhikāravivarjitā // 28
22.d:
अधिवासादिकः स्वेष्टदीक्षाकर्मावसानकः ।
प्राग्लिङ्गिनां मोक्षदीक्षा साधिकारविवर्जिता ॥ 28
22.m:
beginning with the preliminary consecration and ending with the rite of initiation chosen for oneself.
For those previously bearing sect marks, the initiation leading to liberation is devoid of ritual authority [to teach].

22.s:
sādhakācāryatāmārge na yogyāste punarbhuvaḥ /
punarbhuvo'pi jñāneddhā bhavanti gurutāspadam // 29
22.d:
साधकाचार्यतामार्गे न योग्यास्ते पुनर्भुवः ।
पुनर्भुवोऽपि ज्ञानेद्धा भवन्ति गुरुतास्पदम् ॥ 29
22.m:
Such re-initiates are not fit for the path of an adept or a master.
Yet even re-initiates, when kindled by knowledge, become the abode of guruship,

22.s:
mokṣāyaiva na bhogāya bhogāyāpyabhyupāyataḥ /
ityuktavānsvapaddhatyāmīśānaśivadaiśikaḥ // 30
22.d:
मोक्षायैव न भोगाय भोगायाप्यभ्युपायतः ।
इत्युक्तवान्स्वपद्धत्यामीशानशिवदैशिकः ॥ 30
22.m:
leading indeed to liberation, not to enjoyment—or even to enjoyment through being a means to it.
Thus spoke the master Īśānaśiva in his own ritual manual (paddhati),

22.s:
śrīdevyā yāmalīyoktitattvasamyakpravedakaḥ /
gurvantasyāpyadhodṛṣṭiśāyinaḥ saṃskriyāmimām // 31
22.d:
श्रीदेव्या यामलीयोक्तितत्त्वसम्यक्प्रवेदकः ।
गुर्वन्तस्याप्यधोदृष्टिशायिनः संस्क्रियामिमाम् ॥ 31
22.m:
he who properly knew the truth taught in the Devyāyāmala.
Even for one whose guru is of the lower order and adheres to a lower view, having performed this purification,

22.s:
kṛtvā rahasyaṃ kathayennānyathā kāmike kila /
anyatantrābhiṣikte'pi rahasyaṃ na prakāśayet // 32
22.d:
कृत्वा रहस्यं कथयेन्नान्यथा कामिके किल ।
अन्यतन्त्राभिषिक्तेऽपि रहस्यं न प्रकाशयेत् ॥ 32
22.m:
one should explain the secret doctrine; not otherwise, as is stated in the Kāmika:
'Even if consecrated in another Tantra, one should not reveal the secret doctrine.'

22.s:
svatantrastho'pi gurvanto gurumajñamupāśritaḥ /
tatra paścādanāśvastastatrāpi vidhimācaret // 33
22.d:
स्वतन्त्रस्थोऽपि गुर्वन्तो गुरुमज्ञमुपाश्रितः ।
तत्र पश्चादनाश्वस्तस्तत्रापि विधिमाचरेत् ॥ 33
22.m:
Even one belonging to one's own Tantra whose guru was an ignorant man,
and who subsequently lost faith in him, should also undergo this ritual procedure.

22.s:
ajñācāryamukhāyātaṃ nirvīryaṃ mantrameṣa yat /
japtavānsa guruścātra nādhikāryuktadūṣaṇāt // 34
22.d:
अज्ञाचार्यमुखायातं निर्वीर्यं मन्त्रमेष यत् ।
जप्तवान्स गुरुश्चात्र नाधिकार्युक्तदूषणात् ॥ 34
22.m:
Because he recited a powerless mantra that came from the mouth of an ignorant master,
and that guru was not qualified here owing to the stated defect;

22.s:
tato'sya śuddhiṃ prākkṛtvā tato dīkṣāṃ samācaret /
adhodarśanasaṃsthena guruṇā dīkṣitaḥ purā // 35
22.d:
ततोऽस्य शुद्धिं प्राक्कृत्वा ततो दीक्षां समाचरेत् ।
अधोदर्शनसंस्थेन गुरुणा दीक्षितः पुरा ॥ 35
22.m:
therefore, having first performed his purification, he should then perform the initiation.
When one previously initiated by a guru standing in a lower doctrine

22.s:
tīvraśaktivaśātpaścādyadā gacchetsa sadgurum /
tadāpyasya śiśorevaṃ śuddhiṃ kṛtvā sa sadguruḥ // 36
22.d:
तीव्रशक्तिवशात्पश्चाद्यदा गच्छेत्स सद्गुरुम् ।
तदाप्यस्य शिशोरेवं शुद्धिं कृत्वा स सद्गुरुः ॥ 36
22.m:
subsequently approaches a true guru under the influence of an intense descent of power,
then too, having thus purified this novice, that true guru

22.s:
dīkṣādikarma nikhilaṃ kuryāduktavidhānataḥ /
prāpto'pi sadgururyogyabhāvamasya na vetti cet // 37
22.d:
दीक्षादिकर्म निखिलं कुर्यादुक्तविधानतः ।
प्राप्तोऽपि सद्गुरुर्योग्यभावमस्य न वेत्ति चेत् ॥ 37
22.m:
should perform the entire ritual of initiation and the rest according to the prescribed rule.
Even when attained, if the true guru does not recognize his fitness

22.s:
vijñānadāne tacchiṣyo yogyatāṃ darśayennijām /
sarvathā tvabruvanneṣa bruvāṇo vā viparyayam // 38
22.d:
विज्ञानदाने तच्छिष्यो योग्यतां दर्शयेन्निजाम् ।
सर्वथा त्वब्रुवन्नेष ब्रुवाणो वा विपर्ययम् ॥ 38
22.m:
in bestowing knowledge, the disciple should demonstrate his own fitness.
If he does not speak at all, however, or speaks perversely,

22.s:
ajño vastuta eveti tattyaktvetthaṃ vidhiṃ caret /
na tirobhāvaśaṅkātra kartavyā buddhiśālinā // 39
22.d:
अज्ञो वस्तुत एवेति तत्त्यक्त्वेत्थं विधिं चरेत् ।
न तिरोभावशङ्कात्र कर्तव्या बुद्धिशालिना ॥ 39
22.m:
[knowing] that he is indeed ignorant, he should leave him and perform the rite in this way.
No doubt regarding concealment should be entertained here by an intelligent man:

22.s:
adhaḥspṛktvaṃ tirobhūtirnordhvopāyavivecanam /
siddhānte dīkṣitāstantre daśāṣṭādaśabhedini // 40
22.d:
अधःस्पृक्त्वं तिरोभूतिर्नोर्ध्वोपायविवेचनम् ।
सिद्धान्ते दीक्षितास्तन्त्रे दशाष्टादशभेदिनि ॥ 40
22.m:
contact with the lower is concealment, not the discernment of higher means.
Those initiated into the Siddhānta Tantra, which is divided into ten and eighteen,

22.s:
bhairavīye catuḥṣaṣṭau tānpaśūndīkṣayettrike /
siddhavīrāvalīsāre bhairavīye kule'pi ca // 41
22.d:
भैरवीये चतुःषष्टौ तान्पशून्दीक्षयेत्त्रिके ।
सिद्धवीरावलीसारे भैरवीये कुलेऽपि च ॥ 41
22.m:
and in the sixty-four Bhairava Tantras—those bound souls he should initiate into the Trika.
In the Siddhavīrāvalīsāra and also in the Bhairava Kula,

22.s:
pañcadīkṣākramopāttā dīkṣānuttarasaṃjñitā /
tena sarvo'dharastho'pi liṅgoddhṛtyānugṛhyate // 42
22.d:
पञ्चदीक्षाक्रमोपात्ता दीक्षानुत्तरसंज्ञिता ।
तेन सर्वोऽधरस्थोऽपि लिङ्गोद्धृत्यानुगृह्यते ॥ 42
22.m:
the initiation acquired through the fivefold sequence of initiations is called the unexcelled.
Therefore, everyone, even one standing in a lower doctrine, is graced by the removal of their sect marks.

22.s:
yo'pi hṛtsthamaheśānacodanātaḥ suvistṛtam /
śāstrajñānaṃ samanvicchetso'pi yāyādbahūngurūn // 43
22.d:
योऽपि हृत्स्थमहेशानचोदनातः सुविस्तृतम् ।
शास्त्रज्ञानं समन्विच्छेत्सोऽपि यायाद्बहून्गुरून् ॥ 43
22.m:
Moreover, whoever desires comprehensive textual knowledge
prompted by the Great Lord residing in his heart, may also go to many gurus,

22.s:
taddīkṣāścāpi gṛhṇīyādabhiṣecanapaścimāḥ /
jñānopodbalikāstā hi tattajjñānavatā kṛtāḥ // 44
22.d:
तद्दीक्षाश्चापि गृह्णीयादभिषेचनपश्चिमाः ।
ज्ञानोपोद्बलिकास्ता हि तत्तज्ज्ञानवता कृताः ॥ 44
22.m:
and he may take their initiations ending with consecration.
For, performed by those who possess that respective knowledge, they serve to strengthen knowledge.

22.s:
uktaṃ ca śrīmate śāstre tatra tatra ca bhūyasā /
āmodārthī yathā bhṛṅgaḥ puṣpātpuṣpāntaraṃ vrajet // 45
22.d:
उक्तं च श्रीमते शास्त्रे तत्र तत्र च भूयसा ।
आमोदार्थी यथा भृङ्गः पुष्पात्पुष्पान्तरं व्रजेत् ॥ 45
22.m:
And it is repeatedly stated in the glorious scripture:
'Just as a bee in search of fragrance moves from flower to flower,

22.s:
vijñānārthī tathā śiṣyo gurorgurvantaraṃ tviti /
gurūṇāṃ bhūyasāṃ madhye yato vijñānamuttamam // 46
22.d:
विज्ञानार्थी तथा शिष्यो गुरोर्गुर्वन्तरं त्विति ।
गुरूणां भूयसां मध्ये यतो विज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥ 46
22.m:
so a disciple seeking knowledge goes from guru to another guru.'
Among many gurus, he from whom the highest knowledge

22.s:
prāptaṃ so'sya gururdīkṣā nātra mukhyā hi saṃvidi /
sarvajñānanidhānaṃ tu guruṃ saṃprāpya susthitaḥ // 47
22.d:
प्राप्तं सोऽस्य गुरुर्दीक्षा नात्र मुख्या हि संविदि ।
सर्वज्ञाननिधानं तु गुरुं संप्राप्य सुस्थितः ॥ 47
22.m:
is obtained is his true guru; for initiation is not primary here with respect to consciousness.
Having attained a guru who is the treasury of all knowledge, well-established,

22.s:
tamevārādhayeddhīmāṃstattajjijñāsanonmukhaḥ /
iti dīkṣāvidhiḥ prokto liṅgoddharaṇapaścimaḥ // 48
22.d:
तमेवाराधयेद्धीमांस्तत्तज्जिज्ञासनोन्मुखः ।
इति दीक्षाविधिः प्रोक्तो लिङ्गोद्धरणपश्चिमः ॥ 48
22.m:
the wise man, intent on inquiring into various truths, should worship him alone.
Thus has been taught the ritual of initiation ending with the removal of sect marks.
